# hy-memory4dsh

Hy-Memory 2.0 as a native DSH memory component. Three tiers, three scenes, automatic recall before
each model step, automatic capture after each turn, and a manager panel under Settings > Memory.
No sidebar tab, no extra app, no configuration required for the default path.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:$(pwd)
```

Then open Settings > 记忆. The sidecar bootstraps its own Python environment on first use, and the
model route is read from your existing DSH provider settings.

**Keywords for store search:** `dsh-plugin`, `deepseek-harness`, `memory`, `agent-memory`,
`long-term-memory`, `hy-memory`, `memhub`, `three-tier-memory`, `personalization`, `context`.

## What it does

| Tier | Scope | Where it lives | Panel rights |
|---|---|---|---|
| Personal | the user, across every project | `user_id=dsh`, `agent_id=personal` | view, search, edit |
| Project | one workspace path | `agent_id=project:<sha1 of cwd>`, `session_id=project` | view, search, delete |
| Session | one DSH session inside its project | `agent_id=project:<key>`, `session_id=<session id>` | view, search, delete |

Tiers are not separate stores that fight each other. They are one Hy-Memory store with a three-level
namespace, so a memory written while working in a project can be promoted upward and recalled anywhere.
Recall runs one search per tier and merges them, so a session gets its own history, the project's
conventions and the user's long-term preferences in the same injected block.

Scenes follow Hy-Memory's own pipelines. A captured batch that contains file-editing tools is written
as `coding`, a batch with other tools as `working`, and a plain conversation as `chat`. Tool calls and
their results are part of the captured trajectory, not dropped.

## How a turn flows

1. `agent/pre-step`: the plugin searches all enabled tiers (personal, project, session), merges,
   deduplicates, caps the result by item count and characters, neutralizes any tag that could escape
   the injection frame, and appends one sourced user message. It has a hard deadline (1.2 s by
   default); a slow or broken sidecar skips injection instead of delaying the turn.
2. The turn runs normally. The six tools (`memory_search`, `memory_add`, `memory_list`, `memory_get`,
   `memory_update`, `memory_delete`) are available to the model.
3. `turn/end`: the plugin buffers the turn's user/assistant/tool events. Every N turns, or after an
   idle window, it writes the batch to the session tier with the detected scene.
4. Promotion: periodically, one LLM call classifies recent session memories and promotes the durable
   ones into the project tier and then the personal tier. Each promotion is recorded so it never repeats.

## Installation

```bash
node scripts/install.mjs --profile desktop     # uses the shipped dsh CLI: dependency + bundle selection
```

Then reload the DSH page (or restart the app) so the client half joins the plugin graph. Open
Settings > Memory.

The first start needs network once: the plugin creates a private Python 3.12 environment with
`hy-memory==2.0.13` (about 525 MB, via `uv` when available) and downloads an 80 MB local embedding
model. After that everything runs offline. Settings > Memory shows the state and offers a Start button,
so a cold install never blocks app startup.

## Configuration

Everything is optional. Open Settings > Memory for the panel; the defaults below are what a fresh
install uses.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `pro` | `lite` writes embeddings only and needs no LLM; `pro` adds LLM extraction; `ultra` enables System 2 `evolve()` |
| `llm.source` | `dsh` | reuse the model this DSH profile already routes to (provider, base URL and key are read from `$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml` and `$DSH_HOME/.env`); `custom` overrides |
| `embedding.mode` | `local` | `local` runs ONNX MiniLM (384 dims) inside the sidecar; `remote` uses any OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint |
| `recall` | on, 5 items, 1600 chars, min score 0.32 | injection budget |
| `capture` | on, every 3 turns, idle flush 180 s, tools included | capture cadence |
| `promotion` | on, every 8 turns | session to project to personal promotion |
| `tiers` | all on | disable a whole tier |
| `enabled` | on | master switch; off pauses recall, capture and tools, and the panel becomes read-only |
| `ui.sessionPanel` | on | show the optional session-view pane |
| `sidecar.idleStopMs` | 30 min | stop the sidecar after inactivity |

`lite` mode is the no-model fallback: it needs no LLM key at all, only the local embedder.

## Hot reload while installed

The plugin is installed with `link:`, so editing this checkout and then touching the profile's
`cordis.patch.yml` recomposes the tree and reloads the plugin without restarting the app. A
`hy-memory` override row was appended to `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml` for exactly that
purpose; its only content is `enabled: true`, and removing the block returns the row to the bundle's
own patch. Browser code is separate: reload the page after a client rebuild.

## Embeddings

Recall needs vectors, so some embedder is always involved; which one is your choice.

| `embedding.mode` | What runs | Network | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `local` (default) | chromadb's `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` ONNX, 384 dims | once, on first use | about 80 MB downloaded into `~/.cache/chroma/onnx_models`; already present here, then fully offline |
| `remote` | any OpenAI-compatible `/embeddings` endpoint | every call | set `baseURL`, `model`, `apiKey`, `dims`; a multilingual model fixes Chinese recall quality |
| disabled surfaces | lexical fallback only | none | semantic search is unavailable, but recall still returns token-overlap hits |

The local model is English-first, which is why a Chinese question can score below the cutoff; the plugin
falls back to a token-overlap scan in that case. Switching to a multilingual remote embedder removes the
need for that fallback. Nothing else in the plugin requires the ONNX model: capture, promotion, tiers and
the panel work without it, and a machine that never downloads it still gets lexical recall.

## Where data lives

```
$DSH_HOME/integrations/hy-memory/
  settings.json     your settings
  state.json        capture cursors, retry queue, project keys, promotion cursors
  boot.json         activation marker (pid, routes) written by the host half
  sidecar.log       sidecar stdout/stderr
  venv/             private Python environment
  data/             Hy-Memory store: Chroma vectors, Kuzu graph, SQLite history
```

Uninstalling the plugin leaves this directory alone. Delete it to remove all memory.

## How memories get their tier

`memory_add` no longer defaults everything to the personal tier. A small classifier reads the content:
repository facts, paths, commands, endpoints and conventions go to the project tier; preferences and
facts about the user stay personal; when both signals appear the project tier wins so the user profile
does not fill with technical noise; outside a project a project-tier write falls back to personal. Pass
`tier` explicitly to override, and the tool result states where the memory landed.

## Cross-project search

`memory_search` takes `allProjects: true` to search every project this user has touched instead of only
the current one. It fans out one scoped search per known project and merges the hits, each tagged with
its project key. Recall never does this implicitly: daily prompts only see the personal tier, the current
project and the current session, so another project's conventions cannot leak into unrelated work.

## Connecting to MemHub

Settings > Memory carries a MemHub card. MemHub is a separate product with its own store at
`~/.one-memory`; the card detects it read-only and offers three actions.

| Action | What happens |
|---|---|
| 导出到 JSON | pages this plugin's own store (all scenes) into `$DSH_HOME/integrations/hy-memory/exports/hy-memory-<ISO>.json` |
| 从 MemHub 拉取 | reads MemHub's store with a separate short-lived Python process (read-only, on a temporary copy), then writes every entry into the personal tier through this plugin's sidecar |
| 从文件导入 | same import from an absolute JSON path |

Import only ever writes the personal tier, dedupes by content hash persisted in `state.json`, and caps
at 500 entries per call. A MemHub runtime holding its store maps to `memhub_locked` with the holding
pid, so nothing is read while MemHub is writing. The dimension difference between the two stores does
not matter: only text crosses the boundary, and every imported entry is re-embedded locally.

## Coexistence with MemHub

MemHub (the separate local-first product) can be installed at the same time. It reaches DSH by scanning
`$DSH_HOME/sessions` and, if you enabled it there, by adding an MCP client row to a profile patch. This
plugin does not read or write MemHub's own store at `~/.one-memory`, and MemHub does not see this
plugin's store. If both are capturing the same conversations you will get two memories of the same
event, so pick one as the DSH path or keep MemHub for other apps only. The panel's diagnostics card
reports when `~/.one-memory` is present so the collision is visible instead of silent.

## Screenshots

Real captures from a running DSH instance (`docs/screenshots/`):

![Personal tier](docs/screenshots/panel-personal.png)
![Project tier](docs/screenshots/panel-project.png)
![Session tier](docs/screenshots/panel-session.png)

## Verifying it works

```bash
node --test 'test/**/*.test.mjs'     # host unit tests (pure logic)
node test/panel-smoke.mjs            # client bundle registers the right slots
cat "$DSH_HOME/integrations/hy-memory/boot.json"   # host half is live in the running app
```

The panel's diagnostics card shows sidecar state, the resolved model, embedding mode, and per-tier
counts. The activity list shows every recall, capture, promotion and error with timestamps.

## Limits worth knowing

- Working and coding memories live in separate Hy-Memory stores, and the SDK's HTTP surface does not
  forward `scene`, so the plugin reads them through its own bridge routes. A productivity memory is
  only reachable when it carries a `workspace_id`; with `capture.productivity: true` the plugin writes
  the git origin URL (or the repository path) as that id and recall searches with the same scope.
  Default capture routes every batch to the chat store and keeps the detected scene only as a label,
  because the chat store is searchable without extra scope.
- The bundled embedder is the English ONNX MiniLM (384 dims), so a Chinese query can score below the
  threshold against an English-stored memory. Recall therefore falls back to a token-overlap scan of
  recent memories when every semantic tier comes back empty. A remote multilingual embedder
  (`embedding.mode: remote`) removes the need for that fallback.
- The sidecar's own model calls run with thinking disabled. Gateway models that default to a thinking
  channel answer the reconcile prompt with an empty body, which the SDK reports as
  `RECONCILE_FAILED`; disabling thinking is what makes writes reliable.
- Editing is only allowed on personal memories; project and session memories can be deleted, as
  specified. Editing a productivity item is refused rather than silently written into the wrong store.
- Promotion is an LLM call. It runs at most once per window and is bounded by a timeout; a failure is
  recorded and retried next window rather than repeated per turn.
- A new session event type would break other readers, so the plugin never appends to the session log.

## Verified in a running app

- Three tiers hold real data (personal 4, project 11, session 67) and the panel reads all of them.
- Recall injects personal + current-project + current-session hits into a live turn.
- Capture kept a coding batch with 24 tool calls and wrote it through `/bridge/v1/add_scene`, so the coding store grew without touching chat.
- MemHub detection, export, pull (`memhub_locked` while MemHub runs) and import dedupe were exercised live.
- 85 host tests and the panel smoke suite pass; the plugin is installed with `dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:<dir>` and the running app serves its 14 routes.

decision.reason: Held for versioned DSH compatibility. MIT and local-source install instructions are present with complete native host/client modules, but no versioned DSH compatibility contract was found. It captures conversations/tool traces, stores layered memories and can connect to MemHub. Persistent content, model calls and the optional external bridge were not exercised. # Paper Desk · 论文工作台

[![build](https://github.com/fexas/dsh-paper-desk/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/fexas/dsh-paper-desk/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

A Zotero-shaped paper desk for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).
It adds a **Papers** entry to the DSH sidebar, a three-pane PDF reader and a
per-project mind map: the normal DSH sidebar on the left, the document or canvas
in the middle, and a DeepSeek chat / Markdown notebook on the right.

> 本项目也适合中文用户：界面、AI 精读笔记和共读对话默认使用中文。

## Features

- **Projects with a purpose** — choose **Research** (find a problem, build a
  method, compare benchmarks) or **Learning** (build concept dependencies,
  timeline, reading queue and recall exercises). Each project keeps papers,
  tags, annotations, chats, notes and a mind map together.
- **Project mind map** — one persistent React Flow canvas per project, with
  drag-and-drop paper nodes, Markdown/KaTeX nodes, edges, backlinks, automatic
  tidying and a DeepSeek map assistant. Research and learning projects start
  from different templates.
- **Drop PDFs in** — uploads, parses, and files PDFs into a Zotero-style folder
  (`Author et al. - Year - Title`). Title, authors and year are read from the
  PDF metadata and first page.
- **Double-click to read** — click the Read button, or double-click any
  non-interactive part of a paper row.
- **Zotero-shaped paper rows** — expand a paper to see `paper.pdf`, `notes.md`
  and any appendix or supplementary files. Extra files are stored verbatim and
  never parsed.
- **PDF reading** — PDF.js viewer with fit-width/zoom, page navigation,
  selectable text, four highlight colours, paragraph-anchored notes,
  one-click selection translation, and “ask AI” with the selected passage.
- **Math-aware Markdown** — `$...$`, `$$...$$`, `\(...\)` and `\[...\]` render
  in notes and chat using KaTeX's HTML layout with embedded KaTeX fonts.
  Code spans and currency are left alone.
- **AI deep-read note** — on first open DeepSeek writes a structured Markdown
  note: TL;DR, core problem, prior work pros/cons, how this paper fixes the
  cons, motivation + key idea + example, how to read the experiments,
  strengths, limitations and future work. The note is a normal Markdown file
  you edit in the right pane, with preview, autosave and “AI rewrite”.
- **Co-reading chat** — a dedicated DeepSeek conversation per paper. It receives
  the paper text, generated note, highlights and the quoted passage, so
  follow-up questions have context. The conversation is persisted.
- **Tags and search** — Zotero-style tag chips; filter by one or more tags and
  search titles, authors, tags and note excerpts.
- **Your data is plain files** — no database, no lock-in.

```text
paper-desk/
  projects/
    scaling-inference-for-sbi/
      project.json
      mindmap.json          # research or learning map
      mindmap-chat.json     # project-level AI conversation
      papers/
        kuhmichel-et-al-2026-high-dimensional-simulation-based-inference/
          paper.pdf
          paper.txt          # extracted text (AI context)
          notes.md           # Markdown notebook
          annotations.json   # highlights + paragraph notes
          chat.json          # co-reading conversation
          attachments/       # appendix, supplementary material, ...
```

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.x** with the Web GUI and a DeepSeek provider.
- A modern Chromium-based Web renderer (the DSH Desktop app is supported).
- Node.js **22+** for development builds.

Paper Desk uses the active DSH profile's provider/model. It does not ask for a
separate API key. When provider/model are not configured explicitly it selects
the first DeepSeek Flash/Chat route available in the profile.

## Install from GitHub

In DSH, open **Settings → Plugins**, install the bundle from GitHub
(`fexas/dsh-paper-desk`), and enable it. Restart DSH if the host asks for a
restart after installing a new package.

If your DSH version exposes the plugin command directly, the equivalent local
checkout flow is:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fexas/dsh-paper-desk.git
cd dsh-paper-desk
npm ci
npm run build
```

Then add this directory as a `file:` dependency of the active DSH profile and
select `dsh-paper-desk` in that profile's bundle list (see the
[DSH plugin documentation](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)).
The host half has no build step; `client.js` is the pre-built browser half.

## Data location

The default data directory depends on how the plugin is installed:

| Install | Default `projects/` location |
|---|---|
| Linked local checkout | `<plugin-root>/projects/` |
| Managed plugin (under `node_modules`) | `$DSH_HOME/paper-desk/projects/` (usually `~/.dsh/paper-desk/projects/`) |

Override it in the plugin row:

```yaml
- id: dsh-paper-desk
  name: dsh-paper-desk
  config:
    provider: deepseek-account
    model: deepseek-flash
    # dataDir: /absolute/path/to/paper-desk-projects
```

The data directory contains `project.json` plus one folder per paper. Deleting
a project or paper moves it to `projects/.trash/` rather than destroying it.
PDFs, text, notes, annotations and chat history are local files; nothing is
sent anywhere except the model requests made by DeepSeek.

## How it works

```
browser (client.js)                         host (host/service.js)
──────────────────                         ───────────────────────
React slot UI                              Typert Remote `paperDesk`
PDF.js viewer + KaTeX                      projects/, uploads, files
highlight / note state          <──RPC──>  annotations.json, notes.md
DeepSeek chat + note UI                    chat.json, paper.txt
                                           DeepSeek call via ctx.llm
```

- `client.js` is a single browser module built from `client/` with esbuild.
  PDF.js, KaTeX fonts and React Flow CSS are bundled, so no CDN or extra asset
  route is needed.
- The host exposes a small `paperDesk` Remote namespace. The browser never gets
  direct filesystem access.
- Every paper is a directory with human-readable JSON/Markdown files; the UI can
  be removed without losing the research library.

## Project mind map

Every project has a single `mindmap.json`. Open it from the **项目脑图** banner or
the header button in a project.

### Templates

- **Research** starts with:
  - Motivating example / problem to solve
  - Our methods: framework, motivation / key idea, and why it is superior
  - How to evaluate performance: datasets/benchmarks, metrics, baselines/ablations
- **Learning** starts with:
  - Foundations and prerequisites
  - Core concepts, examples and misconceptions
  - Development timeline
  - Paper queue
  - Recall and exercises

Templates are just seeded nodes. Every title, Markdown body and edge is editable,
and **整理布局** runs a dagre layout for the current graph.

### Linking papers and ideas

Open **论文库**, then click or drag a paper onto the canvas. A paper node keeps
a stable `paperId`; any node can also reference papers from the node inspector.
The inspector shows incoming backlinks for the selected node, and clicking a
paper chip opens its reader. This gives a lightweight Zettelkasten-style graph:
papers, concepts, questions and experiments live in one canvas and connect in
both directions.

### Map chat

The right pane switches between **对话** and **节点**:

- **对话** sends the whole graph, the paper library metadata and (optionally)
  the selected node to DeepSeek. The model is explicitly told this is a
  research-strategy or learning-coach session, depending on the project type.
- **节点** edits the selected node's title, type, Markdown body (with formulas),
  linked papers and backlinks.

## Performance notes

The reader shell opens as soon as the paper record arrives. PDF bytes are read
in eight parallel range requests, page 1 renders before the remaining page
boxes and text layer are resolved, and recently opened PDFs stay in a small
in-memory LRU cache. PDF.js runs its worker bundle on the page thread, which
avoids a Chromium/Electron worker handshake failure that can otherwise hang the
viewer. AI note generation runs alongside PDF loading; a compact progress card
shows the live stage and disappears when the note is written.

## Development

```bash
npm ci
npm run build      # rebuild client.js
npm run check      # syntax-check host and built client
```

Source layout:

- `host/service.js` — projects, chunked uploads, annotations, notes, LLM calls
- `client/App.jsx` — project library, paper rows, reader shell, chat and notes
- `client/PdfViewer.jsx` — PDF.js canvas/text/highlight viewer
- `client/MindMapPage.jsx` — React Flow canvas, paper tray, node inspector and map chat
- `client/markdown.js` — Markdown + KaTeX formula rendering
- `client/styles.css` — DSH-token-based UI styles
- `host/mindmap.js` — research/learning templates and graph normalisation
- `build.mjs` — esbuild bundle, PDF.js worker embedding, inline KaTeX fonts and React Flow CSS

Pull requests are welcome. Please keep the UI on DSH theme tokens
(`--dsw-alias-*`) and do not add a separate app shell, CDN dependency or a
second filesystem root.

## Known limitations

- No OCR: image-only PDFs will not have selectable text or AI full-text context.
- The AI note is generated from extracted PDF text; complex multi-column or
  scanned layouts may lose structure.
- The co-reading chat is a focused paper assistant, not a general-purpose DSH
  agent with tool access.
- Data is local to one machine; there is no sync or multi-user layer.

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
Bundled third-party code includes PDF.js (Apache-2.0), KaTeX (MIT), React Flow,
dagre, marked, DOMPurify and lucide.

PDF libraries, local notes and LLM requests are capability signals. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-chapters

**Long memory for local AI: a [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
plugin that archives agent conversations as verbatim chapters, continues sessions from a Table of
Contents at zero inference-token cost, and turns that archive into a shared, searchable knowledge
pool.** Published on npm as [`@fractalsynapse/dsh-chapters`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@fractalsynapse/dsh-chapters);
source at [fractalsynapse/dsh-chapters](https://github.com/fractalsynapse/dsh-chapters).

> **All documentation lives on the documentation site — this README is a doorway, not a duplicate.**
> ### 📖 https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/

## Install (the whole setup)

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @fractalsynapse/dsh-chapters      # install into your harness profile
dsh plugin --profile web update @fractalsynapse/dsh-chapters   # keep current — restart `dsh web` after
```

`--profile <name>` is required on every `dsh plugin` command (`web` = the browser harness profile).
After restart you have the fork button, seven agent tools, twelve `/chapters-*` commands (through
`0.2.17`, including `/chapters-remove`) — and the optional `chapters` preset that routes `/compact`
through the zero-token engine.

## Find the right page for your question

| You want to… | Go to |
|---|---|
| understand what this is / why (the ten benefits) | [Home → “What it gives you”](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/) |
| install, upgrade, uninstall, verify provenance | [§23 Install, upgrade, provenance](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/operations/install/) |
| run your first compaction/continuation | [§1 Quickstart](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/start/quickstart/) → [§2 Your first continuation](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/start/first-continuation/) |
| link a shared knowledge pool (git or TreeDX) | [§3 Link a knowledge pool](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/start/link-pool/) · [§10 The pool](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/knowledge/pool/) |
| run any command — exact syntax, scope, outputs | [§15 Commands](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/reference/commands/) |
| delete a bad chapter (the wrong-project prompt) | [§15 Commands → `/chapters-remove`](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/reference/commands/#chapters-remove--delete-a-bad-chapter-for-real) |
| know what the agent-facing tools do | [§16 Agent tools](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/reference/tools/) |
| tune a threshold, budget, or trigger | [§17 Configuration](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/reference/configuration/) |
| understand *why not summaries* / the economics | [§5 Why not summaries?](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/concepts/why-not-summaries/) |
| read the design rules the system won't break | [§6 The four invariants](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/concepts/invariants/) |
| the theory behind retrieval-over-compression (RLM) | [§8 Recursive context theory](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/concepts/recursive-context/) |
| propose/approve rules for agents | [§13 Rules & governance](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/knowledge/rules/) |
| let a second model propose your next prompt | [§28 Prompt recommendations](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/concepts/prompt-recommendations/) |
| debug something (“seems broken, is it?”) | [§4 FAQ & troubleshooting](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/start/faq/) |
| prompt-cache / llama.cpp behavior | [§21 Cache behavior on llama.cpp](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/evidence/llamacpp-cache/) |
| see measured results (production run + benchmarks) | [§19 Benchmarks](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/evidence/benchmarks/) · [§20 Field study](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/evidence/field-study/) |
| compare with other memory approaches | [§22 The alternatives, compared](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/evidence/comparison/) |
| check security/privacy boundaries | [§27 Security & privacy](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/operations/security/) |
| release history & known-fixed incidents | [§26 Changelog](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/operations/changelog/) |
| **develop the plugin itself** | [§24 Developing](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/operations/development/) → the engineering specs below |

## Developing / contributing

Three ways to set up a development environment — pick whichever fits your workflow:

| Mode | Best for | Command |
|------|----------|---------|
| **Centralized** (your live profile) | Day-to-day development on your main machine | `./dev/install/install.sh && dsh web` |
| **Compartmentalized** (isolated DSH_HOME) | Testing changes without touching your live sessions | `DSH_HOME=/tmp/dsh-dev ./dev/install/install.sh` |
| **Containerized** (full stack) | Isolated platform with vLLM + Playwright + Chromium | `cd dev/install && docker compose up -d` |

All three install the same plugin set: dsh-chapters, [dsh-codegraph](https://github.com/jiangzhenguo/dsh-codegraph)
(structural code search via pre-indexed AST graph), and dsh-tinyfish-search. Full details in
[`dev/install/README.md`](dev/install/README.md). The containerized stack additionally ships its own
vLLM model server (Qwen3-4B-AWQ with inference + systemone endpoints), a DSH Web UI service, and a
CI-capable test runner — everything runs locally with no external API keys required.

The site's Part VI covers the daily loop; the repository itself holds the engineering truth for agents:

- **[`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md)** — working spec for AI agents developing this repo (invariants, budget, hard rules)
- **[`docs/`](docs/)** — deep specs: `contract.md` (host API facts), `architecture.md` (mechanics), `development.md` (build/test loop + tape system), `verify.md` (every claim's procedure), `knowledge-repo.md` (design record), `host-compaction-seam.md`, `provider.md`
- **[`dev/install/`](dev/install/)** — installer, containerized platform, and local-llm skill
- **benchmarks**: `npm run bench` — three arms, local model, never CI ([protocol](benchmarks/README.md))

Feature requests and bugs: [open an issue](https://github.com/fractalsynapse/dsh-chapters/issues) —
measured reports get measured answers.

## License

Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Your conversations, chapters, and knowledge pools stay yours.

No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

| **develop the plugin itself** | [§24 Developing](https://fractalsynapse.github.io/dsh-chapters/operations/development/) → the engineering specs below |

## Developing / contributing

Three ways to set up a development environment — pick whichever fits your workflow:

| Mode | Best for | Command |
|------|----------|---------|
| **Centralized** (your live profile) | Day-to-day development on your main machine | `./dev/install/install.sh && dsh web` |
| **Compartmentalized** (isolated DSH_HOME) | Testing changes without touching your live sessions | `DSH_HOME=/tmp/dsh-dev ./dev/install/install.sh` |
| **Containerized** (full stack) | Isolated platform with vLLM + Playwright + Chromium | `cd dev/install && docker compose up -d` |

All three install the same plugin set: dsh-chapters, [dsh-codegraph](https://github.com/jiangzhenguo/dsh-codegraph)
(structural code search via pre-indexed AST graph), and dsh-tinyfish-search. Full details in
[`dev/install/README.md`](dev/install/README.md). The containerized stack additionally ships its own
vLLM model server (Qwen3-4B-AWQ with inference + systemone endpoints), a DSH Web UI service, and a
CI-capable test runner — everything runs locally with no external API keys required.

The site's Part VI covers the daily loop; the repository itself holds the engineering truth for agents:

- **[`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md)** — working spec for AI agents developing this repo (invariants, budget, hard rules)
- **[`docs/`](docs/)** — deep specs: `contract.md` (host API facts), `architecture.md` (mechanics), `development.md` (build/test loop + tape system), `verify.md` (every claim's procedure), `knowledge-repo.md` (design record), `host-compaction-seam.md`, `provider.md`
- **[`dev/install/`](dev/install/)** — installer, containerized platform, and local-llm skill
- **benchmarks**: `npm run bench` — three arms, local model, never CI ([protocol](benchmarks/README.md))

Feature requests and bugs: [open an issue](https://github.com/fractalsynapse/dsh-chapters/issues) —
measured reports get measured answers.

## License

# 方糕萌宠 · Fanggao Pet

> 一只会跟着 DeepSeek Harness 对话状态变化的方糕萌宠：对话进行时奔跑、完成时躺下睡觉、出错时生气。可鼠标任意拖拽，位置自动记忆。

![三种形态预览](docs/preview.png)

## 特性

- **三态动画**：由当前会话的 `SessionSnapshot` 实时驱动
  | 状态 | 触发条件 | 形象 |
  |------|----------|------|
  | 🏃 奔跑 | `running === true` | 上下弹跳 + 双腿交替摆动 + 速度线 |
  | 😴 睡觉 | 空闲 / 无报错 | 横躺、闭眼、头顶飘 `Z z z` |
  | 😡 生气 | `lastAgentError` / `promptError` / `openError` 存在，或 `openState === 'error'` | 竖眉、撇嘴、红脸、额头青筋脉冲 |
- **悬浮常驻**：渲染在 `shell.overlay` 帧级浮层，始终位于最上层，不占布局。
- **鼠标拖拽**：按住可拖到屏幕任意位置，位置存入 `localStorage`，刷新后保留。
- **永不遮断操作**：浮层本身 click-through，只有方糕本体响应指针事件。
- **纯 SVG + CSS 动画**：矢量、任意分辨率清晰、体积小、跟随时序流畅。

## 安装

本插件是 DeepSeek Harness 的本地 bundle（`@local/fanggao-pet`）：

1. 克隆仓库到本地：
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/gavinff1990/fanggao-pet.git
   ```
2. 在 Harness 中通过插件管理器安装该目录（绝对路径）：
   - 动作：`install_bundle`
   - 目标：`<克隆目录的绝对路径>`
3. 插件会立即激活并出现在页面右下角（默认位置）。

> 安装/卸载时插件管理器会重新链接该 bundle；修改 `client.js` 后重新安装即可热加载。

## 工作原理

- **Host 半**（`index.js`）无需逻辑，只负责注册 bundle。
- **Client 半**（`client.js`）：
  - 注入 `slots` + `sessions` 服务。
  - 订阅 `sessions.list` 找到当前主视图会话（`retainedBy.mainView > 0`）。
  - 订阅该会话的 `SessionFace`（`sessions.binding(id).session`）读取 `SessionSnapshot`，据此选出三种形态。
  - 通过 `ctx.slots.inject('shell.overlay', …)` 注册悬浮层条目，并用指针事件实现拖拽。

## 文件结构

```
fanggao-pet/
├── package.json        # bundle 清单（dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client）
├── cordis.patch.yml    # 插入 fanggao-pet 插件行
├── index.js            # Host 半（空 apply）
├── client.js           # Client 半：SVG 萌宠 + 状态 + 拖拽
├── icon.svg            # 插件管理器中显示的图标
├── locale/{en,zh}.json # 插件标题/描述
└── docs/preview.png    # 形态预览
```

## 自定义

- **颜色/造型**：`client.js` 顶部的 `COLORS` 常量与 `runningPose` / `sleepingPose` / `angryPose` 三个函数。
- **拖拽记忆**：`STORE_KEY`（默认 `fanggao-pet.position`）。
- **默认位置**：`defaultPos()`（默认右下角）。

## 许可

未附带开源协议。若需公开分发，建议补充 `LICENSE`（如 MIT）。

# ShanghaiTech GenAI Plugin

`dsh-shanghaitech-genai@1.0.4`，用于 **DSH Desktop ≥ 0.2.1-rc.2**。配套本地网关与部署脚本见 [ShanghaiTech-GenAI](https://github.com/Github-Anderson/ShanghaiTech-GenAI)。

## 功能

模型来源、Agent 预设及 provider ID 均为 `shanghaitech-genai`（界面显示 ShanghaiTech GenAI）。支持独立 Search/Thinking 选项、网站附件、来源与 usage，以及 Standard 原生工具和权限流程。PDF 文本工具名为 `shanghaitech_genai_read_pdf`。

按钮随 DSH 语言显示为“联网搜索 / 深度思考 / 网页附件”或“Search / Thinking / Attachments”。搜索和思考以高亮表示启用状态，直接调用原网页对应功能；思考选项按网关能力显示，配套配置对 Kimi 和 GPT 系列开放。网页附件在发送时将原文件交给网站图片上传或文档解析接口。

网页附件接受 PNG、JPEG、WebP、GIF 图片（严格小于 20 MiB），以及 PDF、TXT、CSV、DOCX、XLS、XLSX、PPT、PPTX、HTML、JSON 文档（严格小于 10 MiB）。2026-11-01 通过 DeepSeek 网站接口验证新增的六种文档均能提取合成标记；DOC、XML 被网站拒绝，保持关闭。需配套更新网关，并由所选模型开放附件能力；扫描件无文本时不提供 OCR 回退。独立 PDF 文本工具仍只处理 PDF。

## 删除会话

输入区的“删除会话 / Delete session”会显示独立确认，默认勾选“同时删除网站历史 / Also delete website history”。确认后永久删除当前本地会话及其子代理，并清理工作区记录；不删除工作区文件或独立分叉。

同步网站历史时，网站确认成功后才删除本地会话。旧会话缺少上游映射或登录令牌已变更时，请到网站清理历史，或明确取消勾选，仅删除本地会话。生成中或有待处理工作的会话须先停止。

兼容 DSH 默认关闭的全文搜索；已完成删除后的搜索索引刷新异常只显示警告，不再误报为整体失败。功能适配已检查的 JSONL 存储生命周期，不支持的后端会拒绝删除。更新后请完全退出 DSH，包括 Windows 托盘后台或 macOS 后台进程，再重新打开。

## 安装

Windows 和 macOS 本地开发环境均可使用配套仓库的同步与部署脚本，从当前源码打包并安装插件。在两个同级仓库的父目录运行。

Windows（PowerShell）：

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\ShanghaiTech-GenAI\tools\Sync-Local.ps1
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\ShanghaiTech-GenAI\tools\Deploy-Local.ps1
```

macOS（终端）：

```sh
./ShanghaiTech-GenAI/tools/Sync-Local.sh
./ShanghaiTech-GenAI/tools/Deploy-Local.sh
```

部署脚本会自动同步网关密钥；检查完成后完全退出 DSH，再通过对应系统的 `local/deploy/Start.ps1`（Windows）或 `./local/deploy/Start.sh`（macOS）重启。后续更新分别运行 `local/Update.ps1` 或 `./local/Update.sh`。Windows `.ps1` 入口使用 `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File` 调用。配置和网站凭证保存在仓库外的 `local/deploy/private/`。详细参数见配套仓库的[本地开发环境](https://github.com/Github-Anderson/ShanghaiTech-GenAI/blob/main/tools/README.md)。

如果选择安装已发布版本，可在 DSH Desktop 插件安装界面提交以下来源：

```text
github:Github-Anderson/dsh-shanghaitech-genai#v1.0.4
```

凭证引用为 `SHANGHAITECH_GENAI_API_KEY`，网关地址由部署启动脚本通过 `SHANGHAITECH_GENAI_BASE_URL` 提供，默认是 `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1`。已发布的 v1.0.4 可通过 Git 标签安装；本地源码部署使用同步脚本生成的插件包，包含未提交修改。

配置凭证后重启 DSH，新建会话，选择 **ShanghaiTech GenAI** 预设与同名模型来源。网关的首次登录和凭证导入步骤见[配套安装指南](https://github.com/Github-Anderson/ShanghaiTech-GenAI/blob/main/安装指南.md)。

已配置 DSH CLI 的环境也可安装到指定 profile：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile-name> add github:Github-Anderson/dsh-shanghaitech-genai#v1.0.4
```

仓库中的运行入口为可直接加载的 JavaScript，无需编译；私有仓库的 GitHub 安装需要当前 Git 环境有读取权限。`private: true` 用于避免误发布到 npm。

## 插件结构

本包按 [DeepSeek Harness 官方插件打包规范](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/develop/basic/publish)组织为 Bundle：

- `package.json` 声明 `dsh.bundle.patch`、`dsh.client`、导出入口、发布文件和兼容版本。
- `cordis.patch.yml` 挂载模型与会话选项插件，以及 Agent 预设插件。
- `index.cjs` 导出 Cordis 插件的 `name`、`inject` 和 `apply`。
- `client.js` 提供 DSH 客户端界面，`locale/` 提供中英文文本。
- `agent-preset.cjs` 和 `pdf-reader.cjs` 提供 Agent 预设与 PDF 工具。

## 开发检查

Windows（PowerShell）：

```powershell
npm test
npm pack --dry-run
```

macOS（终端）：

```sh
TMPDIR=/private/tmp npm test
npm pack --dry-run
```

macOS 运行离线检查时设置 `TMPDIR=/private/tmp`，避免系统临时目录符号链接触发路径防护；Node 需满足 `package.json` 的版本要求，也可使用 DSH 应用内置 Node/pnpm。`npm test` 运行九组离线检查，使用合成数据和模拟响应。`test-*-sdk.cjs`、`test-sdk.cjs` 与 `test-command.cjs` 用于已安装 DSH SDK 的集成检查，需通过 DSH 的 Electron-as-Node 运行；相应文件中注明了 SDK 路径参数或 `DSH_TEST_SDK_ROOT` 环境变量。

当前源码声明支持 DSH ≥ 0.2.1-rc.2，不设版本上限；不再将 SDK 检查锁定到某个 rc 版本，各 SDK 包仍需版本一致。Git 标签安装仍使用已发布版本；本地验证当前未发布修改时，按配套仓库 `tools/README.md` 先同步再部署。

## 许可证

[MIT License](LICENSE)。保留已有 DeepSeek 版权声明，并记录本项目贡献者的版权。

# @goodjin2/dsh-acp-agent

[English](README.md) | [中文](README.zh.md)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that connects external coding agents to DSH's native session interface. Supports GLM (ZCode), MiniMax, Codex, Claude, Grok, Cursor, and Qoder.

## What it does

**Host side** (loads in the DSH process):

- **ACP agent framework** — transports (stdio, WebSocket), per-agent dialects, frame projection, terminal & file sub-protocols
- **GLM (ZCode) model client** — decrypts local ZCode login, calls GLM Coding Plan, streams responses
- **MiniMax model client** — reads/refreshes MiniMax Code credentials, calls managed gateway
- **Preset dispatch** — registers external agents as DSH presets, takes over sessions, routes turns, handles model switching
- **Quota endpoints** — host-side GLM/MiniMax/Codex/Claude quota routes (credentials never leave the host process)
- **Roster filter** — hides marked presets from the new-session picker
- **Mermaid asset** — serves the Mermaid rendering runtime on demand

**Browser side** (`./client` entry, auto-loaded by DSH Web via the `dsh.client` declaration):

- **Quota pills** — the GLM/MiniMax/Codex/Claude pills under the composer, polling the host routes
- **Model visibility panel** — settings section to hide providers and models from the pickers
- **Model label** — the composer's model chip
- **Switch feedback** — handover notice and switch progress bar when the conversation moves to a new session
- **Turn recovery** — the expand button for interrupted no-text turns; resend for requests that never entered the transcript
- **ACP process view** — terminal/file step rendering for external agent turns. It
  works standalone and, when `@goodjin2/dsh-chat-area` is installed, plugs into that
  package's `assistant-step` wrapper through the seat
  `conversation.chat.node.acp-segment-renderer` (chat-area owns the declaration).

## MiniMax login: refresh, and what happens when it can't

The MiniMax client borrows the local MiniMax Code login
(`~/.minimax/auth/<buildEnv>/<region>/mcode-public/auth.json`) and refreshes it through
the same official OAuth core — same credential store, same cross-process lock — so a
refresh here never invalidates the desktop app or the CLI.

When the refresh token itself is dead, retrying is pointless, so the plugin now says
*where to authorize* instead of failing quietly:

- `resolveCredential` raises `MiniMaxLoginRequiredError` (`reason: 'missing' | 'expired'`);
- the quota route (`GET /threadharbor/minimax/quota`) answers
  `{ ok: false, needsLogin: true, login: { url, userCode?, expiresInSec? } }`;
- a model request that cannot authenticate puts the authorization link into the error
  it streams into the conversation, so the link is clickable where the failure shows up.

The link comes from the same device-authorization flow the desktop app uses
(`POST /oauth2/device/code` → `verification_uri_complete`). The plugin starts one in the
background and waits at most 3 s for the prompt, because while MiniMax Code is running it
holds the auth lock and our login has to queue: the first response may carry just the
account origin, and the next poll (30 s later) the complete link with the user code. Once
the user authorizes, the official core writes the new credential back to the shared
`auth.json` and the next call simply works. Tokens never enter these payloads, log lines
or error strings.

## 0.3.0 — what moved out

Generic conversation-area UI moved to [`@goodjin2/dsh-chat-area`](https://github.com/threadharbor/dsh-chat-area)
in 2026-11: the answer card, the conversation file cards, the Mermaid renderer and
its host route, and the short session-ID bar. This package keeps the ACP side and
no longer exports `./mermaid-asset` — if your profile still lists
`@goodjin2/dsh-acp-agent/mermaid-asset`, replace it with
`@goodjin2/dsh-chat-area/mermaid-asset` (or drop it; chat-area's own bundle patch
declares it).

Browser layering, when both packages are installed: `assistant-step` renders the
**lowest** priority entry, so chat-area wraps at `-50` and this package at `-40`
(fallback for acp-agent-only installs). Only chat-area declares the seat; a second
declaration throws and is swallowed, which used to make the result depend on
assembly order.

## Install

From GitHub Packages:

```sh
# Set up auth (one-time)
echo "//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN" >> ~/.npmrc
echo "@goodjin:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com" >> ~/.npmrc

dsh plugin --profile web add @goodjin2/dsh-acp-agent
```

Or add to your profile's `package.json`:

```json
{
  "dependencies": { "@goodjin2/dsh-acp-agent": "^0.1.0" }
}
```

Then add the agent presets you want to your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. This repo ships its own `cordis.patch.yml` with the seven agent preset rows, the browser-half roster row (`acp-agent-client`, a bare package-name row — DSH only treats rows named exactly that way as client entries), and the host-side `roster-filter` / `zcode-quota` / `minimaxi-quota` / `codex-quota` / `claude-quota` mounts (moved here from the threadharbor umbrella in 2026-11). See the [installation guide](https://github.com/goodjin/threadharbor/blob/main/docs/install-plugins.zh.md) for details.

## Requirements

- DSH ≥ 0.2.1-rc.2
- Node ≥ 22.19 (or ≥ 24)
- For GLM: ZCode desktop app installed and logged in
- For MiniMax: MiniMax Code installed and logged in

## Publish

```sh
gh auth refresh -h github.com -s write:packages
NODE_AUTH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) npm publish --registry https://npm.pkg.github.com
```

## License

MIT

# dsh-chat-area

DSH 会话区增强插件：与跑哪种 agent 无关的会话区功能都归这里。

## 装上会发生什么

- **短会话 ID + 复制**：会话标题栏右端一枚工具，显示去掉 `session-` 前缀的前 8 位
  （完整 id 在 `title` 里），旁边一个「复制」按钮，复制成功后短暂提示。
- **答案卡片**：一轮的最终回答外面套一层卡片，带编辑 / 复制 / 另存为新会话任务。
- **会话尾部文件卡片**：从一轮的输出里认出文件路径，就地展开阅读、编辑、
  发送回会话、用桌面应用打开；超过四个折叠。
- **Mermaid 图渲染**：把 Markdown 里的 ` ```mermaid ` 代码块画成 SVG，可切「图表 /
  源码」。运行时 3.5 MB 不内联进客户端包，第一次遇到图时才从宿主路由
  `/threadharbor/mermaid.js` 懒加载。

| 功能 | 注册位置 |
| --- | --- |
| 短会话 ID + 复制 | `conversation.session.header.utilities`（会话作用域 list） |
| 答案卡片 | 包住 `conversation.chat.node` 的 `assistant-step`（优先级 -50） |
| 会话尾部文件卡片 | `conversation.chat.turnTail` |
| Mermaid | DOM 级（扫已渲染的 Markdown）+ 宿主路由 `/threadharbor/mermaid.js` |

## 与 dsh-acp-agent 的关系（两个包都装时）

ACP 的**进程段**（工具调用/思考的过程卡片）是 agent 专属的，仍留在
`@goodjin2/dsh-acp-agent`。两个包通过一个跨包座位接起来：

1. 本包在重注册 `assistant-step` 包装时**声明**座位
   `conversation.chat.node.acp-segment-renderer`（`children` 表，list 类型）。
2. acp-agent 发现座位存在后，把它的 `AcpProcessBlock` 注册进来。
3. 本包的包装在渲染时按座位取名：带 `acpProcessSegment` 的节点交给它，其余步骤
   走答案卡片。

`assistant-step` 的规则是「优先级最低的那条渲染」。本包用 **-50**、acp-agent 的
兜底用 **-40**，所以本包恒在外层；只装 acp-agent 时它那层生效，ACP 段照样完整。
改优先级必须两个包一起改——`tests/wrap-priority.spec.ts` 钉住了这个先后关系。

## 安装与挂载

```sh
npm install @goodjin2/dsh-chat-area
```

在 profile 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里加上 `@goodjin2/dsh-chat-area` 即可。本包自带
`cordis.patch.yml`（`dsh.bundle.patch`），里面有两行：

- `chat-area-client`：以**裸包名**挂载本包，浏览器半边靠它被扫进
  `window.__DSH_BOOT__`。这一行不是可有可无的：DSH 不按 `package.json` 的
  `dsh.client` 自动装载浏览器包，只看 Loader 的行名是否恰好等于包名
  （`ClientModuleRegistry.resolveMeta` 经 `locatePkgJson` 解析；带子路径的名字
  一律不算客户端行）。少了它，插件装上也什么都不发生，宿主日志里一个字都没有。
- `threadharbor-mermaid-asset`：宿主侧 `/threadharbor/mermaid.js` 这条 exact 路由，
  供浏览器半边懒加载 mermaid 运行时。

## 迁移说明（0.3.0）

mermaid 渲染、答案卡片、会话尾部文件卡片在 0.3.0 从 `@goodjin2/dsh-acp-agent`
迁到本包（agent 无关的通用会话区功能归本包，ACP 专属留在那边）。对应的旧行
`@goodjin2/dsh-acp-agent/mermaid-asset` 在 acp-agent 0.3.0 已删除；从旧版本升上来
时，把 profile 里这条旧行换成 `@goodjin2/dsh-chat-area/mermaid-asset`（或直接删掉，
由本包的 bundle patch 提供）。

## 开发

```sh
npm run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
npm test            # vitest（含产物的装载冒烟测试）
npm run build       # tsc -p tsconfig.json && tsdown → lib/client.js
```

`tests/bundle.spec.ts` 会把 `lib/client.js` 按页面的方式执行一遍（模拟
`window.__ModuleLoader__`、用页面给的 `require` 取 react / primitives、调 `apply`）：
产物格式或 id 写错时，这里会先红，而不是等页面在装配审计里判失败。

构建是**可复现**的：同一份源码连建两次产物字节相同（CSS module 哈希按基名算），
所以 `lib/client.js` 入库后，重建不会平白弄脏工作区，也不会触发无意义的页面热替换。

## Requirements

- DSH >= 0.2.0-rc.2
- 不需要宿主服务：会话 id 来自框架 props，复制走浏览器剪贴板

## License

MIT

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# Adapt ERP

[简体中文](docs/README.zh-CN.md) · [Releases](https://github.com/GuoMonth/dsh-erp/releases)

An ERP assistant is useful after it has seen your screens. Adapt ERP is a [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) plugin: it learns one ERP from the browser you sign into, keeps that map in a local SQLite index, and waits for approval before it changes the system.

You log in. DSH observes the pages you allow it to open. Later conversations read a short summary and one page of evidence, instead of starting again from a blank site. The plugin ships with no knowledge of your company.

Current release: **0.1.3**, for **DSH 0.2.1-rc.5** (upstream prerelease). Requires Node **>=24.18.0 <25**. Desktop checks cover Linux x64. Windows and macOS acceptance is still pending. `npm run verify` does not include a live model or a real ERP.

## When the assistant does not know the ERP

People who work in an ERP, and the operators who run dsh for them, hit the same walls:

- **The menus are local.** Purchasing, stock, and approvals sit behind names, tabs, and roles a general model has not seen. A new chat starts at the login screen again. A screenshot pasted into the prompt leaves with that conversation.
- **The whole site is a poor memory.** After the first look, the next question is usually where a screen is and what was already observed. Putting every menu into the prompt makes that answer slower and less reliable.
- **Looking and posting get tangled.** Opening a page, typing into a field, and saving can happen in one wander. A query that autosaves is still a write. Operators need the open and the change as separate, visible steps.
- **The record has to stay on this machine.** Login state, observations, and the database are working material. A colleague needs a reviewed note, not a copy of the session.

Adapt ERP sits in dsh for that job. It builds a depth-3 index from what the browser actually showed, hands that index back in short pages, and puts an ERP write behind a fresh approval.

### A user looking for a transaction

You signed in once and let the plugin snapshot the entry and the pages you approved. Next week you ask where goods receipt sits and which fields were on that screen. DSH reads the saved summaries and one page of records. It can do that without opening the browser. A question about today's quantities still needs a new observation. The index is what was seen, not a live ledger.

### An operator connecting one site

You have a URL and an account label. You put them in the DSH profile, start `dsh --profile web`, and sign in yourself. You ask for an entry snapshot, then approve each page the controller wants to open. The walk stops at the fields, tabs, and windows already visible. The model is not given a goal of finishing the ERP.

### A builder staying on native dsh

You want the model to call ordinary dsh browser tools, keep the host's approval and Skill machinery, and read a local index. The standard entry is `@guosheng_047/dsh-erp/native` on DSH 0.2.1-rc.5. Set `browserMode: managed` when you want the plugin's own browser. The current plugin does not use Deskwork.

## Who it is for

- ERP users who want later dsh conversations to remember menus, pages, and fields from their own site.
- Operators who configure one system URL, leave the password in the browser, and approve opens and writes one at a time.
- Builders who put that behavior in DeepSeek Harness and need the storage and approval boundaries to stay explicit.

## What it does not do

- It ships no vendor connector, industry template, or knowledge of your site.
- It does not crawl an ERP unattended. A finished round is not coverage of every permission or business rule. Depth stops at 3. Counts describe that round.
- Editing local knowledge does not change the ERP. Filling a field, choosing an option, or a click marked as a mutation each needs its own dsh approval. Scrolling is navigation. After an action, check the page.
- It does not require Deskwork, bind to a Deskwork website, or resume an older exploration queue supplied by the model. The host path is native Browser Use, official Playwright MCP, dsh approvals, and Skills.
- It does not claim Windows, macOS, live-model, or real-ERP acceptance. Smoke installs the packed plugin and exercises the DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 CLI, approvals, SQLite, and Chromium with a deterministic test provider.

Text inside pages and summaries is evidence. It is not an instruction to the model, and it is not permission to post a document.

## Install

With DSH installed and a model configured:

```sh
npm exec --yes --package=pnpm@11.28.5 -- dsh plugin --profile web add @guosheng_047/dsh-erp@latest
```

With only Node installed:

```sh
npm exec --yes --package=@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5 --package=pnpm@11.28.5 -- dsh plugin --profile web add @guosheng_047/dsh-erp@latest
```

Use the full package name. For a fixed release, replace `@latest` with `@0.1.3`. The browser provider prepares Chromium. Linux also needs a graphical session and Chromium system libraries.

## Quick start

Stop DSH and edit `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` (or `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`). Replace an empty `[]`. Merge an existing `id: erp` entry and preserve other plugins.

```yaml
- id: erp
  config:
    system:
      url: "https://erp.example.com/app/"
      account: "work-account"
```

Only `url` is required. `account` is a local identity label, not a password. Login paths, companies, and roles are covered in [configuration](docs/system-configuration.en.md).

1. Start `dsh --profile web` and ask it to call `erp_system_status`.
2. Open the configured entry and sign in yourself. The plugin does not take the password.
3. Ask for an entry snapshot, then `erp_learning_begin`. The controller owns the frontier. Level 1 can be that snapshot alone.
4. Approve each later page open. Level 3 records fields, tabs, and windows already visible, then stops.
5. Ask later questions with `erp_index_read`. Until a level summary exists, that read reports the index as not initialized.

To hand the map to someone else, ask for a Skill export, read the text, and share the directory. The recipient imports it as needs-review and checks it on their own ERP. The export omits structured identity, URLs, field samples, raw observations, screenshots, login data, and confirmations. Free text can still contain private information. The plugin does not upload the directory. Details are in [native operation and sharing](docs/native-and-sharing.en.md).

## How the index works

The plugin is a DSH service. A standard install loads the native entry. It reuses a Browser Use provider when one is already present, and otherwise loads official Playwright MCP. Computer Use loads only when `computerUse: true` is set. That path needs the optional native Cua Driver package and the operating system's permissions. Tool results are short Markdown with a title. An OpenUI payload is added only when that host service is present. DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 does not require one.

A native snapshot is normalized into a `browser-learning-v1` document before it is stored, so the same import path can read it. Exploration is breadth-first and owned by the controller: `erp_learning_begin`, `erp_learning_accept`, `erp_learning_block`, `erp_learning_status`, and `erp_learning_pause`. Callers submit observations. They do not submit the next unit.

| Level | What it records | Approval |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | The entry snapshot, including menus and pages visible there. | This level is the snapshot. Opening another page is the next level. |
| 2 | Pages opened from what level 1 showed. | Each open is a separate approval. |
| 3 | Fields, tabs, and windows visible on those snapshots. | The walk stops. There is no further business-behavior level. |

When a level's frontier is empty, the controller writes one summary, then places the next level on the frontier. A round holds at most 2000 items and accepts at most 200 discoveries at a time. Restart pauses a running round and does not replay website actions.

SQLite is the physical store (schema 4), with evidence files beside the database. There is no graph database. After initialization, `erp_index_read` returns up to 30 compact summaries, with a truncation flag when more exist, and one page of evidence-backed leaves. Omit the node to page the newest summary. Start `after` at an empty string and follow `nextAfter` while `hasMore` is set. Each page holds 1–20 leaves. `erp_knowledge_get` loads one full record. Search, neighbors, and history are the lookup path. `erp_knowledge_record` writes the local database and leaves the ERP unchanged. Level summaries stay in the local index and are omitted from a shared Skill.

Native browser and desktop calls request individual dsh approval. On the managed browser, `effect: navigate` is an open or a scroll, and `effect: mutate` is an ERP write. Fill and select have to be marked mutate. Local corrections and confirmations stay local: they attribute a statement to you and grant no ERP permission.

Saved knowledge is readable without a browser login. Current balances and orders need a fresh observation. Screenshots and page content may be sent to the model provider you configured. The published package does not contain your database, login data, or observations.

The decision record is [ADR 0003](docs/adr/0003-controller-bfs-index.md). Field-level contracts stay in the [knowledge](docs/knowledge.en.md) and [native operation](docs/native-and-sharing.en.md) guides.

## Update or remove

Call `erp_storage_backup`, stop DSH, repeat the installation command, and restart. Keep the same configuration and data root. This index does not continue an exploration queue that an older build accepted from the model. Opening an older SQLite file makes a checked backup and then migrates it. That migration does not mean the old queue still runs, and it does not mean Deskwork compatibility. Older Alpha layout and recovery are covered in [storage](docs/storage.en.md).

```sh
npm exec --yes --package=pnpm@11.28.5 -- dsh plugin --profile web remove @guosheng_047/dsh-erp
```

Stop DSH before removing the plugin. Removal retains your data.

## Documentation

[Guides](docs/index.md) · [Development](docs/development.en.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [MIT](LICENSE) · [Third-party notices](NOTICE.md)

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# TinyMCE HTML Editor for DeepSeek Harness

Edit `.html` and `.htm` files visually with [TinyMCE](https://www.tiny.cloud/) in the
DeepSeek Harness **Better Sidebar** editor. Opening an HTML file from the file tree
(or from an agent file link) shows a WYSIWYG editor instead of the plain code editor.

![plugin icon](./icon.svg)

## What you get

- TinyMCE 6 WYSIWYG editing of the document body, with a toolbar tuned for the
  narrow sidebar: history, blocks/headings, inline formatting, colors, lists,
  alignment, links, images, tables, media, and a source-code dialog.
- **Preview** (rendered page) and **Fullscreen** buttons from the OSS plugins.
- **Save** button and `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+`S`, with dirty indicator and save states.
- Disk-conflict detection: if the file changed on disk after it was opened, the
  save is refused and a **Reload** action is offered instead of clobbering it.
- Head `<style>` blocks are replayed in the editing surface so the WYSIWYG view
  resembles the real page.
- English and Chinese UI strings; the viewer can be disabled from the sidebar's
  Side card settings page like any other file viewer.

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with the [`dsh-better-sidebar`](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar)
  plugin enabled. This plugin registers a **file viewer** through that plugin's
  public registry (`ctx.betterSidebar.registerFileViewer`); without it the plugin
  does nothing.
- No network access and no TinyMCE API key: the runtime is vendored and served
  by this package.

## How it works

| Half | File | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Host | `index.js` | Serves `vendor/tinymce/**` at `/tinymce-editor/vendor/tinymce` (GET/HEAD, MIME, traversal guard, ETag/304). |
| Client | `client.js` | Registers the `.html`/`.htm` viewer (priority 20, `fsRead`), mounts TinyMCE, splices the edited body back into the original document, saves through `/sidebar/write`. |

### Body-only editing

TinyMCE 6 removed the `fullpage` plugin, so the viewer never feeds the whole
document to the editor. It splits the file at the `<body>` / `</body>` tags:

```
prefix (doctype + <html> + <head> + <body …>)   ← untouched
body                                             ← edited by TinyMCE
suffix (</body> + </html>)                       ← untouched
```

On save the editor's body HTML is placed back between prefix and suffix, so
doctypes, meta tags, head scripts/styles and comments survive exactly. Body
`<script>`/`<style>` blocks are additionally passed through TinyMCE's `protect`
option so they round-trip unchanged.

Files without a `<body>` tag (fragments/partials) are edited as a whole.

### Saving

Saving uses the sidebar's own `POST /sidebar/write` route with the `mtime` the
file was loaded with. That keeps the workspace fence and the conflict check in
one place. A `fs-conflict` response becomes the reload banner.

## Limitations

- **Body only.** Content outside `<body>` is preserved but not editable; use the
  code editor for head changes.
- **Relative assets.** Relative image/link URLs are kept verbatim on save, but
  the editor canvas resolves them against the Harness page, so relative images
  may show as broken while editing. Absolute URLs and data URLs render normally.
- **TinyMCE normalizes markup** you touch (attribute quoting, self-closing tags,
  whitespace). Untouched documents round-trip unchanged; edited regions follow
  TinyMCE's serializer.
- TinyMCE's own UI is English (the plugin's own labels are localized).

## Install

### From npm (published package)

**Settings → Plugins → Install bundle**, or:

```js
// plugin_manager
{ action: 'install_bundle', target: 'dsh-tinymce-html-editor@1.0.0' }
```

### From a local checkout (development)

```js
// plugin_manager
{ action: 'install_bundle', target: '/absolute/path/to/TinyMCE for DSH' }
```

Either way the bundle inserts one Loader row, `tinymce-html-editor`. The Better
Sidebar bundle must already be installed and enabled for the viewer to appear.

To remove it: `plugin_manager` `remove_bundle` with `dsh-tinymce-html-editor`, or
the Plugins page.

After installing into an already-open GUI, refresh the page once if the viewer
does not appear immediately: a freshly added client module is picked up by the
live plugin graph, but a page that booted before the install may still be
running its old module set.

### Health check

`GET http://127.0.0.1:<port>/tinymce-editor/health` reports:

```json
{ "ok": true, "version": "1.0.0", "clientUrl": "plugins/??dsh-tinymce-html-editor/client.js&rev=…",
  "clientReady": true, "clientReadyAt": 1730000000000 }
```

`clientReady` flips to `true` when a connected page has loaded the client half
and registered the viewer (the client posts a small beacon on apply).

## Layout

```
tinymce-html-editor/
├── package.json          # dsh.bundle patch + dsh.client web module
├── cordis.patch.yml      # inserts the tinymce-html-editor row
├── index.js              # Host: static TinyMCE asset route
├── client.js             # Client: file viewer + editor component
├── locale/{en,zh}.json   # Plugin Manager title/description
├── icon.svg
├── test/client.test.mjs  # document splice + registration tests
└── vendor/tinymce/       # TinyMCE 6.8.6 subset (MIT, see license.txt)
```

## Testing

```bash
node --test test/client.test.mjs
```

The tests evaluate the real client bundle with a minimal React/DOM stub and
cover the body splice, head-style extraction and viewer registration.

## Third-party notices

TinyMCE 6.8.6 is © Tiny Technologies, Inc. and is redistributed under the MIT
license; the full text and third-party notices are in
`vendor/tinymce/license.txt` and `vendor/tinymce/notices.txt`.

# attendance-clock · 打卡倒计时

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

一个 [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) 插件：在 Web 界面消息输入框底部常驻一行极简打卡状态芯片。

![icon](icon.svg)

## 功能

- **上班打卡倒计时**：工作日上班时间（默认 08:30）截止，未打卡时显示剩余时间，点击芯片即完成打卡（按天记录在浏览器 `localStorage`，重启不丢）
- **醒目提醒**：截止前 5 分钟橙色 + 闪烁并发送浏览器系统通知；前 1 分钟红色急促闪烁 + 二次通知；过点未打卡补发提醒
- **下班倒计时 + 进度圆环**：打卡后显示距下班时间的倒计时。总时长按 `下班 − min(打卡时刻, 上班)` 计算：早打卡起点更早，晚打卡总长不缩水
- **悬浮设置卡片**：鼠标悬浮芯片弹出设置卡，可直接修改上班/下班时间（即时生效，保存在本机浏览器）
- **午休模式**：设置卡内一键开关；开启后可设定午休开始/结束时间，打卡后的倒计时随之分相位——
  - 上午显示「上班倒计时」（下午时段显示「下班倒计时」）
  - 午休期间显示「午休倒计时」（距午休结束），进度圆环暂停推进
  - 进度圆环扣除午休时长，下班时恰好走满；午休结束前 5 分钟发系统提醒
- **状态语义**：已下班（绿 ✔ 满环）/ 缺卡（红）/ 休息日（灰），悬停可看完整规则
- **主题自适应**：全部颜色使用 DSH 主题 token（`--dsw-alias-*`），深浅色主题自动适配；界面语言中/英自动切换

## 安装

包为纯 JavaScript、无构建脚本，三种渠道任选其一（对应 DSH《打包与安装插件》规范）：

**① 本地目录 / git 克隆**（改源码即时生效）——在 DSH 会话中让 Agent 执行：

```text
plugin_manager install_bundle → <本仓库克隆路径>
```

**② tarball**（免构建授权，适合分发）：

```sh
pnpm pack                                  # 产出 attendance-clock-x.y.z.tgz
dsh plugin --profile <名称> add ./attendance-clock-x.y.z.tgz
```

**③ GitHub 直装**：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <名称> add github:hualiyexi/attendance-clock
```

## 兼容性

manifest 声明 `engines.dsh: ">=0.2.0-0 <0.3.0-0"`：适配 DSH `0.2.x` 运行时（预发布版本也参与匹配）。版本不满足时安装/启动会明确拒绝，不会带病加载。

## 配置

所有时间都在**悬浮设置卡片**中调整（鼠标悬浮芯片即弹出）：

| 设置项 | 默认值 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| 上班时间 | 08:30 | 上班打卡截止；此前未打卡显示上班倒计时，点击芯片打卡 |
| 下班时间 | 17:30 | 下班时间；须晚于上班时间 |
| 午休模式 | 关 | 开启后打卡时段分为上午/午休/下午三个相位 |
| 午休开始 | 12:00 | 需早于午休结束 |
| 午休结束 | 13:30 | 午休结束前 5 分钟发系统提醒 |

修改立即生效，保存在本机浏览器的 `localStorage`（键 `dsw-att.settings`）。

提醒阈值：`RING_MS`（默认截止前 5 分钟）、`SOON_MS`（前 1 分钟），在 `client.js` 顶部调整。

> 说明：这些是**浏览器端**参数，渲染在 Web 页面的 Client 模块不接收 cordis 行配置，因此没有做成插件 Config 字段——避免提供"可配置但不生效"的假选项；DSH 的配置规范（不同部署不同值的参数应走 Config）适用于 Host 侧插件。

## 目录结构

```text
attendance-clock/
├── package.json        # bundle 清单（dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client + engines.dsh）
├── cordis.patch.yml    # Loader patch：插入插件行
├── index.js            # Host 半（空实现，渲染在 Client）
├── client.js           # Client 半：芯片组件、状态机、通知、圆环
├── locale/zh.json      # 中文资源（含 Plugin Manager 展示元数据）
├── locale/en.json      # 英文资源
└── icon.svg            # 原创图标
```

## 许可

[MIT](LICENSE)

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
DSH One

The DeepSeek Harness (dsh) bridge for VS Code: dsh is installed by you, DSH One locates and starts it, embeds the dsh UI in your editor, and turns VS Code into dsh's launcher and display.

简体中文

> Unofficial community project, not affiliated with DeepSeek. "dsh" belongs to its original project. --- ## What it does - **dsh UI inside VS Code** — dsh web runs as a local service; DSH One assembles the official dsh web chat UI into a VS Code panel, and the sidebar runs dsh's sidebar UI with dsh-one's own sessions tree in place of the official workspaces panel. - **Start or reuse** — the extension probes the configured port and adopts an already-running dsh instance by connecting to it; otherwise it starts its own `dsh web`. It never downloads or installs dsh for you: the one automatic network call is a silent check of npm's `latest` tag for the status-bar hint, and an upgrade runs in a visible terminal only when you ask for one. - **Runs where you work** — dsh is started with the folder you have open in VS Code as its working directory, and the sidebar puts the matching dsh workspace first and tags it `vscode`. - **Sessions sidebar** — dsh-one's own sessions tree: sessions grouped by dsh workspace, with inline rename, pin, mark-as-unread, your own tag groups, multi-select (bulk recycle / archive), a recycle bin, and dsh's session search with the hit text highlighted. Hover a session row for the `⋯` menu, or right-click for the same menu; workspace rows have their own menu (rename, tag group, copy path, archive all its sessions, open the folder in a new window, remove from the list). The tree renders from dsh's live session and workspace data, so it keeps itself current — there is no refresh button. - **Chat area = the official dsh UI** — the conversation area is the official dsh web UI, the same components the browser page loads, assembled inside VS Code behind a local loopback proxy that handles login and leaves out the plugins that must not load there (the official app frame and the official sidebar — VS Code owns both areas, and dsh-one's own frame plugin takes over). Clicking the DSH One activity-bar icon opens the sidebar and the chat area together; clicking a session in the sidebar focuses the chat area on it. ## Screenshots > Every image under `docs/screenshot/` was captured before 2.0.0 and shows the 1.x UI: the sidebar, the status bar card and the chat area all look different now (the chat area is the official dsh web UI, the sidebar is the sessions tree described above). They are kept only for the part that did not change — how DSH One sits in the VS Code window. | Sidebar with dsh missing (1.x) | Status bar hover (1.x) | | --- | --- | | ![](docs/screenshot/en/install-guide.jpeg) | ![](docs/screenshot/en/status-bar-menu.jpeg) | ## Quick start Install DSH One from the VS Code Marketplace and click the DSH One activity-bar icon. On first use the extension locates dsh and starts the service automatically. The service listens on `127.0.0.1` only. If dsh is not installed yet, the sidebar says so and offers a **View install guide** button. The guide tab holds the one-line install command (a community script maintained by dsh-one): pick your platform, copy, run. The script reuses a compatible Node (`^22.19` or `>= 24`) or downloads an official portable Node — no admin rights needed — then installs the official `@deepseek-ai/dsh` package. Matching uninstall scripts live in [`install/`](install/). Prefer to set it up yourself? Install dsh manually instead (needs Node `^22.19` or `>= 24`): ```bash npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@next ``` `@next` resolves to `0.1.5-rc.3` today, which is the same version the untagged `npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh` (npm `latest`) installs — **both tags point at the verified 0.1.5 line**, so either command lands on a supported version. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR VS["VS Code window"] -->|"activates"| EXT["DSH One extension"] EXT -->|"1. locate dsh"| DSH["dsh executable
(dshOne.dshPath or PATH)"] DSH -->|"2. probe port (default 3080)"| PROBE{"dsh already
listening?"} PROBE -->|"yes — adopt it"| SRV["dsh web service
127.0.0.1:<port>"] PROBE -->|"no — spawn"| SPAWN["dsh web --host 127.0.0.1 --port <port>"] SPAWN -->|"verify"| SRV SRV -->|"3. display"| UI["assembled chat panel +
sessions sidebar"] ``` 1. **Locate** — the `dshOne.dshPath` setting wins; otherwise `dsh` is looked up on PATH. 2. **Start or reuse** — the configured port is checked to see whether a dsh instance is already running: if so, the extension connects to it and leaves it alone; otherwise it starts its own `dsh web`, with the folder you have open in VS Code as the working directory. 3. **Display** — the official dsh web chat UI is assembled into a VS Code panel behind a local loopback proxy (login cookie handling + the plugins that must not load there dropped), and the sidebar renders dsh's sidebar UI with dsh-one's sessions tree in place of the official workspaces panel. 4. **Keep in step** — the sidebar tree renders from dsh's live session and workspace data and the status bar follows the service state. DSH One writes into dsh's workspace list only when you add or create a workspace from the sidebar. ## Using DSH One - **Sidebar (default)** — click the DSH One activity-bar icon: the sidebar opens with the sessions list, and the assembled chat area opens next to it (once per window; if you close it, it stays closed). Pick a session in the sidebar to focus the chat area on it, or start a new session from a workspace row (its hover buttons, or its right-click menu); the toolbar `+` adds a workspace instead. - **Chat area** — `DSH One: Open Chat` opens the chat area explicitly (this is the same command the default-open path uses). - **Common commands** (`Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P`): | Command | Description | | --- | --- | | `DSH One: Open Chat` | Open the chat area | | `DSH One: Restart Service` / `DSH One: Stop Service` | Restart / stop the dsh service | | `DSH One: Show Status Panel` | Open the status-bar action panel (same as clicking the status-bar item) | | `DSH One: Show Logs` | Show the extension log | | `DSH One: Copy Local Access Link` / `DSH One: Copy LAN Access Link` | Copy the tokenized dsh web link (the LAN link requires LAN access to be on) | | `DSH One: Restart dsh for LAN Access` / `DSH One: Restart dsh for Local-only Access` | Toggle LAN reachability (takes effect with the restart) | | `DSH One: Check for dsh Updates` | Compare against the npm `latest` tag; offers Upgrade when a newer version exists | | `DSH One: Upgrade dsh` | Run the global install command in the integrated terminal; restart the dsh service afterwards | | `DSH One: View dsh Installation Guide` | Open the install guide tab (platform one-liner script + copy, plus a link to the official docs) | - **Status bar** — shows the service state. **Click** it to open the action panel, which lists the actions available in the current state (open in browser, check for updates or upgrade, copy access link, restart/stop, show logs, …) one action per row; **hover** shows the same set of actions as one link per row. For the instance DSH One manages, the hover also states whether LAN access is on, with a one-click restart to switch it when it is off. ## Settings | Setting | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `dshOne.dshPath` | `string` | `""` | Path to the dsh executable; empty means look up `dsh` on PATH | | `dshOne.port` | `number` | `3080` | Service port; `0` lets the OS assign one (adoption probe is skipped) | | `dshOne.autoStart` | `boolean` | `true` | Start (or reuse) the dsh web service when the extension activates | | `dshOne.lanAccess` | `boolean` | `false` | Expose the dsh web service to your local network (dsh itself still listens on 127.0.0.1; DSH One forwards from your LAN address). Anyone on the network with the tokenized link can use dsh. Needs dsh `0.1.5-rc.1` or newer — the oldest release this was verified against; on an older dsh the setting is ignored (with a warning) and the service stays local-only | ## Security and permissions - **Local only by default** — dsh always listens on `127.0.0.1`. With LAN access enabled (`dshOne.lanAccess`, or the one-click restart from the status bar), DSH One forwards from your LAN address to the local service — **anyone on the same network with the tokenized link can use dsh** (it can run commands on your machine). Only enable it on trusted networks and switch back to local-only from the status bar when done. - **Your dsh data stays dsh's** — sessions, workspaces and dsh settings belong to dsh. DSH One never deletes those files; the actions you take in the UI (archive, recycle, remove a workspace) go through dsh's own services. The extension also keeps files of its own under `~/.dsh`: plugin state (pins, unread marks, tag groups, the recycle bin) in `~/.dsh/dsh-one/.json` — the location and format the dsh plugin convention uses, so an official dsh page reads the same copy — and `~/.dsh/dsh-owned.json`, the record that tells the dsh process it started apart from another window's. It also looks there to find a dsh installed by the community script, creates the folder under `~/.dsh/workspaces/` when you create a workspace from the sidebar, and can open `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` in an editor tab from the settings page. Uninstalling the extension leaves all of it in place. - **No runtime management** — the extension does not download or manage Node.js / dsh installs; “Check for Updates / Upgrade” only runs npm's global install command in a visible terminal that you can interrupt. - **Process safety** — adopting an already-running dsh only connects to it and never kills it: `DSH One: Stop Service` / `Restart Service` end the process DSH One started, and nothing else. An instance started outside the extension (in your terminal, or by another VS Code window) is stopped only through `DSH One: Stop External Instance` / `Restart External Instance`, each behind its own confirmation dialog. Closing or reloading the VS Code window does not stop dsh, and neither does uninstalling the extension. ## Compatibility - **VS Code**: `^1.96.0`. - **dsh**: installed by you via npm (Node `^22.19` or `>= 24`). The **0.1.5 line** is verified end to end, and it is the line both npm tags point at today (`latest` = `next` = `0.1.5-rc.3`), so the plain install and the `@next` below both land on a verified version. - **Platforms**: Windows / macOS / Linux. ### dsh version tracking A scheduled GitHub Action ([dsh-upstream-watch](.github/workflows/dsh-upstream-watch.yml)) checks for new [dsh releases](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases) daily; for each new version it runs the automated probe suite (24 checks: the wire protocol, the front-end artifacts the gateway serves — boot contract, combo endpoint, Origin fence —, the client contract surface the assembled UI depends on, and the installed official artifacts: the internal identifiers inside the official packages plus the export names of the 27 official icons we take, a family that broke every one of our plugins once when upstream renamed it) and files an `upstream-watch` issue with the results. The last two badges above show the latest upstream release and the latest probe outcome; the full test list, per-version readings and known failures live in [docs/dsh-compat-checklist.md](docs/dsh-compat-checklist.md). **dsh versions.** Measured per version with a whole round of `npm run verify:lab`. The three groups are kept apart on purpose: | dsh version | Status | |---|---| | `0.1.6-alpha.1` | **verified** — 69 suites, 3620 assertions, zero failures (2026-09-22) | | `0.1.6-alpha.2` | verified — four drifts were found and fixed here (none of them visible to the probes, which only read bytes): the client started adopting the plugin roster the gateway pushes over `/plugins/events`, which reinstated the plugins we block and removed our own (the whole page rendered blank); the session list stopped carrying `current`, which left the sidebar tree with workspaces but no sessions (and the git card without a working directory); the session service dropped `open` / `select` / `clear`, which made clicking a session do nothing; and the `completed` flag moved off the session row into the `sessionStatus` hook, which lost the “finished, not opened yet” dot. One further drift (fixed in #225) broke the sidebar panel outright: a conversation-area card began waiting for a service the sidebar tree does not provide, so the panel showed the official boot-audit failure instead of the session tree. (Drift record for the earlier `0.1.6-alpha.1` round: the `details` slot was renamed to `rightbar`, new root-level hooks appeared, and the composer's `imageIds` / `addImages` became `attachmentIds` / `addAttachments`.) | | `0.1.5-rc.3` | **verified** — 73 suites, 3681 assertions, zero failures (2026-09-23, #238; 73 was the suite count of that round, before F-73 landed in #243). **This is what both npm tags install today** (`latest` = `next` = 0.1.5-rc.3), and what the `@next` in the quick start resolves to | | `0.1.5-rc.2` | **verified** — 73 suites, 3681 assertions, zero failures (2026-09-23, #238; 73 was the suite count of that round, before F-73 landed in #243); it is the floor of the version gate. Earlier the same line read “verified broken” with two failures, both of which turned out to be judgements pinned to 0.1.6-only shapes and were fixed in #238: the composer's ＋ is present in that generation too — it simply carries a different official label («指令» / «Commands» instead of “Add files or run commands”, that generation has no `pickFiles`) — and that generation reports a failing entry as `failed to … loader entry …` rather than the boot audit, which the startup self-heal now recognises (with one documented consequence: the per-audit entry count does not exist there, so the “too many entries at once” guard cannot apply). One limitation of that generation itself: archiving a session has **no undo** there — the official artifacts carry no unarchive carrier and no `unarchiveSession` method at all, so the archived-session section our tree adds for 0.1.7 deliberately does not appear (an entry without an action behind it would be a dead button); F-72 judges that negative invariant and records it | | `0.1.7-alpha.2` | **verified broken** — 48 of 74 suites pass / 26 fail (2026-09-24, exclusive window). Both blockers that made the whole round fail are fixed. **#236**: the official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` renamed its whole icon set from size suffixes to weight suffixes (`IconCloseFill14` → `IconCloseFillMedium` / `IconCloseFillRegular`, and 26 more we import); a name that is gone resolves to `undefined` instead of failing to load, so our sidebar tree's slot entry crashed at render (`slot entry crashed in 'sidebar.workspaces': Error: Minified React error #130`). **#243**: the roster baseline parameter was built by comma-joining the per-batch revs, and 0.1.7 splits the application batch in two so a rev now really contains a comma — the parameter came out truncated, the mirror read that as “the whole roster changed”, and tearing our own frame plugin down took the `root` slot registration with it and blanked the page. The remaining 26 failures are classified entry by entry in #244: 21 are judgements or fixtures pinned to 0.1.6 shapes (that generation redrew its icons, reworded entries and changed the slot shapes; the features themselves work), **none** is confirmed product breakage on 0.1.7, and 5 are not yet classified — F-71 among them is the suite's own click timeout, so it is an unstable test rather than a broken product. The same release also made `__DSH_BOOT__.batches[].url` relative (`plugins/??…` instead of `/plugins/??…`), which broke the mirror's combo fetch before anything could run at all — that one is fixed too. **Not a supported version.** | | `0.1.2-rc.1` | **verified broken** — 52 of 69 suites pass.
