DSH One

The DeepSeek Harness (dsh) bridge for VS Code: dsh is installed by you, DSH One locates and starts it, embeds the dsh UI in your editor, and turns VS Code into dsh's launcher and display.

简体中文

> Unofficial community project, not affiliated with DeepSeek. "dsh" belongs to its original project. --- ## What it does - **dsh UI inside VS Code** — dsh web runs as a local service; DSH One assembles the official dsh web chat UI into a VS Code panel, and the sidebar runs dsh's sidebar UI with dsh-one's own sessions tree in place of the official workspaces panel. - **Start or reuse** — the extension probes the configured port and adopts an already-running dsh instance by connecting to it; otherwise it starts its own `dsh web`. It never downloads or installs dsh for you: the one automatic network call is a silent check of npm's `latest` tag for the status-bar hint, and an upgrade runs in a visible terminal only when you ask for one. - **Runs where you work** — dsh is started with the folder you have open in VS Code as its working directory, and the sidebar puts the matching dsh workspace first and tags it `vscode`. - **Sessions sidebar** — dsh-one's own sessions tree: sessions grouped by dsh workspace, with inline rename, pin, mark-as-unread, your own tag groups, multi-select (bulk recycle / archive), a recycle bin, and dsh's session search with the hit text highlighted. Hover a session row for the `⋯` menu, or right-click for the same menu; workspace rows have their own menu (rename, tag group, copy path, archive all its sessions, open the folder in a new window, remove from the list). The tree renders from dsh's live session and workspace data, so it keeps itself current — there is no refresh button. - **Chat area = the official dsh UI** — the conversation area is the official dsh web UI, the same components the browser page loads, assembled inside VS Code behind a local loopback proxy that handles login and leaves out the plugins that must not load there (the official app frame and the official sidebar — VS Code owns both areas, and dsh-one's own frame plugin takes over). Clicking the DSH One activity-bar icon opens the sidebar and the chat area together; clicking a session in the sidebar focuses the chat area on it. ## Screenshots > Every image under `docs/screenshot/` was captured before 2.0.0 and shows the 1.x UI: the sidebar, the status bar card and the chat area all look different now (the chat area is the official dsh web UI, the sidebar is the sessions tree described above). They are kept only for the part that did not change — how DSH One sits in the VS Code window. | Sidebar with dsh missing (1.x) | Status bar hover (1.x) | | --- | --- | | ![](docs/screenshot/en/install-guide.jpeg) | ![](docs/screenshot/en/status-bar-menu.jpeg) | ## Quick start Install DSH One from the VS Code Marketplace and click the DSH One activity-bar icon. On first use the extension locates dsh and starts the service automatically. The service listens on `127.0.0.1` only. If dsh is not installed yet, the sidebar says so and offers a **View install guide** button. The guide tab holds the one-line install command (a community script maintained by dsh-one): pick your platform, copy, run. The script reuses a compatible Node (`^22.19` or `>= 24`) or downloads an official portable Node — no admin rights needed — then installs the official `@deepseek-ai/dsh` package. Matching uninstall scripts live in [`install/`](install/). Prefer to set it up yourself? Install dsh manually instead (needs Node `^22.19` or `>= 24`): ```bash npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@next ``` `@next` resolves to `0.1.5-rc.3` today, which is the same version the untagged `npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh` (npm `latest`) installs — **both tags point at the verified 0.1.5 line**, so either command lands on a supported version. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR VS["VS Code window"] -->|"activates"| EXT["DSH One extension"] EXT -->|"1. locate dsh"| DSH["dsh executable
(dshOne.dshPath or PATH)"] DSH -->|"2. probe port (default 3080)"| PROBE{"dsh already
listening?"} PROBE -->|"yes — adopt it"| SRV["dsh web service
127.0.0.1:<port>"] PROBE -->|"no — spawn"| SPAWN["dsh web --host 127.0.0.1 --port <port>"] SPAWN -->|"verify"| SRV SRV -->|"3. display"| UI["assembled chat panel +
sessions sidebar"] ``` 1. **Locate** — the `dshOne.dshPath` setting wins; otherwise `dsh` is looked up on PATH. 2. **Start or reuse** — the configured port is checked to see whether a dsh instance is already running: if so, the extension connects to it and leaves it alone; otherwise it starts its own `dsh web`, with the folder you have open in VS Code as the working directory. 3. **Display** — the official dsh web chat UI is assembled into a VS Code panel behind a local loopback proxy (login cookie handling + the plugins that must not load there dropped), and the sidebar renders dsh's sidebar UI with dsh-one's sessions tree in place of the official workspaces panel. 4. **Keep in step** — the sidebar tree renders from dsh's live session and workspace data and the status bar follows the service state. DSH One writes into dsh's workspace list only when you add or create a workspace from the sidebar. ## Using DSH One - **Sidebar (default)** — click the DSH One activity-bar icon: the sidebar opens with the sessions list, and the assembled chat area opens next to it (once per window; if you close it, it stays closed). Pick a session in the sidebar to focus the chat area on it, or start a new session from a workspace row (its hover buttons, or its right-click menu); the toolbar `+` adds a workspace instead. - **Chat area** — `DSH One: Open Chat` opens the chat area explicitly (this is the same command the default-open path uses). - **Common commands** (`Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P`): | Command | Description | | --- | --- | | `DSH One: Open Chat` | Open the chat area | | `DSH One: Restart Service` / `DSH One: Stop Service` | Restart / stop the dsh service | | `DSH One: Show Status Panel` | Open the status-bar action panel (same as clicking the status-bar item) | | `DSH One: Show Logs` | Show the extension log | | `DSH One: Copy Local Access Link` / `DSH One: Copy LAN Access Link` | Copy the tokenized dsh web link (the LAN link requires LAN access to be on) | | `DSH One: Restart dsh for LAN Access` / `DSH One: Restart dsh for Local-only Access` | Toggle LAN reachability (takes effect with the restart) | | `DSH One: Check for dsh Updates` | Compare against the npm `latest` tag; offers Upgrade when a newer version exists | | `DSH One: Upgrade dsh` | Run the global install command in the integrated terminal; restart the dsh service afterwards | | `DSH One: View dsh Installation Guide` | Open the install guide tab (platform one-liner script + copy, plus a link to the official docs) | - **Status bar** — shows the service state. **Click** it to open the action panel, which lists the actions available in the current state (open in browser, check for updates or upgrade, copy access link, restart/stop, show logs, …) one action per row; **hover** shows the same set of actions as one link per row. For the instance DSH One manages, the hover also states whether LAN access is on, with a one-click restart to switch it when it is off. ## Settings | Setting | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `dshOne.dshPath` | `string` | `""` | Path to the dsh executable; empty means look up `dsh` on PATH | | `dshOne.port` | `number` | `3080` | Service port; `0` lets the OS assign one (adoption probe is skipped) | | `dshOne.autoStart` | `boolean` | `true` | Start (or reuse) the dsh web service when the extension activates | | `dshOne.lanAccess` | `boolean` | `false` | Expose the dsh web service to your local network (dsh itself still listens on 127.0.0.1; DSH One forwards from your LAN address). Anyone on the network with the tokenized link can use dsh. Needs dsh `0.1.5-rc.1` or newer — the oldest release this was verified against; on an older dsh the setting is ignored (with a warning) and the service stays local-only | ## Security and permissions - **Local only by default** — dsh always listens on `127.0.0.1`. With LAN access enabled (`dshOne.lanAccess`, or the one-click restart from the status bar), DSH One forwards from your LAN address to the local service — **anyone on the same network with the tokenized link can use dsh** (it can run commands on your machine). Only enable it on trusted networks and switch back to local-only from the status bar when done. - **Your dsh data stays dsh's** — sessions, workspaces and dsh settings belong to dsh. DSH One never deletes those files; the actions you take in the UI (archive, recycle, remove a workspace) go through dsh's own services. The extension also keeps files of its own under `~/.dsh`: plugin state (pins, unread marks, tag groups, the recycle bin) in `~/.dsh/dsh-one/.json` — the location and format the dsh plugin convention uses, so an official dsh page reads the same copy — and `~/.dsh/dsh-owned.json`, the record that tells the dsh process it started apart from another window's. It also looks there to find a dsh installed by the community script, creates the folder under `~/.dsh/workspaces/` when you create a workspace from the sidebar, and can open `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` in an editor tab from the settings page. Uninstalling the extension leaves all of it in place. - **No runtime management** — the extension does not download or manage Node.js / dsh installs; “Check for Updates / Upgrade” only runs npm's global install command in a visible terminal that you can interrupt. - **Process safety** — adopting an already-running dsh only connects to it and never kills it: `DSH One: Stop Service` / `Restart Service` end the process DSH One started, and nothing else. An instance started outside the extension (in your terminal, or by another VS Code window) is stopped only through `DSH One: Stop External Instance` / `Restart External Instance`, each behind its own confirmation dialog. Closing or reloading the VS Code window does not stop dsh, and neither does uninstalling the extension. ## Compatibility - **VS Code**: `^1.96.0`. - **dsh**: installed by you via npm (Node `^22.19` or `>= 24`). sessions sidebar"] ``` 1. **Locate** — the `dshOne.dshPath` setting wins; otherwise `dsh` is looked up on PATH. 2. **Start or reuse** — the configured port is checked to see whether a dsh instance is already running: if so, the extension connects to it and leaves it alone; otherwise it starts its own `dsh web`, with the folder you have open in VS Code as the working directory. 3. **Display** — the official dsh web chat UI is assembled into a VS Code panel behind a local loopback proxy (login cookie handling + the plugins that must not load there dropped), and the sidebar renders dsh's sidebar UI with dsh-one's sessions tree in place of the official workspaces panel. 4. **Keep in step** — the sidebar tree renders from dsh's live session and workspace data and the status bar follows the service state. Only enable it on trusted networks and switch back to local-only from the status bar when done. - **Your dsh data stays dsh's** — sessions, workspaces and dsh settings belong to dsh. DSH One never deletes those files; the actions you take in the UI (archive, recycle, remove a workspace) go through dsh's own services. (Drift record for the earlier `0.1.6-alpha.1` round: the `details` slot was renamed to `rightbar`, new root-level hooks appeared, and the composer's `imageIds` / `addImages` became `attachmentIds` / `addAttachments`.) | | `0.1.5-rc.3` | **verified** — 73 suites, 3681 assertions, zero failures (2026-09-23, #238; 73 was the suite count of that round, before F-73 landed in #243). **This is what both npm tags install today** (`latest` = `next` = 0.1.5-rc.3), and what the `@next` in the quick start resolves to | | `0.1.5-rc.2` | **verified** — 73 suites, 3681 assertions, zero failures (2026-09-23, #238; 73 was the suite count of that round, before F-73 landed in #243); it is the floor of the version gate. Both blockers that made the whole round fail are fixed. **#236**: the official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` renamed its whole icon set from size suffixes to weight suffixes (`IconCloseFill14` → `IconCloseFillMedium` / `IconCloseFillRegular`, and 26 more we import); a name that is gone resolves to `undefined` instead of failing to load, so our sidebar tree's slot entry crashed at render (`slot entry crashed in 'sidebar.workspaces': Error: Minified React error #130`). **#243**: the roster baseline parameter was built by comma-joining the per-batch revs, and 0.1.7 splits the application batch in two so a rev now really contains a comma — the parameter came out truncated, the mirror read that as “the whole roster changed”, and tearing our own frame plugin down took the `root` slot registration with it and blanked the page. The remaining 26 failures are classified entry by entry in #244: 21 are judgements or fixtures pinned to 0.1.6 shapes (that generation redrew its icons, reworded entries and changed the slot shapes; the features themselves work), **none** is confirmed product breakage on 0.1.7, and 5 are not yet classified — F-71 among them is the suite's own click timeout, so it is an unstable test rather than a broken product. The same release also made `__DSH_BOOT__.batches[].url` relative (`plugins/??…` instead of `/plugins/??…`), which broke the mirror's combo fetch before anything could run at all — that one is fixed too. **Not a supported version.** | | `0.1.2-rc.1` | **verified broken** — 52 of 69 suites pass. That generation has no `openSession` at all, so “make a session the current one” — the main path — does not work (three root causes are listed in #234) | | every other version | **not tested** — including a `0.1.6` release (if one ships) and anything at or above `0.2.0` | **Version gate.** The assembled chat expects dsh `[0.1.5-rc.2, 0.2.0)`: the floor is the oldest version that passes a whole round, and nothing above the ceiling has been verified. The gate never blocks — a version outside the range gets an info banner at the top of the panel, and the banner carries the install command to run, not just the range: `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.5-rc.3`, which is the zero-failure round **and** the version both npm tags point at today (so following the quick start or the one-line script below also lands on it). `alpha` = `0.1.7-alpha.2` is inside the range but measured broken — do not install it. One known limitation: the gate is a whole-range check, so a version inside the range that is measured broken — `0.1.7-alpha.2` right now — passes silently. **On every upstream release, run the checks below** (prerequisites and details in the checklist). The browser lab appears twice on purpose: once on the candidate version, once on the dsh you have installed. | Check | Command | Covers | |---|---|---| | upstream probe | `node scripts/dsh-upstream-watch/probe.mjs --command dsh --expect-version ` | wire surface + client contract surface + installed official artifacts: are the slot names, root-level hooks, field/method names and internal identifiers we depend on still there | | browser verification on the candidate | `npm run verify:lab-version ` | does the assembly build up at all **on that version**: four trees boot with no crashed slot and no missing contract. Installs the candidate into a temp dir and runs the lab against it, leaving your installed dsh untouched. This is the gate 0.1.6-alpha.2's blank page walked past — probes read bytes and cannot see it | | browser verification on your install | `npm run verify:lab` | the same assertions against the dsh on your `PATH`; run it after every change to the assembly | | host-half verification | `npm run verify:host-half` | the gateway-side plugin half against official dsh | Who finds what: the probe runs daily in CI and catches renamed slots, hooks and fields before users hit them; the browser lab is the first check for any change to the assembly; VS Code verification (`scripts/dev-ui-test.sh`) is the final authority for host-layer behavior (CSP, clipboard, native menus, webview lifecycle). | Item | Coverage | |---|---| | Startup & auth (ready line, `?token=` cookie exchange, 401 fingerprint) | probe | | Unary RPC (`session/*`, `workspace/*`, `agentPresets/*`, `commands/*` args shapes) | probe | | WebSocket streams (`session/follow` snapshot, `session/control` baseline) | probe | | Client contract surface (slot names, root hooks, field names the assembly depends on) | probe | | Internal identifiers inside the installed official packages (silent-failure dependencies) | probe | | Assembled trees on a real gateway (boot, slots filled, no crashed entry) | browser verification — also on the **candidate** version via `verify:lab-version` | | Host-half plugin against official dsh | `verify:host-half` | | Live-streaming rendering, approvals/questions through the assembled chat | manual (per-version issue) | | Session-format migration & rollback, sandbox container regression | manual (per-version issue) | ### Known limitations - **Windows: subagent / background commands may pop a console window** — when dsh runs without a console (the extension's startup path), Windows gives every child process dsh spawns (bash, pwsh, taskkill, …) its own visible console window. This is an upstream dsh bug ([#1564](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1564); root causes [#1344](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1344) and [#1102](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1102)): a verified patch is proposed upstream but not shipped yet — wait for a dsh release and re-check afterwards. - **Remote (SSH/WSL/containers) not verified** — the extension supports running on the remote side, but this is untested. - **Multiple windows** — each VS Code window manages its own service, and a second window on the same port connects to the running instance instead of starting another. With `port: 0` every window gets its own instance and its own port, and the dsh UI then loses its stored session selection (browser storage is keyed per origin) — a fixed port is the better choice. ## Uninstall Uninstall the extension from the VS Code extensions view. dsh itself is installed by you and is not touched: the extension stops no dsh process when it goes away (stop the service yourself beforehand if you want it down), dsh data (workspaces, sessions) stays in place, and so do the files under `~/.dsh` that DSH One kept. ## Development Build from source with `npm install && npm run build`. `dist/` and `packages/*/lib/` are build outputs and are not in the repository, so build once before running anything that consumes them (`npm test` and the `verify:*` scripts run the build first themselves). The full guide — npm scripts, debugging, the verification lanes — is in [docs/development.md](docs/development.md). --- ## License MIT © dsh-one contributors

DSH One

The DeepSeek Harness (dsh) bridge for VS Code: dsh is installed by you, DSH One locates and starts it, embeds the dsh UI in your editor, and turns VS Code into dsh's launcher and display.

It never downloads or installs dsh for you: the one automatic network call is a silent check of npm's `latest` tag for the status-bar hint, and an upgrade runs in a visible terminal only when you ask for one. - **Runs where you work** — dsh is started with the folder you have open in VS Code as its working directory, and the sidebar puts the matching dsh workspace first and tags it `vscode`. - **Sessions sidebar** — dsh-one's own sessions tree: sessions grouped by dsh workspace, with inline rename, pin, mark-as-unread, your own tag groups, multi-select (bulk recycle / archive), a recycle bin, and dsh's session search with the hit text highlighted. If dsh is not installed yet, the sidebar says so and offers a **View install guide** button. The guide tab holds the one-line install command (a community script maintained by dsh-one): pick your platform, copy, run. (dshOne.dshPath or PATH)"] DSH -->|"2. probe port (default 3080)"| PROBE{"dsh already
listening?"} PROBE -->|"yes — adopt it"| SRV["dsh web service
127.0.0.1:<port>"] PROBE -->|"no — spawn"| SPAWN["dsh web --host 127.0.0.1 --port <port>"] SPAWN -->|"verify"| SRV SRV -->|"3. display"| UI["assembled chat panel +

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
DSH One

The DeepSeek Harness (dsh) bridge for VS Code: dsh is installed by you, DSH One locates and starts it, embeds the dsh UI in your editor, and turns VS Code into dsh's launcher and display.

简体中文

> Unofficial community project, not affiliated with DeepSeek. "dsh" belongs to its original project. --- ## What it does - **dsh UI inside VS Code** — dsh web runs as a local service; DSH One assembles the official dsh web chat UI into a VS Code panel, and the sidebar runs dsh's sidebar UI with dsh-one's own sessions tree in place of the official workspaces panel. - **Start or reuse** — the extension probes the configured port and adopts an already-running dsh instance by connecting to it; otherwise it starts its own `dsh web`. It never downloads or installs dsh for you: the one automatic network call is a silent check of npm's `latest` tag for the status-bar hint, and an upgrade runs in a visible terminal only when you ask for one. - **Runs where you work** — dsh is started with the folder you have open in VS Code as its working directory, and the sidebar puts the matching dsh workspace first and tags it `vscode`. - **Sessions sidebar** — dsh-one's own sessions tree: sessions grouped by dsh workspace, with inline rename, pin, mark-as-unread, your own tag groups, multi-select (bulk recycle / archive), a recycle bin, and dsh's session search with the hit text highlighted. Hover a session row for the `⋯` menu, or right-click for the same menu; workspace rows have their own menu (rename, tag group, copy path, archive all its sessions, open the folder in a new window, remove from the list). The tree renders from dsh's live session and workspace data, so it keeps itself current — there is no refresh button. - **Chat area = the official dsh UI** — the conversation area is the official dsh web UI, the same components the browser page loads, assembled inside VS Code behind a local loopback proxy that handles login and leaves out the plugins that must not load there (the official app frame and the official sidebar — VS Code owns both areas, and dsh-one's own frame plugin takes over). Clicking the DSH One activity-bar icon opens the sidebar and the chat area together; clicking a session in the sidebar focuses the chat area on it. ## Screenshots > Every image under `docs/screenshot/` was captured before 2.0.0 and shows the 1.x UI: the sidebar, the status bar card and the chat area all look different now (the chat area is the official dsh web UI, the sidebar is the sessions tree described above). They are kept only for the part that did not change — how DSH One sits in the VS Code window. | Sidebar with dsh missing (1.x) | Status bar hover (1.x) | | --- | --- | | ![](docs/screenshot/en/install-guide.jpeg) | ![](docs/screenshot/en/status-bar-menu.jpeg) | ## Quick start Install DSH One from the VS Code Marketplace and click the DSH One activity-bar icon. On first use the extension locates dsh and starts the service automatically. The service listens on `127.0.0.1` only. If dsh is not installed yet, the sidebar says so and offers a **View install guide** button. The guide tab holds the one-line install command (a community script maintained by dsh-one): pick your platform, copy, run. The script reuses a compatible Node (`^22.19` or `>= 24`) or downloads an official portable Node — no admin rights needed — then installs the official `@deepseek-ai/dsh` package. Matching uninstall scripts live in [`install/`](install/). Prefer to set it up yourself? Install dsh manually instead (needs Node `^22.19` or `>= 24`): ```bash npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@next ``` `@next` resolves to `0.1.5-rc.3` today, which is the same version the untagged `npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh` (npm `latest`) installs — **both tags point at the verified 0.1.5 line**, so either command lands on a supported version. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR VS["VS Code window"] -->|"activates"| EXT["DSH One extension"] EXT -->|"1. locate dsh"| DSH["dsh executable
(dshOne.dshPath or PATH)"] DSH -->|"2. probe port (default 3080)"| PROBE{"dsh already
listening?"} PROBE -->|"yes — adopt it"| SRV["dsh web service
127.0.0.1:<port>"] PROBE -->|"no — spawn"| SPAWN["dsh web --host 127.0.0.1 --port <port>"] SPAWN -->|"verify"| SRV SRV -->|"3. display"| UI["assembled chat panel +
sessions sidebar"] ``` 1. **Locate** — the `dshOne.dshPath` setting wins; otherwise `dsh` is looked up on PATH. 2. **Start or reuse** — the configured port is checked to see whether a dsh instance is already running: if so, the extension connects to it and leaves it alone; otherwise it starts its own `dsh web`, with the folder you have open in VS Code as the working directory. 3. **Display** — the official dsh web chat UI is assembled into a VS Code panel behind a local loopback proxy (login cookie handling + the plugins that must not load there dropped), and the sidebar renders dsh's sidebar UI with dsh-one's sessions tree in place of the official workspaces panel. 4. **Keep in step** — the sidebar tree renders from dsh's live session and workspace data and the status bar follows the service state. DSH One writes into dsh's workspace list only when you add or create a workspace from the sidebar. ## Using DSH One - **Sidebar (default)** — click the DSH One activity-bar icon: the sidebar opens with the sessions list, and the assembled chat area opens next to it (once per window; if you close it, it stays closed). Pick a session in the sidebar to focus the chat area on it, or start a new session from a workspace row (its hover buttons, or its right-click menu); the toolbar `+` adds a workspace instead. - **Chat area** — `DSH One: Open Chat` opens the chat area explicitly (this is the same command the default-open path uses). - **Common commands** (`Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P`): | Command | Description | | --- | --- | | `DSH One: Open Chat` | Open the chat area | | `DSH One: Restart Service` / `DSH One: Stop Service` | Restart / stop the dsh service | | `DSH One: Show Status Panel` | Open the status-bar action panel (same as clicking the status-bar item) | | `DSH One: Show Logs` | Show the extension log | | `DSH One: Copy Local Access Link` / `DSH One: Copy LAN Access Link` | Copy the tokenized dsh web link (the LAN link requires LAN access to be on) | | `DSH One: Restart dsh for LAN Access` / `DSH One: Restart dsh for Local-only Access` | Toggle LAN reachability (takes effect with the restart) | | `DSH One: Check for dsh Updates` | Compare against the npm `latest` tag; offers Upgrade when a newer version exists | | `DSH One: Upgrade dsh` | Run the global install command in the integrated terminal; restart the dsh service afterwards | | `DSH One: View dsh Installation Guide` | Open the install guide tab (platform one-liner script + copy, plus a link to the official docs) | - **Status bar** — shows the service state. **Click** it to open the action panel, which lists the actions available in the current state (open in browser, check for updates or upgrade, copy access link, restart/stop, show logs, …) one action per row; **hover** shows the same set of actions as one link per row. For the instance DSH One manages, the hover also states whether LAN access is on, with a one-click restart to switch it when it is off. ## Settings | Setting | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `dshOne.dshPath` | `string` | `""` | Path to the dsh executable; empty means look up `dsh` on PATH | | `dshOne.port` | `number` | `3080` | Service port; `0` lets the OS assign one (adoption probe is skipped) | | `dshOne.autoStart` | `boolean` | `true` | Start (or reuse) the dsh web service when the extension activates | | `dshOne.lanAccess` | `boolean` | `false` | Expose the dsh web service to your local network (dsh itself still listens on 127.0.0.1; DSH One forwards from your LAN address). Anyone on the network with the tokenized link can use dsh. Needs dsh `0.1.5-rc.1` or newer — the oldest release this was verified against; on an older dsh the setting is ignored (with a warning) and the service stays local-only | ## Security and permissions - **Local only by default** — dsh always listens on `127.0.0.1`. With LAN access enabled (`dshOne.lanAccess`, or the one-click restart from the status bar), DSH One forwards from your LAN address to the local service — **anyone on the same network with the tokenized link can use dsh** (it can run commands on your machine). Only enable it on trusted networks and switch back to local-only from the status bar when done. - **Your dsh data stays dsh's** — sessions, workspaces and dsh settings belong to dsh. DSH One never deletes those files; the actions you take in the UI (archive, recycle, remove a workspace) go through dsh's own services. The extension also keeps files of its own under `~/.dsh`: plugin state (pins, unread marks, tag groups, the recycle bin) in `~/.dsh/dsh-one/.json` — the location and format the dsh plugin convention uses, so an official dsh page reads the same copy — and `~/.dsh/dsh-owned.json`, the record that tells the dsh process it started apart from another window's. # 天工 / Tiangong Workbench

A **requirement-to-delivery workbench** for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`).

Create an app (or a project), describe what you need or attach a requirement document, and the
workbench runs the loop: it understands the requirement, plans a task graph, dispatches child
agents, verifies their test evidence, and records the delivery — with as little manual
intervention as possible. Every task stays bound to its own DSH session.

![Task board](docs/assets/board.png)

## What it does

- **Requirement intake** — paste text or attach a `.md` / `.markdown` / `.txt` document (≤512 KiB) right in the panel.
- **Planning as a contract** — the agent submits a validated DAG (owners, stages, dependencies, acceptance criteria); invalid plans are rejected with the exact reason.
- **Dispatch loop** — one ready work item at a time goes to a child agent, gets woken when it stalls, and its result is reported back with test evidence.
- **Evidence-gated completion** — a work item is done only with a real exit code, a positive pass count and zero failures; otherwise it becomes a person's decision.
- **Per-project delivery session** — each project gets a durable DSH session; the ledger records the binding, the model and the agent preset.
- **Task cockpit** — team graph, task list, decisions, usage and delivery artifacts for every job.
- **Automatic accounting** — token usage and cost per job, budgets, stall watchdog and round trip-breakers, with human gates on the exceptions.

| Requirement upload | Team flow |
|---|---|
| ![New task with an attached requirement document](docs/assets/task.png) | ![Team flow graph](docs/assets/flow.png) |

![Task session chat](docs/assets/chat.png)

## Install

Requires DSH **0.2.1-rc.0 or newer** (`engines.dsh` in the manifest).

This package is part of the [`jossion/dsh-tiangong`](https://github.com/jossion/dsh-tiangong) monorepo
(`packages/workbench`), so install it from a checkout:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jossion/dsh-tiangong.git
```

Then add the package directory to a profile with DSH's Plugin Manager (`install_bundle`) — or, for a
CLI profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add /path/to/dsh-tiangong/packages/workbench
```

Restart DSH after installing, then open **Plugins → Installed** to confirm `@jos/workbench` is active
and the **工作台 / Tiangong** entry appears in the sidebar.

The package resolves `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` from the DSH host for its `Config` schema; the
manifest declares it as a peer dependency.

## Configuration

The plugin exports a Schemastery `Config`, so every option is validated when the row activates and is
visible in Plugin Manager:

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `dataDir` | `""` | Ledger and deliveries location; empty means `~/.dsh/workbench` |
| `appsRoot` | `""` | Root for app workspaces created by the closed loop; empty means `<dataDir>/apps` |
| `agentPreset` | `""` | Agent preset for delivery sessions; empty uses the deployment default |
| `provider` / `model` | `""` | Legacy host-side planner route; empty uses the deployment default |
| `autoRun` | `true` | Drive intake-created jobs automatically |
| `wakeCooldownMs` | `4000` | Minimum gap between two wakes of the same agent |
| `planTimeoutMs` | `900000` | A planning turn without a plan becomes a human gate after this |
| `planNudgeMs` | `120000` | Send one planning reminder after this |
| `maxRounds` | `60` | Wake-round trip-breaker per job |
| `budgetUsd` | `0` | USD budget; `0` disables the gate |
| `budgetTokens` | `0` | Token budget; `0` disables the gate |
| `priceInputPerMTok` / `priceOutputPerMTok` | `0` | USD per 1M tokens for cost accounting |
| `loopTickMs` | `10000` | Safety-net loop interval |
| `stallAfterWakes` | `6` | Wakes without board progress before the stall gate fires |

## Data

The append-only ledger `~/.dsh/workbench/events.jsonl` is the single source of truth; every panel
view is a projection of it. Delivered apps keep their SQLite databases under the project workspace
the panel reads directly.

## Development

```bash
cd packages/workbench
npm test          # node:test suite
```

## License

# dsh-pet-jt

> **dsh-pet 的个性化增强分支**（JT = 自己的增强版）：整套桌宠能力原样保留，另加两块设置—— > **定时提醒**（自定义提示语，气泡复用对话气泡）与**随机出现 / 隐藏频率**（各 1–120 分钟随机）。 > 可与原版 [`dsh-pet`](https://github.com/PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet) **同时安装**，两份设置互不影响。 - 上游：`PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet`（MIT），本仓库基于其 **0.3.8** 的源码与全部动画素材（`assets/webm`、字体、表情包、通知图标）。 - 本分支不改上游已有的行为语义，只做**加法**：新增两个配置段、两块设置卡片、一条宿主定时器与一段客户端显隐调度。 - 图标：`assets/logo-jt.png`（AI 生成的毛线帽小鲸鱼，512 → 256px）；设置页导航用同一张图抠出的 alpha 剪影（`src/client/brand.ts`，CSS mask 只吃 alpha）。 --- ## 一、新增功能 ### 1. 定时提醒 在设置页「桌宠配置 JT」→「定时提醒」里维护任务列表，每条任务： | 字段 | 说明 | | --- | --- | | 时刻 | `HH:MM`（24 小时制），每天触发一次 | | 提示语句 | 显示在气泡里的原话，上限 120 字 | | 启用 | 单条开关（另有总开关） | - 到点后由**宿主**写一次 `pets..say` 叶子——与碎碎念、对话回复、第三方 `/broadcast` **完全同一个出口**， 所以气泡外观、显示时长（12 秒）、说话动画全部**复用对话气泡**，没有第二套气泡。 - 同一分钟同一条任务只触发一次；DSH 没在运行而错过的时刻**不补发**。 - 提醒会投给「当前交互桌宠」（与 `/chatjt` 的目标一致）；该宠物不存在时跳过。 - 提醒触发同时也是一次「说话」，因此会立刻把正在隐藏的宠物叫回桌面（见下一条）。 ### 2. 随机出现 / 隐藏频率 | 字段 | 说明 | | --- | --- | | 出现后最短 / 最长停留 | 出现后在 `[最短, 最长]` 分钟内**随机**某一刻隐藏 | | 隐藏后最短 / 最长 | 隐藏后在 `[最短, 最长]` 分钟内**随机**某一刻重新出现 | - 四个值单位都是分钟，各自 **1–120**，且「最短」不得大于「最长」（设置页与宿主两侧同一套校验）。 - 例：出现后最短 5 / 最长 20 → 宠物出现后 5–20 分钟内的某个随机时刻隐藏； 隐藏后最短 10 / 最长 30 → 10–30 分钟内的某个随机时刻回来。 - 隐藏是 `opacity: 0 + visibility: hidden + pointer-events: none`，**组件不卸载**：视频、动画、气泡、 拖拽位置全部保留，回来时是「同一只宠物」而不是重开一只；带 0.45s 淡入淡出。 - 任何一次说话（碎碎念 / 对话 / 定时提醒）都会让它立刻现身，并**从现在重新随机**下一次隐藏时间—— 不会出现「正说着话突然消失」。 - 关闭开关 = 一直显示（等价原版行为）。 - 作用范围：**网页 overlay 与桌面模式的透明窗口都生效**。网页端是整只宠物淡出（组件不卸载， 动画/气泡/拖拽位置全保留）；桌面端是主进程 `win.hide()`（整窗消失，隐藏期间连点击穿透都不用管， 回来时 `showInactive()` 并重新钉一次置顶）。 ### 3. 双击查看余额 - **双击宠物** = 查看余额，等价右键菜单里的「查看余额」：POST `/dsh-pet-jt-7340/balance`， 余额气泡由 `/state` 推送，网页端与桌面端行为一致。 - 拖拽中、刚拖完、飞行中被按住的那一下不算双击（那是在玩宠物）。 - 与「余额功能」开关无关：手动查看不受开关限制（开关只关自动轮询与档位动画）。 --- ## 二、和原版 dsh-pet 的隔离 两个插件可以同时开着，**任何一路都不重叠**： | 维度 | 原版 dsh-pet | 本分支 dsh-pet-jt | | --- | --- | --- | | npm 包名 | `dsh-pet` | `dsh-pet-jt` | | bundle entry id | `dsh-pet` | `dsh-pet-jt` | | 浏览器模块 id | `dsh-pet` | `dsh-pet-jt` | | HTTP 前缀 | `/dsh-pet-7340/...` | `/dsh-pet-jt-7340/...` | | 用户数据目录 | `~/.dsh/dsh-pet/` | `~/.dsh/dsh-pet-jt/` | | 配置文件 | 各自目录下的 `main-config.jsonc` | 同左（互不影响） | | Cordis 服务 | `petApi7340` | `petApiJt7340` | | 斜杠命令 | `/pet`、`/chat`、`/balance` | `/petjt`、`/chatjt`、`/balancejt` | | overlay 插槽 id | `pet` | `pet-jt` | | 设置页分区 id / 标题 | `pet-config` / 桌宠配置 | `pet-jt-config` / 桌宠配置 JT | | CSS / CSS 变量前缀 | `dsh-pet-` / `--dsh-pet-` | `dsh-pet-jt-` / `--dsh-pet-jt-` | > 命令名加 `jt` 后缀是必要的：DSH 的 `/` 命令表是全局的，两个插件都注册 `/pet` 会撞名。 > 设置页标题也不同（导航图标按分区标题匹配），所以两行会并排出现、各自独立。 --- ## 三、安装 插件以 DSH bundle 形式安装（与 dsh-pet 相同的机制）： ```bash # 方式一：命令行挂到某个 profile（ 换成你的，如 desktop） dsh plugin --profile add "D:/path/to/dsh-pet-jt" # 方式二：在 DSH 的插件管理里选择「安装本地 bundle」，指向本仓库目录 ``` 装完刷新页面，设置面板里会多出一行 **「桌宠配置 JT」**（图标是那只 Q 版小鲸鱼）。 > 依赖说明：`react` / `react-dom` / `@deepseek-ai/*` 全部由 DSH 宿主提供（peerDependencies）， > 本包不重复安装；`dsh.bundle.patch` 会把 `dsh-pet-jt` 这一行插进配置树。 --- ## 四、配置文件 设置页的「保存」写的是 `~/.dsh/dsh-pet-jt/main-config.jsonc`（可手改，JSONC 支持注释）。 两个新增段的形状： ```jsonc { // 定时提醒：每天 HH:MM 触发一次，语句进对话气泡 "reminders": { "enabled": true, "tasks": [ { "id": "r1", "time": "10:30", "text": "该喝水啦，起来动一动～", "enabled": true }, { "id": "r2", "time": "15:00", "text": "盯屏幕太久啦，看看窗外吧", "enabled": true } ] }, // 随机出现 / 隐藏：四项都在 1~120 分钟，且 min ≤ max "visibilityCycle": { "enabled": true, "visibleMin": 5, "visibleMax": 20, "hiddenMin": 10, "hiddenMax": 30 } } ``` - 两个字段都是**整段替换**语义（与 `physics` / `font` 一致）：写了就用自己那份，缺键按内置默认。 - 非法值（时刻不是 `HH:MM`、语句为空、时长越界或 min > max）→ 宿主告警并回落内置默认，不会让插件起不来。 - 设置页只提交它管理的字段；手写在文件里的其它高级字段（`animations`、`memes`、`whisperPrompt` …） 在保存时**原样透传保留**。 --- ## 五、开发 ```bash npm install --ignore-scripts # 只装构建期依赖（react 类型 / tsdown / typescript） npm run build # tsdown → lib/client.js + lib/index.js + lib/standalone.js npm run typecheck # tsc --noEmit ``` 新增/改动集中在这几个文件： | 文件 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `src/shared/extras.ts` | 两个新配置的**形状 / 默认值 / 校验 / 随机时长**（浏览器与设置页共用） | | `src/host/reminders.ts` | 宿主侧自包含副本：校验 + 「这一拍该触发哪些提醒」的纯判定 | | `src/host/index.ts` | `dsh-pet-jt: reminders` 定时器（启动对齐 15s，命中分钟写 `say` 叶子） | | `src/host/config.ts` | 读写两侧的整段校验 + `saveUserConfig` 白名单/透传 | | `src/client/settings.ts` | 两块新卡片（增删提醒、四个分钟输入）+ 保存时提交两段 | | `src/client/pet.ts` | 容器级显隐调度（随机时长、说话即现身）+ `hidden` 淡出 + 双击查余额 | | `src/client/brand.ts` | 设置页导航图标（从生图图标抠出的 alpha 剪影，内联 PNG data URI） | | `runtime/electron-helper/sprite.js` | 桌面端显隐调度 + 双击查余额 | | `runtime/electron-helper/{main,preload}.js` | `pet:set-visible` 通道（窗口级 hide/showInactive） | | `assets/config.jsonc` | 内置默认值（带注释，设置页「同步」会整份写进用户层） | --- ## 六、已知限制 - 提醒时间精度是「分钟」，对表间隔 15 秒；DSH 未运行期间错过的提醒不补发。 - 每条任务只有「每天一个时刻」，没有「工作日 / 每 N 小时」之类的重复规则； 需要一天多次就建多条任务（上限 40 条）。 - 桌面端「显示/隐藏」是窗口级操作：隐藏期间若从托盘强制唤醒，下一次到点仍会按配置继续循环。 --- ## 七、许可与致谢 - 本仓库沿用上游的 **MIT** 许可（见 `LICENSE`），动画素材、字体、表情包均来自上游仓库。 - 上游作者与项目：[PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet](https://github.com/PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet)。 - 本分支只对「配置段 / 设置页 / 定时器 / 显隐调度」做增量改动，其余代码与素材保持上游原样。

# agent-skilltree

**Status: M1 — policy-first skill tree for DeepSeek Harness (DSH).**

Allocate human-granted **skill points** across Development, Research and Personal Assistant nodes;
a **PolicyCompiler** turns the resulting `SkillTreeState` into an `AgentPolicy`; a real
`ctx.tools.guard` enforces path hygiene and locked sensitive tools. The agent can only inspect and
export — it can never allocate its own permissions.

![agent-skilltree running as a DSH plugin](ui/preview-dsh.png)

Host pin: `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5`. Public name: `agent-skilltree`. MIT. No secrets in repo.

**Not affiliated** (not affiliated) with DeepSeek, xAI, Blizzard, Cursor or any LLM/game vendor. The skill-tree UI is
an original implementation; the interaction metaphor is inspired by classic ARPG skill trees.

---

## Why this exists

A flat tool allowlist is either too permissive or too blunt. This project makes capability a
**budgeted, human-owned tree**:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  SP[SkillPoints · human] --> STS[SkillTreeState]
  STS --> PC[PolicyCompiler]
  OSP[OsProfile · detect] --> PC
  PC --> AP[AgentPolicy]
  AP --> HX["DSH tools.guard · path hygiene · locked tools"]
```

```
SkillPoints (human) → SkillTreeState → PolicyCompiler → AgentPolicy → DSH guard
```

- A point spent on **Development → Safe Patch** produces `toolAsk: patch`, not a silent grant.
- **Personal Assistant → Send Email** stays `toolAsk: email_send`; it is never auto-approved.
- **Governance → Strict Path Mode** turns on path-hygiene checks; Windows paths on macOS are denied.
- The agent cannot grant points, respec, unlock dangerous nodes, or clear the constitution.

## Domains and nodes

| Domain | Nodes |
|---|---|
| **Core** | perception (vision/search/memory/files), execution (tools, budgets, parallel, subagents) |
| **Development** | Repo Read, Safe Patch, Test Runner, Release |
| **Research** | Citation Check, Scholar Search, Research Synthesis |
| **Personal Assistant** | Inbox Read, Calendar Read, Draft Reply, Send Email, Schedule |
| **Governance** | consent, safety, audit, respec, build export, strict path mode |

51 nodes total. The YAML catalog is [`skills/mvp-36.yaml`](skills/mvp-36.yaml).

## Presets (human builds)

| Preset | Points | What the agent can do | Human approval |
|---|---:|---|---|
| [`solo-dev`](presets/solo-dev.yaml) | 26 | Read repos, run tests, propose safe patches, summarise diffs | `patch`, `release` |
| [`research-analyst`](presets/research-analyst.yaml) | 30 | Search, verify citations, read scholarly sources, synthesise | outbound network |
| [`personal-assistant`](presets/personal-assistant.yaml) | 24 | Read inbox/calendar, draft replies, propose schedules | `email_send`, `calendar_write` |
| [`ops-squad`](presets/ops-squad.yaml) | 32 | Fan out to subagents, run parallel operations | shell / write / network |
| [`reader-safe`](presets/reader-safe.yaml) | 18 | View images, search, read files, summarise only | write / shell / network |

Every preset carries `agent_purpose_zh` / `agent_purpose_en` so the operator knows exactly what the
agent is for — not just which nodes are lit. Details: [`docs/operations.md`](docs/operations.md).

## Quick start

```bash
npm ci
npm run check                 # build + 18 vitest + hygiene/secret fallback
npm run ui:data               # generate ui/nodes.js from the YAML catalog
npm run skilltree -- presets  # list human builds
npm run skilltree -- preset solo-dev
npm run ui:serve              # http://127.0.0.1:8780/preview.html
```

State defaults to `~/.dsh/skilltree-state.json` (atomic write, mode 0600). Override with
`SKILLTREE_STATE=/path`. The CLI and UI server share the same file; the DSH plugin reads it on every
guard call.

## Install into DSH (tested locally)

```bash
cp -a ~/.dsh/profiles/headless ~/.dsh/profiles/skilltree-test
dsh plugin --profile skilltree-test add /path/to/agent-skilltree
dsh --profile skilltree-test --dump-config   # shows "# == agent-skilltree"
dsh --profile skilltree-test --help          # loads without crash
```

The plugin is a `dsh.bundle.patch` layer; a linked install warns that peer dependencies are not resolved; they are optional in M1. Use `file:`
or a registry install for production. See [`docs/operations.md`](docs/operations.md) for rollback.

## What is actually effective

| Layer | Status |
|---|---|
| `PolicyCompiler` (SkillTreeState → AgentPolicy) | ✅ real; 18 tests |
| `pathHygieneCheck` (Path Hygiene + Shell Dialect; allow/deny/ask; never rewrites argv) | ✅ real |
| `ctx.tools.guard` (path hygiene + locked sensitive tools) | ✅ real; fake-host and DSH profile load verified |
| `skilltree.inspect` / `skilltree.export` | ✅ executable read-only tools |
| Human CLI `grant` / `allocate` / `respec` / `preset` | ✅ real |
| Persistent state shared by CLI / UI / plugin | ✅ real |
| Interactive grimdark UI | ✅ static HTML/JS; Grok Imagine art |
| `ask` approval flow | ❌ M1 treats `ask` as deny |
| turnCap / subagent / sandbox runtime enforcement | ❌ compiled into policy, not yet enforced |
| Cordis client UI / product Gateway | ❌ later |

## UI

- `ui/preview.html` — interactive tree: 5 domain tabs, state badges (`READY` / `LOCK` / `PREREQ` / `✓`),
  prerequisite edges, inspector, allocate/respec/export.
- `npm run ui:serve` — local server on `127.0.0.1:8780`, with `GET/POST /api/state` so the UI writes the
  same `skilltree-state.json` as the CLI and plugin.
- Art: `ui/assets/background-grimdark.png`, `node-frame.png`, `sigils.png` — generated with **Grok
  Imagine** (xAI), original, no third-party IP.
- Composite preview: `ui/preview-dsh.png` (DSH shell blurred behind the plugin UI; no usage text readable).

## Documentation

- [`docs/operations.md`](docs/operations.md) — install, presets, CLI, UI server, state, troubleshooting.
- [`docs/m1-limits.md`](docs/m1-limits.md) — what M1 does not enforce yet.
- [`docs/builds/`](docs/builds/) — older reference builds (YAML + preview art).

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE).

decision.reason: Static evidence chain reviewed. MIT plus NOTICE, explicit local-source install and pinned DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 bind checked-in dist entries and local modules. Host exposes read-only inspect/export tools and registers a tools guard or pre-execute fallback from persisted human allocations. The client is explicitly a deferred UI shell; this admission does not claim a complete graphical skill-tree product or prove guard enforcement. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# agent-ui-zh-hant

**狀態：M0 scaffold（繁中語包／港式詞表）——不是完整全介面覆蓋。**

KINFX 用的 **DSH 相容** Web GUI **繁體中文（香港）** locale pack：以官方 API `addLanguage`＋`register` 注入 `zh-Hant`（fallback `zh`），P0 命名空間含 `common`／`settings`／`chat`／`sidebar`（另附 `conversation`、`settings.locale`）。  
**同 DeepSeek、xAI 或其他 LLM 廠商無隸屬關係（Not affiliated）。** 技術段可寫「相容 DSH（DeepSeek Harness）」。

宿主釘選：`@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5`（內建語系只有 `zh`／`en`）。  
**不**用 `@mimateinn/dsh-i18n` 做主線（peer 對 0.2.x 不相容）。**不**整樹 fork harness。獨立於 L0 `agent-home-recipes`。

## English (short)

M0 **Traditional Chinese (Hong Kong)** locale pack for a DSH-compatible web GUI. Registers `zh-Hant` via official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-locale` APIs. P0 namespaces: `common`, `settings`, `chat`, `sidebar`. MIT. No secrets. Not affiliated with DeepSeek or other LLM vendors. Desktop chrome / hardcoded strings remain out of scope (see gaps).

## 架構示意

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph host ["DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 web GUI"]
    locale["dsh-client-locale\nzh / en built-in"]
  end
  pack["agent-ui-zh-hant\naddLanguage zh-Hant\nregister P0 dicts"]
  gloss["glossaries/zh-HK\n港式詞表"]
  pack --> locale
  gloss -.->|polish| pack
  picker["Settings → General → Language"] --> locale
```

*(Placeholder diagram — M0 has no runtime converter; dicts are pre-baked.)*

## 圖文占位

| 步驟 | 截圖／GIF（稍後補） |
|------|---------------------|
| 安裝插件後重啟 | `docs/images/install.png`（占位） |
| Language 選「繁體中文（香港）」 | `docs/images/language-picker.png`（占位） |
| 側欄「新對話」等港式用詞 | `docs/images/sidebar-hk.png`（占位） |

## 一鍵安裝

本插件是 **dsh bundle**（`dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml` insert），`dsh plugin add` 會寫入 profile layer，不是 plain dependency。

```bash
# 1) 釘宿主（若未裝）
npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5

# 2) 用本機路徑加 bundle 插件（發佈前）
export DSH_HOME="${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.agent-ui-zh-hant-dsh}"
mkdir -p "$DSH_HOME"
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/agent-ui-zh-hant

# 3) 重啟宿主／Web GUI，然後：
#    Settings → General → Language → 繁體中文（香港）
```

公開 npm／GitHub 後可改：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add agent-ui-zh-hant
# 或：dsh plugin --profile web add github:Kinfxhk/agent-ui-zh-hant
```

密鑰不需要、亦不應寫入本庫。只有空的 [`.env.example`](.env.example)。

## 本地檢查

```bash
npm run check          # 檔案／JSON／插件 export／粗略 secret 掃描
npm run extract:outline  # 打印抽取步驟（不寫檔）
# 有本機 dsh 時可重抽簡中源：
# npm run extract
# 改 dicts/zh-Hant 後：node scripts/embed.mjs
```

## P0 覆蓋

| ns | 來源包（抽取） | M0 |
|----|----------------|----|
| `common` | `dsh-client-locale` | ✅ |
| `settings` | `dsh-client-ui-settings-general` | ✅ |
| `chat` | `dsh-client-ui-chat` | ✅ |
| `sidebar` | `dsh-client-ui-sidebar` | ✅ |
| `conversation` | `dsh-client-ui-conversation` | ✅ 附送 |
| `settings.locale` | `dsh-client-locale` | ✅ 附送 |

港式詞見 [`glossaries/zh-HK.md`](glossaries/zh-HK.md)。缺口見 [`docs/gaps.md`](docs/gaps.md)。

## Desktop／硬編碼缺口（必讀）

- **Desktop 原生選單**（Application／Edit…）不經 client locale → 仍 en／簡中。
- **內聯 text map**、**第三方插件文案**、**註冊時凍結字串** → 語包覆蓋不到。
- 其餘未註冊 ns → fallback `zh` → `en`。

## 合規

*Not affiliated with DeepSeek or other vendors. Not legal advice. No secrets in git. Locale strings derived from a local dsh install are transformed for zh-Hant/HK; respect upstream licenses.*

## 授權

# dsh-slim-agent

面向消费级显卡本地小模型（1.7B–8B）与短上下文（4K–8K）环境的 DeepSeek Harness (DSH) 预设插件。通过“窄主代理 + 隔离子代理”的分工架构，在降低主窗口上下文开销的同时，提供受控的联网搜索与子代理多步研究能力。

[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.3.0--alpha.2-orange.svg)](https://github.com/langtune1111/dsh-slim-agent/releases)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-%3E%3D0.2.1--rc.1%20(0.2.1--rc.5%20verified)-blue.svg)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
[![CI](https://github.com/langtune1111/dsh-slim-agent/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/langtune1111/dsh-slim-agent/actions)

> ⚠️ **项目状态与环境说明**
> - 当前版本：`0.3.0-alpha.2`。**0.3.0 起移除 `task_complete`**（其 `concludeTurn()` 会丢弃最终答复，实测 3 次调用 3 次空答复），主代理工具面由 6 降为 5，并新增 `tools/pre-execute` 执行期白名单硬闸。
> - 上一版 `0.2.3-beta.1` 已在 **DSH desktop 0.2.1-rc.5 (Windows / 本地环境)** 上完成端到端联调与原生 `startActivation` 验证。
> - 本项目不包含虚构的性能跑分数字；固定开销数据均由透明脚本测量或经验估算得到（见第四节「开源复现指南」）。
> - `bash` 工具默认要求宿主提供沙箱接口 (`ctx.subprocess.spawn`)；在无沙箱的宿主上会明确报错拒绝执行。

---

## 一、 架构设计与分工机制

> **🔬 实验进行中：本地小模型到底能不能靠 agent 自己上网查资料？**
>
> | 项 | 内容 |
> |---|---|
> | 目标 | 验证 1.7B / 4B 模型在 **8K 上下文**下能否完成实时检索、多源核验、多跳推理、本地+联网四类任务 |
> | 设计 | **7 个 arm**：极简 / 标准 / slim 无搜索 / slim 有搜索 / slim 完整 / slim+task_complete / pi，全部只跑各自代码路径，不给任何一组外挂搜索 |
> | 变量 | 只拨产品自身开关（`enableSearch` / `enableSubagent` / `enableTaskComplete`），网页内容用冻结快照锁死 |
> | 作弊红线 | **DeepSeek 搜索 API 全程禁用**（插件层 + 凭据层 + 代码层 + 运行时层四重保证），违反即作废 |
> | 题量 | 12 主线（4 类 × 3）+ **3 道超纲题**（预期全灭，单列不计入主通过率） |
> | 状态 | ✅ **已完成：180 次受控运行** |
>
> **结论：严格口径通过率 `0/180`。** 但「能不能跑完」差异巨大——完整 slim 平均 78 s 收敛，
> 而「有搜索、无子代理」那一组平均发起 **26.8 次搜索后超时**（0/24 完成）。
> 子代理在这个量级上买到的是**不跑飞**，不是**答得对**；引用合规全线为 0。
>
> - 📊 **最新 Benchmark 报告** → [联网研究能力专项实验（180 次运行）](benchmark/history/2026-11-03__v0.3.0-alpha.1__web-research/REPORT.md)


在短上下文（4K / 8K）下运行全功能 Agent 时，数十个工具定义与长篇网页正文极易占满上下文窗口，并导致小模型产生工具选择幻觉。本插件采用“窄主代理 + 宽子代理”的分工模型：

```
                              用户输入任务
                                  │
                                  ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 主代理 (Main Agent) — 运行于 4K/8K 短上下文                              │
│ • 固定开销：约 0.9K ~ 1.2K tokens (含 tool-fs)                          │
│ • 仅暴露 5 个基础工具：                                                  │
│   read        edit        bash        web_search       subagent        │
└─────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                                      │ 遇到多网页阅读 / 深度资料比对
                                      ▼ 委派子代理 (subagent)
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 子代理 (Subagent) — 独立执行环境                                        │
│ • 拥有完整调研工具面 (web_search, web_fetch, read, bash...)             │
│ • 执行多步阅读、检索与比对                                              │
│ • 任务完成或预算耗尽后整体销毁                                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                                      │ 仅回传结构化提炼结论
                                      │ 【已确认结论】+【未验证疑点】+【建议下一步】
                                      ▼ (原始网页长文绝不进入主上下文)
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 主代理整合结论，执行本地代码修改并完成任务                               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 主代理 5 个工具职责

| 工具 | 来源 | 职责说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `read` / `edit` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs` | 标准文件读取与单处精确修改，受宿主工作区沙箱约束 |
| `bash` | 本插件 | 单条命令执行。默认由 `ctx.subprocess.spawn` 监管，绑定工作区并写审计日志 |
| `web_search` | 本插件 | 仅返回 3–5 条 `[来源标签] [标题](URL) (年份) - 一行摘要`，**不返回网页正文** |
| `subagent` | 本插件 | 委派子代理执行深度研究，通过原生 `startActivation` 调度，只回传提炼报告 |

主代理工具白名单具备 **fail-closed** 机制：`system-prompt/assemble` 过滤异常时返回空工具集；同时用 `tools/pre-execute` 做执行期硬闸——只在列工具时过滤不够，DSH 的 `fs-observation-policy` 会在模型读过文件后中途注册 `write` / `read_image`，那一轮不再走 assemble，越界工具会漏给模型（实测 `slim@65536` T2 第 4 次调用起工具数由 6 变 8）。

---

## 二、 架构的优势与不足 (Trade-offs)

客观评估“窄主宽子”架构的技术利弊与适用边界：

### 优势 (Advantages)
1. **主上下文开销受控**：主代理工具面收窄至 5 个基础工具，固定 Schema 开销显著降低，为实际任务留出 85%+ 上下文空间，缓解小模型因工具冗余导致的格式与选择错误。
2. **长篇网页正文物理隔离**：检索与长文阅读限制在独立的子代理会话中完成，原始 HTML/Markdown 不回流到主上下文，杜绝 4K/8K 窗口的直接溢出。
3. **显存并发防护**：通过异步信号量限制子代理并发为 1（默认，可配置），保证单卡本地部署时主子代理分时复用推理通道，避免多代理并发抢占显存引发 OOM。
4. **自洽免 Key 检索线索**：内置 DuckDuckGo / Wikipedia 降级检索链，辅以来源分类标签（`[源码仓库]`、`[文档站]`、`[社区讨论]`、`[百科]`）与年份线索，降低时效性问题上的盲目虚构。

### 不足与局限 (Limitations & Trade-offs)
1. **端到端推理耗时与总 Token 增加（时间换空间）**：
   - 虽然主代理上下文节省了，但子代理在独立会话中多轮执行搜索和阅读，**整个任务端到端消耗的总 Token 数和推理耗时实际上是增加的**；
   - 在本地单显卡部署时，主代理与子代理必须串行分时推理，如果子代理轮次较多，用户的**整体等待时间会明显长于单次直接回答**。
2. **依赖小模型的意图拆解质量**：
   - 1.7B–4B 模型本身的指令拆解与规划能力有限。若主代理生成的 `task_description` 或 `expected_output` 模糊不清，子代理容易检索偏航；若主模型未能准确判断何时该调用 `subagent`，分层优势将无法发挥。
3. **信息有损压缩（无法追溯正文细节）**：
   - 子代理只回传提炼后的三段式报告，主模型无法查看原始网页细节。如果子代理提炼遗漏了关键参数或代码段，主模型将无法补救。
4. **来源标签仅为域名启发式分类**：
   - `classifySource` 仅根据 Hostname 正则分类（例如将 docs.* 标为文档站、github.com 标为源码仓库），**并非真正的语义级事实核验**，无法识别虚假内容、社区争议或过时技术博客。
5. **轮次与工具预算为软约束**：
   - 当前 `maxTurnsDefault` 与 `maxToolCalls` 主要通过 Prompt 提示词进行约束，尚未接入基于子会话事件的外部强行终止（kill）硬熔断。

---

## 三、 实测数据与测试环境 (Empirical Measurements)

本仓库拒绝脱离实测的编造数字。以下展示本插件在真实硬件与网络环境下的**自测可复现基准数据**：

### 1. 真实测试环境 (Testbed Environment)
- **宿主机硬件**：x86_64 CPU (8 核 16 线程)，NVIDIA RTX 消费级显卡（6GB–12GB 显存，LM Studio 测试基准）；
- **操作系统**：Windows 11 x64 (Build 22631) 及本地 Windows 10 x64；
- **Node.js 运行时**：v24.16.0 / v22.11.0 / v20.18.0；
- **DSH 宿主内核**：DeepSeek Harness v0.2.1-rc.5 (Electron v44.7.0)；
- **云端 CI 矩阵**：GitHub Actions（Ubuntu 22.04 LTS、macOS 14 Sonoma、Windows Server 2022 × Node 20 / 22）。

---

### 2. 实测数据表

#### ① 首轮固定上下文开销拆解实测 (Fixed Prompt Overhead)
测试对象包含完整的 5 条极简系统工作规则及 6 个主代理工具定义：

| 组成部分 | 字符数 (Chars) | 估算/实测 Token | 占 8K 窗口比例 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **系统提示词 (Persona)** | 147 字符 | **~147 tokens** | 1.8% | 5 条工作规则，无冗余环境快照 |
| **4 个自注册工具 Schema** | 1,320 字符 | **~370 tokens** | 4.5% | `bash`, `web_search`, `task_complete`, `subagent` |
| **通信包装与消息帧** | - | **~120 tokens** | 1.5% | ChatML / Role 协议标记损耗 |
| **宿主 tool-fs 工具定义** | ~1,100 字符 | **~290 tokens** | 3.5% | 宿主注入的 `read` 与 `edit` |
| **首轮端到端固定总开销** | **约 2,567 字符** | **约 927 tokens** | **11.3%** | **稳定落在 0.9K ~ 1.1K 区间** |
| **8K (8,192) 任务剩余空间** | - | **~7,265 tokens** | **88.7%** | 充足留存给多轮任务对话 |
| **4K (4,096) 任务剩余空间** | - | **~3,169 tokens** | **77.4%** | 在 4K 极限短窗口下依然高度可用 |

#### ② 真实网络检索 Token 压制实测 (Search Token Suppression)
在真实网络环境下执行 `searchWeb(ctx, query, { maxResults: 4 })` 检索并统计注入主窗口的 Token 量：

| 检索用例 | 搜索引擎 | 耗时 (Latency) | 命中条数 | 本插件注入字符数 | 注入主窗口 Token | 对比：直接抓取网页正文 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `"nodejs LTS"` | DuckDuckGo | 1,454 ms | 5 条 | 790 字符 | **~277 tokens** | 5 篇网页全文通常占用 **15,000 ~ 35,000 tokens**（单次即溢出） |
| `"fastify vs express"` | DuckDuckGo | 1,820 ms | 4 条 | 812 字符 | **~284 tokens** | 4 篇技术博客通常占用 **12,000 ~ 28,000 tokens** |

> **实测结论**：通过线索截断与信源染色，主代理单次检索的世界知识消耗被严格控制在 **250 ~ 300 tokens** 以内（仅占 8K 窗口的 **3% 左右**），将原本会挤爆窗口的庞大长文物理隔离在子代理中。

#### ③ 子代理并发互斥锁（AsyncSemaphore）开销实测
执行 10,000 次高频 `acquire() / release()` 争抢微基准：
- **总耗时**：`13.52 ms`（10,000 次争抢循环）；
- **单次锁操作平均耗时**：**`1.35 微秒 (μs)`**；
- **锁开销占一次 10 秒任务的比例**：`0.0001%`（几乎零 CPU 损耗，无任何死锁与竞态发生）。

#### ④ 26 项单元测试与 CI 矩阵通过率
- **本地全套单测耗时**：`1.5s ~ 2.8s`（26 项离线测试全部通过，0 failure, 0 skipped）；
- **GitHub Actions 跨平台 6 节点矩阵**：
  - Windows (Node 20 / 22): 全部通过（耗时约 41s）
  - Ubuntu (Node 20 / 22): 全部通过（耗时约 26s）
  - macOS (Node 20 / 22): 全部通过（耗时约 33s）

---

### 3. 四种 Agent 配置 × 五档上下文窗口 横向实测（2026-11-03）

> ⚠️ **本节数据采自 `0.2.3-beta.1`**：当时主代理仍是 6 个工具（含 `task_complete`）。`0.3.0-alpha.1` 移除该工具后的数据见 [联网研究专项实验方案](benchmark/history/2026-11-03__v0.3.0-alpha.1__web-research/PLAN.md)。

在一台只有 6 GB 显存的消费级机器上，用 `llama.cpp` 本地服务两个真实 GGUF 模型，对比本插件预设、DSH 标准模式、DSH 极简模式与 `pi` agent 在 2K / 4K / 8K / 64K / 256K 五档窗口下的端到端表现。**共 72 次受控运行，token 数与耗时全部由线路上的计量代理记录，不是估算。**

**固定开销（首轮 prompt tokens，含工具 schema）**

| 配置 | 工具数 | LFM3 1.7B | Qwen3.5 4B | 占 8K 窗口 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **slim-agent（本插件）** | 6 | **1,289** | 1,401 | 15.7% ~ 17.1% |
| DSH 标准模式 | 24 | 6,073 | 6,186 | **74.1% ~ 75.5%** |
| DSH 极简模式 | 2 | 895 | 974 | 10.9% ~ 11.9% |
| `pi` agent | 4 | 1,441 | 1,567 | 17.6% ~ 19.1% |

**通过率（每格 2 个任务：写文件+执行、读文件取数）**

| 配置 | LFM3 2K | 4K | 8K | 64K | 256K | Qwen3.5 2K | 4K | 8K | 64K | 256K |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **slim-agent** | 0/2 | 0/2 | 1/2 | 1/2 | 2/2 | 0/2 | 0/2 | 1/2 | 1/2 | N/A |
| DSH 标准 | 0/2 | 0/2 | 0/2 | 2/2 | 1/2 | 0/2 | 0/2 | 0/2 | 1/2 | N/A |
| DSH 极简 | 0/2 | 0/2 | 2/2 | 2/2 | 2/2 | 0/2 | 0/2 | 2/2 | 2/2 | N/A |
| `pi` agent | 0/2 | 0/2 | 2/2 | 2/2 | 2/2 | 0/2 | 0/2 | 2/2 | 2/2 | N/A |

**四条硬结论**

1. **2K 窗口对四套配置全部不可用**，且原因完全相同：框架把 `max_tokens` 夹到 `1`，模型只能吐 1 个 token。小模型 Agent 的现实下限是 4K，且必须把工具面压到 1K 以内。
2. **8K 窗口是分水岭**：标准模式 24 个工具吃掉 74% 窗口，只剩 1 token 生成预算，实测两次全部失败；本插件（6 工具 / 1.3K）与极简、pi 均可正常完成工具调用。
3. **端到端速度 `pi` 最快、本插件最慢**：同任务下 `pi` 约为本插件的 1/3 耗时。插件把 6 个工具 + 5 条系统规则塞进主代理，换来检索与子代理能力，代价是小模型更容易进入多轮工具循环——这与"时间换空间"的定位一致。
4. **256K 能不能跑取决于模型架构**：LFM3 是滑窗注意力，同一张 6 GB 卡上真的开得出 256K；Qwen3.5 4B 的全注意力 KV 需要 8–9 GB，三种 offload 组合均 OOM。

**实测暴露并已修复的缺陷**：`preset-core.mjs` 原本的 `inject` 只声明了 `['tools','systemPrompt']`，却在代码里访问 `ctx.subprocess` / `ctx.subagents` / `ctx.agents` / `ctx.web`。在严格作用域的宿主上会直接抛 `cannot get property "subprocess" without inject`，插件整体不挂载——连白名单钩子都装不上，主代理反而会看到宿主全部工具。现已改为声明 `subprocess` / `subagents` 为必需、`web` / `agents` 经 `optionalService()` 可选读取，26 项单测与端到端复跑均通过。

**仍待修复（报告第 8.2 节）**：白名单只在 `system-prompt/assemble` 时过滤。若模型先 `read` 一次文件，DSH 的 `fs-observation-policy` 会在运行中途补注册 `write` / `read_image`，这两个越界工具会漏给模型（`slim@65536` T2 实测第 4 次调用起工具数从 6 变 8）。建议改用 `tools/pre-execute` 做执行期硬闸。

> 📄 **完整报告（环境数据、逐次明细、失效证据、复现命令）** → [benchmark/history/…/REPORT.md](benchmark/history/2026-11-03__v0.2.3-beta.1__llamacpp-four-arm-matrix/REPORT.md)

---

## 四、 🧪 开源复现指南 (How to Reproduce)

所有开发者均可在本地完全复现上述数据与测试：

### 1. 复现全套 26 项离线单元测试
```bash
git clone https://github.com/langtune1111/dsh-slim-agent.git
cd dsh-slim-agent
npm test
```
*（无需配置任何 API Key，100% 离线运行，验证沙箱调用、并发防死锁与配置保护）*

### 2. 复现固定开销字符经验估算
```bash
npm run estimate
```

### 3. 在本地真实模型上复现带 6 工具 Schema 的端到端 Prompt 开销
在本地启动 LM Studio（或 Ollama / vLLM），加载您的 4B 模型并开启 Local Server（如 `http://127.0.0.1:1234`），运行：
```bash
node benchmark/run.mjs --overhead --base http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 --model qwen3.5-4b --key <你的APIKey>
```
*脚本会自动向本地模型发送包含完整 6 个工具 Schema 的请求，读取模型返回的真实 `usage.prompt_tokens` 并写入 `benchmark/results/`。*

### 4. 记录与汇总标准评测任务用例
```bash
# 记录一次标准测试用例的执行结果（用例规范见 benchmark/cases.json）
node benchmark/run.mjs --record --case CASE_B --model qwen3.5-4b --ok --note "命中最新 Node.js LTS"

# 查看汇总统计
node benchmark/run.mjs --summary
```

---

## 四、 📦 安装与使用指南

### 安装方式

```bash
# 方式 1：推荐直接发网址给 DSH 客户端对话框自动安装
“帮我安装这个插件：https://github.com/langtune1111/dsh-slim-agent”

# 方式 2：通过 DSH CLI 命令行添加
dsh plugin add dsh-slim-agent

# 方式 3：下载 Release 离线包安装
dsh plugin add ./dsh-slim-agent-0.2.3-beta.1.tgz
```

### 🚀 重启一次即用 (One-Restart Setup)

本插件采用**内存注册表即刻激活 + 静态原子持久化双保险机制**：
- 安装完成后，**仅需完全退出并重启 1 次 DSH 客户端**；
- 打开任意新对话，在左上角的 **模式 (Preset)** 下拉列表中，即可直接选用：
  > 👉 **「中小模型·轻量知识增强 (8K Slim)」**

### 插件配置参数 (`config`)

可在预设定义或安装配置中调节以下参数：

```yaml
concurrencyLimit: 1        # 子代理并发上限（默认 1，防显存 OOM）
searchEngine: auto         # 搜索路由：auto (优先宿主，降级内置) | builtin (只用内置) | host (只用宿主)
maxTurnsDefault: 8         # 子代理默认轮次提示（软限制）
maxTurnsDeep: 12           # 深度研究最大轮次上限
maxToolCalls: 15           # 子代理工具调用上限提示
bash: sandbox              # 命令执行策略：sandbox (默认，需宿主沙箱) | local (本地执行+危险正则拦截) | off (不注册)
autoInstall: true          # 是否自动将预设维护至 ~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml（写前备份 .bak，原子重命名）
```

---

## 五、 本地模型部署建议配置 (LM Studio)

1. **测试基线模型**：推荐使用 `LFM-3 1.7B Q5_K_M`（极小规模）或 `Qwen3.5 4B Q4_K_M`（主力）；
2. **上下文设置**：在参数面板中将 **Context Length** 手动设为 **`8192`**（亦可用于测试 `4096` 极限窗口）；
3. **显存配置**：GPU Offload 设为 Max（4B Q4KM 权重约 2.6GB，8K KV Cache 约 0.8GB，合计约 3.8GB，可在 6GB 消费级显卡上流畅运行）；
4. 启动 Local Server（默认 `http://127.0.0.1:1234`），DSH 客户端通过 OpenAI 兼容适配器连接。

---

## 六、 🧪 自动化测试套件

本仓库包含 **26 项全离线单元测试**（不依赖外部网络与任何第三方 npm 包），覆盖安全策略、状态机契约与安装器防护：

```bash
npm test
```

测试覆盖范围：
- 信源分类器（域名启发式、年份正则）
- 异步信号量并发与防死锁释放保证
- 真实的 `ctx.subprocess.spawn` 沙箱参数分发与 `bash: off` 行为
- 破坏性命令正则拦截（`local` 模式）
- 搜索引擎三模式路由隔离（`builtin` / `host` / `auto`）
- 主代理工具白名单 fail-closed 异常保护
- 子代理原生 `startActivation` 接口契约
- 安装器单边损坏标记拒绝写入与 `.bak` 备份失败硬熔断防护

GitHub Actions CI 在 Ubuntu / Windows / macOS × Node 20 / 22 矩阵上全绿通过。

---

decision.reason: Static evidence chain reviewed. MIT, documented Git installation, engines.dsh at least 0.2.1-rc.1 and fixed host plus dynamically referenced preset-core.mjs form the chain. No lifecycle hook. Activation writes a managed preset block and copies core code into DSH_HOME; core uses public search and host subagents. Default shell mode refuses a missing subprocess service; explicit local mode uses child_process. These powerful options and configuration writes are recorded without execution or a sandbox guarantee. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.
