# dsh-opencode-session

Injects the OpenCode per-conversation `x-opencode-session` header on LLM
requests that the agent loop does not stamp, so every request to the pi-ai
`opencode` / `opencode-go` routes carries the header the OpenCode gateway now
requires.

## Problem

Since 2026-09-05 OpenCode Go enforces `x-opencode-session` on every inference
request ([docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/go/#where-can-i-use-it)). The agent
loop already stamps `GenerateOptions.sessionId` on conversation requests
(`packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts`), which the pi-ai opencode adapters
turn into the header. Hand-built auxiliary calls omit it — the
`experimental-auto-review` gate is the visible one, and its review prompt fails
with:

```
400: {"type":"MissingSessionID","message":"Request is missing x-opencode-session and cannot be routed efficiently. ..."}
```

Upstream tracking: [deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness#5495](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/5495).

## How it works

Registers a `prepend` listener on the `llm/stream` waterfall
(`packages/llm/dsh-llm`). When a request targets an OpenCode provider and has
no `sessionId`, it re-dispatches `ctx.llm.stream({ ...options, sessionId })`;
the injected request re-enters the waterfall with its session id set and passes
straight through to the adapter, so other listeners still run exactly once.

The injected id is the initiating conversation's DSH session id, recovered with
`ctx.agents.currentInitiator()` — the same value the loop stamps. Tool
execution runs inside the initiator scope, so the auto-review review call (made
from its `tools/pre-execute` listener) attributes to its parent conversation.

## Why reuse the conversation session id (no cache fork)

`x-opencode-session` is a per-conversation routing/affinity hint, not a stateful
session object: it pins consecutive requests of one conversation to the same
backend so prefix-based prompt caching hits. Prompt caches are content-addressed
by token prefix, so a divergent auxiliary request only misses its own prefix —
it does not evict the conversation's cached prefix.

- Official guidance: a **stable session id per conversation**, applied to
  **all** outbound inference requests
  ([opencode/docs/go](https://opencode.ai/docs/go/#where-can-i-use-it);
  [deepseek-harness#5495](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/5495)).
- The validated reference client Hermes sends the header "on main and auxiliary
  OpenCode requests" — one id per conversation for both
  ([docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/go/#where-can-i-use-it);
  [PR #101864](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/101864)).
- Harness's own compaction auxiliary calls already stamp
  `sessionId: agent.session.id`
  (`packages/compaction/compaction-basic/src/summarizer.ts`).
- A separate id would split affinity and was called "cache misses, slower &
  pricier" ([prior art](https://github.com/beihzb/dsh-opencode-session-header)).

If you later observe cache-hit degradation and prefer isolation, set
`sessionIdMode: 'per-call'` (below) — no code change needed.

## Config

```yaml
- id: opencode-session
  name: dsh-opencode-session
  config:
    providers: [opencode, opencode-go]   # routes that require the header
    sessionIdMode: conversation           # conversation | per-call
    fallbackSessionId: null               # optional stable id when unattributed
```

- `providers` — provider routes whose requests get the header. Default the
  pi-ai `opencode` and `opencode-go` routes. Commands / session config can add a
  custom gateway route.
- `sessionIdMode` — `conversation` (default) reuses the initiating
  conversation's id; `per-call` gives each unattributed request a fresh id.
- `fallbackSessionId` — stable id used when no initiator attributes the request
  (`ctx.agents.currentInitiator()` is `undefined`). Defaults to a
  process-stable uuid, so a request is never sent headerless.

## Install / mount

In-tree plugin (`plugins/opencode-session/`); it declares `dsh.bundle.patch` and
mounts through its own bundle layer, so `dsh plugin add` reconciles it into
`dsh.profile.bundles` and no manual `cordis.patch.yml` insert is written.

```sh
# web profile
npm run plugins

# desktop profile (the desktop app's CLI; the app must be quit first)
npm run build:desktop -- --plugins-only
```

Then restart dsh. Verify the loader entry appears and the profile's
`dsh.profile.bundles` lists `dsh-opencode-session`.

## Tests

```sh
pnpm run build   # tsdown -> lib/index.js
pnpm test        # node:test over the built injector decision function
```

## Known limitations & retirement

- Requests that already carry `sessionId` (conversation loop) and non-OpenCode
  providers are strictly passed through; the plugin never rewrites them.
- This is a stopgap: once upstream ships per-conversation session headers on
  every adapter path (discussion
  [#5495](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/5495)),
  the plugin becomes a no-op and can be removed
  (`dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-opencode-session`, restart).
- Prior art (not used here): `dsh-opencode-session-header` patches global
  `fetch` (beihzb) and `dsh-opencode-session` (brackrat); this plugin uses the
  official `llm/stream` seam and needs no transport patching.
# dsh-gui

A thin desktop shell for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
web UI. It is **not** a repackaged harness — it runs the dsh CLI that
`harness.json` selects (the `@deepseek-ai/dsh` registry package in the default
`npm` runtime, or the built `deepseek-harness` git submodule in `source`),
hosts the web server itself, and shows the full harness UI in a single webview
window. Nothing else is drawn: just the OS title bar and border.

## What it does

On launch the entry exe:

1. Opens one **frameless** webview window immediately and shows a loading page
   inside it. A harness cold start takes ~10 s (it is CPU-bound inside the
   harness), so the window never waits for it.
2. Spawns the dsh CLI selected by `harness.json` — that runtime's `bin.js` — with
   `web --port <port> --no-open`, and pins `DSH_HOME` to `./.dsh` inside this
   repository.
3. Waits until the harness answers `GET /` with `200` on `127.0.0.1:<port>`,
   then hands the tokenized URL to the shell page, which hosts the harness UI
   in one **child webview per connection tab**. A harness that cannot be
   spawned or never becomes ready is reported on the loading page (the window
   stays open) instead of behind a message box. On exit dsh-gui tears the
   harness process tree down; the harness runs inside a kill-on-close Windows
   job object, so the kernel enforces that teardown even when dsh-gui itself is
   killed (Task Manager, closing the terminal it was launched from).

The `ui/` page is a thin shell only: a drag-anywhere title bar with
**connection tabs** (VSCode-style, one per connected DSH backend), a **＋**
new-connection button, and on their inner side a hamburger (☰) menu — the
standard minimize / maximize / close controls come after it, and the hamburger
menu carries the tab list plus **新建连接** / **关闭当前连接** and the existing
**关于** / **退出** entries. The new-connection dialog supports a local backend
(probe the port, or start the built-in harness on it), a remote backend
(VSCode Remote SSH style: load the frontend, or SSH-deploy it to another host,
reaching it over an SSH local port forward), and a Docker backend (start dsh
inside a running container via `docker exec` and bridge its loopback port with
a `docker exec -i` stdio tunnel — no port mapping required). The connection
chrome lives in the
native title bar — the embedded harness page renders none of it. The About
dialog shows the version (exact git tag, else the commit short hash), license,
and GitHub link for dsh-gui, the deepseek-harness submodule, the whale-girl
app-icon submodule, and every plugin package under `plugins/`. The harness UI
itself goes on talking to its self-hosted server over plain HTTP exactly like a
browser.

## Screenshot

![dsh-gui screenshot](docs/dsh-gui/images/dsh-gui-screenshot.png)

## Features

### GUI shell

- **Frameless single-window shell** — a drag-anywhere custom title bar with
  native minimize / maximize / close controls; the title bar colors follow the
  light/dark theme reported by the embedded harness page.
- **Window first, loading page while the harness boots** — the window appears
  as soon as the process starts (WebView2 initialization only) and shows a
  loading card with the elapsed wait; the tab webview replaces it the moment
  the harness answers. Harness failures appear on that card, and the window
  keeps working (drag, minimize, close) throughout.
- **Native Windows 11 title-bar interactions** — hovering maximize shows the
  OS Snap Layouts flyout, double-clicking the title bar toggles
  maximize/restore, double-clicking the top border vertically fills/restores
  the window (including drag-to-restore), and the top-left app icon opens the
  window-control menu.
- **VSCode-style connection tabs** — one tab per connected DSH backend, with
  close buttons and persisted tab/active state; closing the last tab reopens
  the new-connection dialog.
- **New connection (`＋`)** — local backend (probe the port, or start the
  built-in harness on it), remote backend (load the frontend, or SSH-deploy
  it to another host and reach it through a loopback-only SSH local port
  forward), and Docker backend (start dsh in a running container via
  `docker exec -d`, then bridge its loopback port with a `docker exec -i`
  stdio tunnel — the container needs no `-p` port mapping; the container-side
  user, working directory and environment-variable list are configurable).
- **Hamburger menu (`☰`)** — tab list, `新建连接` / `关闭当前连接`, `检查更新`,
  `关于` / `退出`.
- **About dialog** — version (git tag or commit short hash), license, and
  GitHub link for dsh-gui, the harness, the icon submodule, and every plugin.
  A plain click copies the URL; **Ctrl+click** opens it in the system default
  browser.
- **Update dialog** — checks two kinds of rows and lets you pick which updates
  to run. **git rows** are this checkout and its non-`plugins/` submodules;
  each is compared against its remote default branch and offers a target
  (latest commit / latest tag). The top-level row's **更新** performs the
  git-layer update in the dialog (root reset plus recursive submodule sync)
  and then asks for `npm run build` and a restart; selected submodule rows go
  through a detached launcher that exits the app, runs the updates in a
  console window, rebuilds, and restarts the shell. **npm plugin rows** are
  the npm packages pinned by the `plugins/**/*.mjs` install scripts
  (`installNpmPlugin` with an exact `name@version` literal); each row
  compares that pin with the registry's latest version, and its **更新**
  button rewrites the pin in the install script and re-runs that wrapper in
  place — the app keeps running and the reinstalled plugin takes effect after
  a restart, with no rebuild needed. npm plugin rows have no tag/commit
  target and no **更新日志** button (a GitHub release cannot be mapped
  reliably onto an npm version). A batch that mixes both kinds updates the
  npm rows in place first, then restarts through the detached git flow, and a
  failed npm row never blocks the git rows, while a batch made up only of npm
  plugin rows finishes in place without exiting the app. Each row's module
  name links to that repository's **Releases list** page
  (`https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases`) whenever its origin is a
  GitHub repository — resolved locally for git rows, so that link is there
  from the first paint, and from the package's registry manifest
  `repository` for npm plugin rows, so it appears once the registry check
  lands; a non-GitHub or missing remote leaves the name as plain text. As
  with the changelog title, the row name is not selectable, so a plain click
  opens the system default browser. The dialog recommends AI-sync updates:
  each updatable submodule or npm plugin row and the bottom bar offer an
  **AI 更新** button that returns to the project home screen, selects the
  dsh-gui directory there, selects the 「创造模式」(cordis) preset, and
  prefills a prompt that asks the agent to sync the submodule(s) to the chosen
  target — for an npm plugin row, to raise the exact `packageSpec` in its
  install script and reinstall the package — and verify the result in the
  `.staging/dsh-gui` validation worktree — a git
  worktree of this checkout on the `staging/verify` branch whose runtime root
  is `<repository root>/.staging`, so the whole copy lives inside the session
  workspace — the worktree's WebUI must actually load, adaptation commits go
  straight onto `staging/verify` without approval, a harness update
  additionally needs a computer-use check that the GUI starts and runs, and
  phase two merges that branch back into this checkout only after you approve
  the verification report (the bottom button lists every updatable module with
  its combo choice, and every npm plugin row with its install script and
  target version; the preset can still be changed before sending). Each
  behind git row also has an **更新日志** button:
  for a tag target it shows the official GitHub Release notes for **every**
  release the update brings in — all tags between the current checkout and the
  update target, newest first, so a checkout several releases behind sees the
  whole span instead of just the target tag's notes — when the remote is a
  GitHub repository and releases exist, otherwise it asks the dsh AI to
  summarize the commits between the current checkout and the update target —
  through the running harness's raw-LLM route (the dsh-ai-update plugin,
  default model from the Models page), which creates no session, so the run
  never appears in the DSH session list; when that route is unavailable the
  shell retries it once and then falls back to the one-shot headless mode
  (`dsh --profile headless`), whose session store is redirected to a temp
  directory — neither path persists a session. The markdown result renders
  in a scrollable, selectable dialog whose copy button copies the raw source
  text; the provenance line and any failure message (for example a
  GitHub-Release fetch error) are selectable as well, so a problem can be
  copied out verbatim into a report. When the changelog came from a real
  GitHub release, the module name in the dialog title becomes a link to the
  repository's **Releases list** page (`https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases`,
  never a per-tag `/releases/tag/…` subpage); the title line is not selectable,
  so a plain click there opens the system default browser. **Ctrl+click** on a
  link in the body opens the URL in the system default browser (a plain click
  stays a text-selection gesture, since a webview link cannot spawn a popup on
  its own).

### Plugins

- **`dsh-remote`** — multi-backend remote mode: the connection tabs,
  new-connection dialog, local backend start, and VSCode Remote SSH-style
  deploy/tunnel described above (see `plugins/remote/dsh-remote/docs/`).
- **`dsh-sidebar-qa`** — select conversation text → right-panel follow-up
  question in a dedicated same-workspace session (`❓追问·<主题>`), without
  interrupting the main conversation; thin consumer of `dsh-better-sidebar`
  (see `plugins/better-sidebar/`; installed by the
  better-sidebar wrapper, after dsh-better-sidebar).
- **`dsh-better-sidebar`** — service-first sidebar workbench (right sidebar
  + bottom panel): per-session explorer, CodeMirror editor + file viewers
  (image/PDF/Markdown/HTML/code), real terminal (xterm.js + node-pty with
  reconnect replay; optional `terminal_*` model tools, off by default), Git
  panel, embedded browser, and background-job page (see
  `plugins/better-sidebar/`).
- **`dsh-ai-update`** — browser-half bridge behind the update dialog's AI
  update buttons: receives the shell's `dsh-gui:ai-update` message, returns
  to the new-session home, selects the dsh-gui workspace, auto-selects the
  「创造模式」(cordis) preset for the blank session (a refusal fails the
  request instead of silently using the default), and prefills the composer
  with the update prompt — never creating a session directly (see
  `plugins/ai-update/dsh-ai-update/docs/`).
- **`dsh-deep-whale`** — whale-girl skin series; currently ships the
  hot-pluggable `maid-atelier` skin (light/dark palace backgrounds, navy lace
  UI overlay, Q-version sidebar, embedded assets).
- **`dsh-skill-mcp-center`** — Skill & MCP management center: a "Skill & MCP"
  settings section for browsing, enabling and deleting skills and for adding,
  editing, enabling and removing MCP servers (hot-applied without restart),
  plus an MCP live-status sidebar tab when `dsh-better-sidebar` is installed.
- **`dsh-pause`** — a pause point right before the agent's next model request
  in a tool round: while paused the composer stays usable, a bare Enter in the
  main input (or the pause control) releases it, and text typed meanwhile is
  carried along as a steering message. No in-flight call is interrupted and
  the model does not notice the pause; the per-session switch is off by
  default.

- **`ds-harness-remote`** — community P2P remote access: continue the running
  Harness and its workspaces from another PC, a phone, or the web over a
  low-latency, end-to-end encrypted connection (no public listener or router
  port forwarding), plus a host-side `remote_*` tool group for listing hosts
  and workspaces and driving Harness sessions from an Agent. Installs from
  npm and mounts through its own bundle patch (`ds-harness-remote` entry;
  `ds-harness-remote-tui` only for dsh-tui profiles); independent of the
  in-repo `dsh-remote` multi-backend mode.

![dsh-gui with the plugin features expanded](docs/dsh-gui/images/dsh-gui-features.png)

## Requirements

- Windows 10/11 with the **WebView2 Evergreen runtime** (ships with most modern
  Windows / Edge installs).
- **Node.js** `^22.19 || >=24.2` and **npm** on `PATH` (used by the build tooling
  and by the shell to launch `bin.js`). The `>=24.2` floor is real: the harness
  CLI entry is gated on `import.meta.main`, which Node only provides from
  22.18.0 / 24.2.0 on — on 24.0–24.1 `bin.js` exits 0 without starting and the
  shell reports `harness exited before becoming ready (status exit status: 0)`.
- **Rust** toolchain (`rustc`/`cargo`) for the entry exe.

Everything fetched at build time (npm packages, the pnpm store, cargo crates)
lands inside the runtime root or the standard local caches — no global install of
the harness is ever performed.

The tooling is a single cross-platform Node CLI (`scripts/dsh-gui.mjs`) exposed
through npm scripts, so the same commands work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
(WSL).

## Layout

The installation spans two roots. The **repository root** is the git checkout; the
**runtime root** is its parent directory and holds the DSH home, the toolchain and
the entry binary. `DSH_GUI_ROOT` and `DSH_GUI_RUNTIME_ROOT` override them, and a
single-directory checkout keeps working because both roots then resolve to the
same directory (see [docs/dsh-gui/nested-clone-layout.md](docs/dsh-gui/nested-clone-layout.md)).
Keeping the runtime out of the workspace matters on Windows: the sandbox labels
the workspace tree with a Low integrity label, and a process started from an
executable inside that tree inherits it (see
[docs/dsh-gui/windows-acl-low-integrity-label.md](docs/dsh-gui/windows-acl-low-integrity-label.md)).

```
<runtime-root>/
├─ .dsh/                    # (runtime) harness home: profiles/plugins/sessions
├─ .harness/                # npm-runtime install of @deepseek-ai/dsh
├─ .toolchain/ .pnpm-store/ # pinned pnpm and the shared package cache
├─ dsh-gui.exe              # the Tauri shell entry binary (`dsh-gui` elsewhere)
└─ dsh-gui/                 # the git checkout — also the DSH workspace
   ├─ .staging/             # upgrade validation worktree (.staging/dsh-gui on the
   │                        #   staging/verify branch) and its runtime root
   ├─ harness.json          # selects the dsh runtime (npm registry or source build)
   ├─ deepseek-harness/     # git submodule: the pinned harness checkout — version
   │                        #   source, built in place only in `source` mode
   ├─ package.json          # npm scripts: setup / build / install:plugins / start / ...
   ├─ src-tauri/            # the Tauri shell (Rust); cargo output at target/<profile>/
   │  ├─ ui/                # the frameless shell page: title bar (connection tabs,
   │  │                     #   + button, hamburger menu, window controls), the
   │  │                     #   new-connection dialog, and the About dialog
   │  └─ whale-icon/        # git submodule: the DeepSeek Harness whale-girl icon pack
   │                        #   (DeepSeekHarness-WhaleGirl.ico is the app icon)
   ├─ scripts/
   │  └─ dsh-gui.mjs        # the cross-platform CLI behind every npm script
   ├─ presets/              # agent preset sources: each presets/<id>/ directory owns
   │                        #   its install.mjs; the build installs every preset as an
   │                        #   @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset row (see presets/README.md)
   ├─ plugins/              # plugin wrappers, preset-style: each plugins/<id>/ owns
   │                        #   an install.mjs; npm wrappers pin exact registry
   │                        #   versions in the script, in-tree wrappers also own
   │                        #   their package dir (see plugins/README.md)
   └─ global_template.agents/  # versioned agent-config template: the always-loaded
                            #   docs and the user-level skills (the `review` skill
                            #   among them); the build ships AGENTS.global_template.md
                            #   to .dsh/AGENTS.md and fills missing files of this tree
                            #   into <runtime-root>/.dsh/ (docs/, skills/), never
                            #   overwriting an existing one — except the third-party
                            #   docs/awesome-design-md submodule, whose design-md/
                            #   content replaces .dsh/docs/awesome-design-md/ on
                            #   every build (read-only reference, no repo metadata)
```

## npm scripts

Every command below is a `package.json` entry that forwards to the
cross-platform Node CLIs — `scripts/dsh-gui.mjs` for the main lifecycle, while
`scripts/staging.mjs` and `scripts/harness.mjs` own their own commands. The
detailed sections marked in the table are expanded further down.

| npm script | Command | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npm run setup` / `npm run build` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs setup` / `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs build` | one-shot build: toolchain, harness runtime, entry exe, plugins, presets, global agent template (see [Build (one shot)](#build-one-shot)) |
| `npm run build:exe` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs build --skip-harness` | build the entry exe only, skipping the harness runtime step |
| `npm run build:webui` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs build --skip-exe` | harness runtime + plugin/preset installs only, skipping cargo |
| `npm run build:desktop` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs build-desktop` | build the Electron desktop app into `<runtime-root>/desktop`, compile the shim, install plugins into the desktop profile (see [docs/dsh-gui/desktop-app.md](docs/dsh-gui/desktop-app.md)) |
| `npm run build:all` | `npm run build && npm run build:desktop` | both targets in one command: the Tauri shell build, then the desktop build; stops at the first failing step |
| `npm run build:desktop-plugins` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs build-desktop --plugins-only` | reinstall the plugin set into the desktop profile only, reusing the landed `<runtime-root>/desktop` app (see [docs/dsh-gui/desktop-app.md](docs/dsh-gui/desktop-app.md)) |
| `npm run rebuild` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs rebuild` | full build with every skip disabled: runtime reinstalled, every plugin installed again (see [Build (one shot)](#build-one-shot)) |
| `npm run install:plugins` / `npm run plugins` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs install` | run every plugin install script under `plugins/` (see [Adding plugins at runtime](#adding-plugins-at-runtime)) |
| `npm run test:scripts` | `node --test scripts/plugin-install.test.mjs` | unit tests for the plugin-install fast path and reinstall switches |
| `npm run staging` | `node scripts/staging.mjs` | staging-workspace workflow: `ensure`, `sync [--rebase]`, `status`, `clean --yes [--branch]` (see [Validating an upgrade in the staging worktree](#validating-an-upgrade-in-the-staging-worktree)) |
| `npm run harness` | `node scripts/harness.mjs` | foreground harness backend, no shell window or browser (see [Run](#run)) |
| `npm start` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs run` | detached desktop shell (see [Run](#run)) |
| `npm run shortcut` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs shortcut` | Windows desktop shortcut (see [System shortcut (Windows)](#system-shortcut-windows)) |

## Build (one shot)

```powershell
npm run setup
```

This is idempotent and writes only under the runtime root:

- Bootstraps **pnpm 11.7.0** into `.toolchain/` (the exact version the harness
  pins), so a system pnpm is not required.
- Brings the dsh runtime selected by `harness.json` up to date (contract and
  limits: [docs/dsh-gui/harness-runtime.md](docs/dsh-gui/harness-runtime.md)):
  - `npm` (the checked-in runtime): installs `@deepseek-ai/dsh@<version>` into
    `<runtime-root>/.harness/` from the registry, where `<version>` is read from the
    submodule's `apps/cli/package.json`. Nothing under `deepseek-harness/` is
    compiled.
  - `source`: runs `pnpm install --store-dir <runtime-root>/.pnpm-store --frozen-lockfile` and
    `pnpm run build` (host lib + web `dist/`) inside `deepseek-harness/`.
- Whichever runtime is selected, the package cache lives at
  `<runtime-root>/.pnpm-store/` — not in a global store.
- Compiles the entry exe with `cargo build --release` (**release by default**)
  and copies it to the runtime root (`dsh-gui.exe` on Windows, `dsh-gui`
  elsewhere).
- Runs every plugin install script under `plugins/` — each
  `plugins/<id>/install.mjs` installs and mounts its plugin packages into the
  web profile: npm wrappers add their exact-pinned registry packages through
  `installNpmPlugin`, and in-tree wrappers build and link their own package
  directory (see [Adding plugins](#adding-plugins-at-runtime)). A plugin the
  profile already holds at its exact pinned version — installed, mounted, with
  its bundle row in `dsh.profile.bundles` — is **skipped**: `dsh plugin add`
  would re-resolve the whole profile graph for nothing. `link:` installs skip
  only that dependency write; the package itself is still built.
- Runs every agent-preset install script under `presets/` — since harness
  `dsh-v0.1.7-rc.2` each `presets/<id>/` directory lands as an
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` declaration row in the profile patch and
  appears on the preset roster (see `presets/README.md` for the pattern; the
  retired `.dsh/.agent-presets/` directory is no longer discovered).
- Fills in the **global agent template** — `AGENTS.global_template.md` is
  deployed to `<runtime-root>/.dsh/AGENTS.md` (the harness home's user-global
  instruction file), and the `global_template.agents/` tree is merged into
  `<runtime-root>/.dsh/` itself (`docs/`, `skills/`), so its always-loaded docs
  and user-level skills (the `review` skill among them) reach every session
  from the harness home — no `DSH_AGENTS_HOME` override is needed. Only missing
  files are written: an already-installed doc or skill is never overwritten, so
  your edits to the installed copy survive every build. An installation from the
  retired layout is migrated in the same step: a `<runtime-root>/.dsh/.agents/`
  tree is merged up into `.dsh/` (and removed once every file lives there), and
  `.agents/` path references in an already-installed `AGENTS.md` are rewritten
  to the home-relative paths — the only in-place edit, because those references
  point at a directory that no longer exists.

The result is the entry binary at the runtime root (cargo keeps its own
output at `src-tauri\target\release\` or `target\debug\`).

Flags (pass after `--`): `--debug` for a `cargo build` debug build,
`--skip-harness` to skip the dsh runtime install/build, `--skip-exe` to skip
cargo entirely (runtime/plugins only — useful on Linux without Tauri system
deps), `--force-harness` to reinstall or rebuild the runtime even when it is
current (the same as `DSH_HARNESS_REBUILD=1`), and `--rebuild` to disable every
skip at once (`--force-harness` plus reinstalling every plugin; the plugin
scripts see `DSH_PLUGIN_REBUILD=1`).
Example: `npm run build -- --debug`.

`npm run rebuild` is the same as `npm run build -- --rebuild`: use it after
changing plugin sources, masks, or profile state by hand, or when a plugin needs
to be installed again even though its pinned version is already in the profile.
The global agent template is still never overwritten — that rule is about your
edits, not about being current.

> Packaging/installer generation is intentionally disabled (`bundle.active:
> false` in `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`). The app always runs from this
> installation, which is what lets you `git pull` the submodule or add plugins and
> pick them up on the next launch.

## Run

```powershell
npm start
# or double-click the entry binary at the runtime root
```

`npm start` launches the entry exe detached: the terminal returns immediately
and closing it never kills dsh-gui (or its harness child). The launcher and
entry exe both pin `DSH_HOME` to the runtime root's `.dsh`. Startup refuses an
already occupied loopback port and, on Windows, also verifies that the listener
belongs to the Node child it just spawne

# dsh-remote

多后端远程连接插件（DeepSeek Harness GUI）。标题栏标签页、汉堡菜单、新建连接页、
本地后端启动 + 远端 SSH 启动 dsh 与安全隧道转发（VSCode Remote SSH 风格，不部署代码）、
以及 Docker 连接（`docker exec` 启动容器内 dsh 并桥接回环端口，**无需端口映射**）。非侵入、自托管。

详见 [docs/README.md](docs/README.md)。

# dsh-gui

A thin desktop shell for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
web UI. It is **not** a repackaged harness — it runs the dsh CLI that
`harness.json` selects (the `@deepseek-ai/dsh` registry package in the default
`npm` runtime, or the built `deepseek-harness` git submodule in `source`),
hosts the web server itself, and shows the full harness UI in a single webview
window. Nothing else is drawn: just the OS title bar and border.

## What it does

On launch the entry exe:

1. Opens one **frameless** webview window immediately and shows a loading page
   inside it. A harness cold start takes ~10 s (it is CPU-bound inside the
   harness), so the window never waits for it.
2. Spawns the dsh CLI selected by `harness.json` — that runtime's `bin.js` — with
   `web --port <port> --no-open`, and pins `DSH_HOME` to `./.dsh` inside this
   repository.
3. Waits until the harness answers `GET /` with `200` on `127.0.0.1:<port>`,
   then hands the tokenized URL to the shell page, which hosts the harness UI
   in one **child webview per connection tab**. A harness that cannot be
   spawned or never becomes ready is reported on the loading page (the window
   stays open) instead of behind a message box. On exit dsh-gui tears the
   harness process tree down; the harness runs inside a kill-on-close Windows
   job object, so the kernel enforces that teardown even when dsh-gui itself is
   killed (Task Manager, closing the terminal it was launched from).

The `ui/` page is a thin shell only: a drag-anywhere title bar with
**connection tabs** (VSCode-style, one per connected DSH backend), a **＋**
new-connection button, and on their inner side a hamburger (☰) menu — the
standard minimize / maximize / close controls come after it, and the hamburger
menu carries the tab list plus **新建连接** / **关闭当前连接** and the existing
**关于** / **退出** entries. The new-connection dialog supports a local backend
(probe the port, or start the built-in harness on it), a remote backend
(VSCode Remote SSH style: load the frontend, or SSH-deploy it to another host,
reaching it over an SSH local port forward), and a Docker backend (start dsh
inside a running container via `docker exec` and bridge its loopback port with
a `docker exec -i` stdio tunnel — no port mapping required). The connection
chrome lives in the
native title bar — the embedded harness page renders none of it. The About
dialog shows the version (exact git tag, else the commit short hash), license,
and GitHub link for dsh-gui, the deepseek-harness submodule, the whale-girl
app-icon submodule, and every plugin package under `plugins/`. The harness UI
itself goes on talking to its self-hosted server over plain HTTP exactly like a
browser.

## Screenshot

![dsh-gui screenshot](docs/dsh-gui/images/dsh-gui-screenshot.png)

## Features

### GUI shell

- **Frameless single-window shell** — a drag-anywhere custom title bar with
  native minimize / maximize / close controls; the title bar colors follow the
  light/dark theme reported by the embedded harness page.
- **Window first, loading page while the harness boots** — the window appears
  as soon as the process starts (WebView2 initialization only) and shows a
  loading card with the elapsed wait; the tab webview replaces it the moment
  the harness answers. Harness failures appear on that card, and the window
  keeps working (drag, minimize, close) throughout.
- **Native Windows 11 title-bar interactions** — hovering maximize shows the
  OS Snap Layouts flyout, double-clicking the title bar toggles
  maximize/restore, double-clicking the top border vertically fills/restores
  the window (including drag-to-restore), and the top-left app icon opens the
  window-control menu.
- **VSCode-style connection tabs** — one tab per connected DSH backend, with
  close buttons and persisted tab/active state; closing the last tab reopens
  the new-connection dialog.
- **New connection (`＋`)** — local backend (probe the port, or start the
  built-in harness on it), remote backend (load the frontend, or SSH-deploy
  it to another host and reach it through a loopback-only SSH local port
  forward), and Docker backend (start dsh in a running container via
  `docker exec -d`, then bridge its loopback port with a `docker exec -i`
  stdio tunnel — the container needs no `-p` port mapping; the container-side
  user, working directory and environment-variable list are configurable).
- **Hamburger menu (`☰`)** — tab list, `新建连接` / `关闭当前连接`, `检查更新`,
  `关于` / `退出`.
- **About dialog** — version (git tag or commit short hash), license, and
  GitHub link for dsh-gui, the harness, the icon submodule, and every plugin.
  A plain click copies the URL; **Ctrl+click** opens it in the system default
  browser.
- **Update dialog** — checks two kinds of rows and lets you pick which updates
  to run. **git rows** are this checkout and its non-`plugins/` submodules;
  each is compared against its remote default branch and offers a target
  (latest commit / latest tag). The top-level row's **更新** performs the
  git-layer update in the dialog (root reset plus recursive submodule sync)
  and then asks for `npm run build` and a restart; selected submodule rows go
  through a detached launcher that exits the app, runs the updates in a
  console window, rebuilds, and restarts the shell. **npm plugin rows** are
  the npm packages pinned by the `plugins/**/*.mjs` install scripts
  (`installNpmPlugin` with an exact `name@version` literal); each row
  compares that pin with the registry's latest version, and its **更新**
  button rewrites the pin in the install script and re-runs that wrapper in
  place — the app keeps running and the reinstalled plugin takes effect after
  a restart, with no rebuild needed. npm plugin rows have no tag/commit
  target and no **更新日志** button (a GitHub release cannot be mapped
  reliably onto an npm version). A batch that mixes both kinds updates the
  npm rows in place first, then restarts through the detached git flow, and a
  failed npm row never blocks the git rows, while a batch made up only of npm
  plugin rows finishes in place without exiting the app. Each row's module
  name links to that repository's **Releases list** page
  (`https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases`) whenever its origin is a
  GitHub repository — resolved locally for git rows, so that link is there
  from the first paint, and from the package's registry manifest
  `repository` for npm plugin rows, so it appears once the registry check
  lands; a non-GitHub or missing remote leaves the name as plain text. As
  with the changelog title, the row name is not selectable, so a plain click
  opens the system default browser. The dialog recommends AI-sync updates:
  each updatable submodule or npm plugin row and the bottom bar offer an
  **AI 更新** button that returns to the project home screen, selects the
  dsh-gui directory there, selects the 「创造模式」(cordis) preset, and
  prefills a prompt that asks the agent to sync the submodule(s) to the chosen
  target — for an npm plugin row, to raise the exact `packageSpec` in its
  install script and reinstall the package — and verify the result in the
  `.staging/dsh-gui` validation worktree — a git
  worktree of this checkout on the `staging/verify` branch whose runtime root
  is `<repository root>/.staging`, so the whole copy lives inside the session
  workspace — the worktree's WebUI must actually load, adaptation commits go
  straight onto `staging/verify` without approval, a harness update
  additionally needs a computer-use check that the GUI starts and runs, and
  phase two merges that branch back into this checkout only after you approve
  the verification report (the bottom button lists every updatable module with
  its combo choice, and every npm plugin row with its install script and
  target version; the preset can still be changed before sending). Each
  behind git row also has an **更新日志** button:
  for a tag target it shows the official GitHub Release notes for **every**
  release the update brings in — all tags between the current checkout and the
  update target, newest first, so a checkout several releases behind sees the
  whole span instead of just the target tag's notes — when the remote is a
  GitHub repository and releases exist, otherwise it asks the dsh AI to
  summarize the commits between the current checkout and the update target —
  through the running harness's raw-LLM route (the dsh-ai-update plugin,
  default model from the Models page), which creates no session, so the run
  never appears in the DSH session list; when that route is unavailable the
  shell retries it once and then falls back to the one-shot headless mode
  (`dsh --profile headless`), whose session store is redirected to a temp
  directory — neither path persists a session. The markdown result renders
  in a scrollable, selectable dialog whose copy button copies the raw source
  text; the provenance line and any failure message (for example a
  GitHub-Release fetch error) are selectable as well, so a problem can be
  copied out verbatim into a report. When the changelog came from a real
  GitHub release, the module name in the dialog title becomes a link to the
  repository's **Releases list** page (`https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases`,
  never a per-tag `/releases/tag/…` subpage); the title line is not selectable,
  so a plain click there opens the system default browser. **Ctrl+click** on a
  link in the body opens the URL in the system default browser (a plain click
  stays a text-selection gesture, since a webview link cannot spawn a popup on
  its own).

### Plugins

- **`dsh-remote`** — multi-backend remote mode: the connection tabs,
  new-connection dialog, local backend start, and VSCode Remote SSH-style
  deploy/tunnel described above (see `plugins/remote/dsh-remote/docs/`).
- **`dsh-sidebar-qa`** — select conversation text → right-panel follow-up
  question in a dedicated same-workspace session (`❓追问·<主题>`), without
  interrupting the main conversation; thin consumer of `dsh-better-sidebar`
  (see `plugins/better-sidebar/`; installed by the
  better-sidebar wrapper, after dsh-better-sidebar).
- **`dsh-better-sidebar`** — service-first sidebar workbench (right sidebar
  + bottom panel): per-session explorer, CodeMirror editor + file viewers
  (image/PDF/Markdown/HTML/code), real terminal (xterm.js + node-pty with
  reconnect replay; optional `terminal_*` model tools, off by default), Git
  panel, embedded browser, and background-job page (see
  `plugins/better-sidebar/`).
- **`dsh-ai-update`** — browser-half bridge behind the update dialog's AI
  update buttons: receives the shell's `dsh-gui:ai-update` message, returns
  to the new-session home, selects the dsh-gui workspace, auto-selects the
  「创造模式」(cordis) preset for the blank session (a refusal fails the
  request instead of silently using the default), and prefills the composer
  with the update prompt — never creating a session directly (see
  `plugins/ai-update/dsh-ai-update/docs/`).
- **`dsh-deep-whale`** — whale-girl skin series; currently ships the
  hot-pluggable `maid-atelier` skin (light/dark palace backgrounds, navy lace
  UI overlay, Q-version sidebar, embedded assets).
- **`dsh-skill-mcp-center`** — Skill & MCP management center: a "Skill & MCP"
  settings section for browsing, enabling and deleting skills and for adding,
  editing, enabling and removing MCP servers (hot-applied without restart),
  plus an MCP live-status sidebar tab when `dsh-better-sidebar` is installed.
- **`dsh-pause`** — a pause point right before the agent's next model request
  in a tool round: while paused the composer stays usable, a bare Enter in the
  main input (or the pause control) releases it, and text typed meanwhile is
  carried along as a steering message. No in-flight call is interrupted and
  the model does not notice the pause; the per-session switch is off by
  default.

- **`ds-harness-remote`** — community P2P remote access: continue the running
  Harness and its workspaces from another PC, a phone, or the web over a
  low-latency, end-to-end encrypted connection (no public listener or router
  port forwarding), plus a host-side `remote_*` tool group for listing hosts
  and workspaces and driving Harness sessions from an Agent. Installs from
  npm and mounts through its own bundle patch (`ds-harness-remote` entry;
  `ds-harness-remote-tui` only for dsh-tui profiles); independent of the
  in-repo `dsh-remote` multi-backend mode.

![dsh-gui with the plugin features expanded](docs/dsh-gui/images/dsh-gui-features.png)

## Requirements

- Windows 10/11 with the **WebView2 Evergreen runtime** (ships with most modern
  Windows / Edge installs).
- **Node.js** `^22.19 || >=24.2` and **npm** on `PATH` (used by the build tooling
  and by the shell to launch `bin.js`). The `>=24.2` floor is real: the harness
  CLI entry is gated on `import.meta.main`, which Node only provides from
  22.18.0 / 24.2.0 on — on 24.0–24.1 `bin.js` exits 0 without starting and the
  shell reports `harness exited before becoming ready (status exit status: 0)`.
- **Rust** toolchain (`rustc`/`cargo`) for the entry exe.

Everything fetched at build time (npm packages, the pnpm store, cargo crates)
lands inside the runtime root or the standard local caches — no global install of
the harness is ever performed.

The tooling is a single cross-platform Node CLI (`scripts/dsh-gui.mjs`) exposed
through npm scripts, so the same commands work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
(WSL).

## Layout

The installation spans two roots. The **repository root** is the git checkout; the
**runtime root** is its parent directory and holds the DSH home, the toolchain and
the entry binary. `DSH_GUI_ROOT` and `DSH_GUI_RUNTIME_ROOT` override them, and a
single-directory checkout keeps working because both roots then resolve to the
same directory (see [docs/dsh-gui/nested-clone-layout.md](docs/dsh-gui/nested-clone-layout.md)).
Keeping the runtime out of the workspace matters on Windows: the sandbox labels
the workspace tree with a Low integrity label, and a process started from an
executable inside that tree inherits it (see
[docs/dsh-gui/windows-acl-low-integrity-label.md](docs/dsh-gui/windows-acl-low-integrity-label.md)).

```
<runtime-root>/
├─ .dsh/                    # (runtime) harness home: profiles/plugins/sessions
├─ .harness/                # npm-runtime install of @deepseek-ai/dsh
├─ .toolchain/ .pnpm-store/ # pinned pnpm and the shared package cache
├─ dsh-gui.exe              # the Tauri shell entry binary (`dsh-gui` elsewhere)
└─ dsh-gui/                 # the git checkout — also the DSH workspace
   ├─ .staging/             # upgrade validation worktree (.staging/dsh-gui on the
   │                        #   staging/verify branch) and its runtime root
   ├─ harness.json          # selects the dsh runtime (npm registry or source build)
   ├─ deepseek-harness/     # git submodule: the pinned harness checkout — version
   │                        #   source, built in place only in `source` mode
   ├─ package.json          # npm scripts: setup / build / install:plugins / start / ...
   ├─ src-tauri/            # the Tauri shell (Rust); cargo output at target/<profile>/
   │  ├─ ui/                # the frameless shell page: title bar (connection tabs,
   │  │                     #   + button, hamburger menu, window controls), the
   │  │                     #   new-connection dialog, and the About dialog
   │  └─ whale-icon/        # git submodule: the DeepSeek Harness whale-girl icon pack
   │                        #   (DeepSeekHarness-WhaleGirl.ico is the app icon)
   ├─ scripts/
   │  └─ dsh-gui.mjs        # the cross-platform CLI behind every npm script
   ├─ presets/              # agent preset sources: each presets/<id>/ directory owns
   │                        #   its install.mjs; the build installs every preset as an
   │                        #   @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset row (see presets/README.md)
   ├─ plugins/              # plugin wrappers, preset-style: each plugins/<id>/ owns
   │                        #   an install.mjs; npm wrappers pin exact registry
   │                        #   versions in the script, in-tree wrappers also own
   │                        #   their package dir (see plugins/README.md)
   └─ global_template.agents/  # versioned agent-config template: the always-loaded
                            #   docs and the user-level skills (the `review` skill
                            #   among them); the build ships AGENTS.global_template.md
                            #   to .dsh/AGENTS.md and fills missing files of this tree
                            #   into <runtime-root>/.dsh/ (docs/, skills/), never
                            #   overwriting an existing one — except the third-party
                            #   docs/awesome-design-md submodule, whose design-md/
                            #   content replaces .dsh/docs/awesome-design-md/ on
                            #   every build (read-only reference, no repo metadata)
```

## npm scripts

Every command below is a `package.json` entry that forwards to the
cross-platform Node CLIs — `scripts/dsh-gui.mjs` for the main lifecycle, while
`scripts/staging.mjs` and `scripts/harness.mjs` own their own commands. The
detailed sections marked in the table are expanded further down.

| npm script | Command | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npm run setup` / `npm run build` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs setup` / `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs build` | one-shot build: toolchain, harness runtime, entry exe, plugins, presets, global agent template (see [Build (one shot)](#build-one-shot)) |
| `npm run build:exe` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs build --skip-harness` | build the entry exe only, skipping the harness runtime step |
| `npm run build:webui` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs build --skip-exe` | harness runtime + plugin/preset installs only, skipping cargo |
| `npm run build:desktop` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs build-desktop` | build the Electron desktop app into `<runtime-root>/desktop`, compile the shim, install plugins into the desktop profile (see [docs/dsh-gui/desktop-app.md](docs/dsh-gui/desktop-app.md)) |
| `npm run build:all` | `npm run build && npm run build:desktop` | both targets in one command: the Tauri shell build, then the desktop build; stops at the first failing step |
| `npm run build:desktop-plugins` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs build-desktop --plugins-only` | reinstall the plugin set into the desktop profile only, reusing the landed `<runtime-root>/desktop` app (see [docs/dsh-gui/desktop-app.md](docs/dsh-gui/desktop-app.md)) |
| `npm run rebuild` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs rebuild` | full build with every skip disabled: runtime reinstalled, every plugin installed again (see [Build (one shot)](#build-one-shot)) |
| `npm run install:plugins` / `npm run plugins` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs install` | run every plugin install script under `plugins/` (see [Adding plugins at runtime](#adding-plugins-at-runtime)) |
| `npm run test:scripts` | `node --test scripts/plugin-install.test.mjs` | unit tests for the plugin-install fast path and reinstall switches |
| `npm run staging` | `node scripts/staging.mjs` | staging-workspace workflow: `ensure`, `sync [--rebase]`, `status`, `clean --yes [--branch]` (see [Validating an upgrade in the staging worktree](#validating-an-upgrade-in-the-staging-worktree)) |
| `npm run harness` | `node scripts/harness.mjs` | foreground harness backend, no shell window or browser (see [Run](#run)) |
| `npm start` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs run` | detached desktop shell (see [Run](#run)) |
| `npm run shortcut` | `node scripts/dsh-gui.mjs shortcut` | Windows desktop shortcut (see [System shortcut (Windows)](#system-shortcut-windows)) |

## Build (one shot)

```powershell
npm run setup
```

This is idempotent and writes only under the runtime root:

- Bootstraps **pnpm 11.7.0** into `.toolchain/` (the exact version the harness
  pins), so a system pnpm is not required.
- Brings the dsh runtime selected by `harness.json` up to date (contract and
  limits: [docs/dsh-gui/harness-runtime.md](docs/dsh-gui/harness-runtime.md)):
  - `npm` (the checked-in runtime): installs `@deepseek-ai/dsh@<version>` into
    `<runtime-root>/.harness/` from the registry, where `<version>` is read from the
    submodule's `apps/cli/package.json`. Nothing under `deepseek-harness/` is
    compiled.
  - `source`: runs `pnpm install --store-dir <runtime-root>/.pnpm-store --frozen-lockfile` and
    `pnpm run build` (host lib + web `dist/`) inside `deepseek-harness/`.
- Whichever runtime is selected, the package cache lives at
  `<runtime-root>/.pnpm-store/` — not in a global store.
- Compiles the entry exe with `cargo build --release` (**release by default**)
  and copies it to the runtime root (`dsh-gui.exe` on Windows, `dsh-gui`
  elsewhere).
- Runs every plugin install script under `plugins/` — each
  `plugins/<id>/install.mjs` installs and mounts its plugin packages into the
  web profile: npm wrappers add their exact-pinned registry packages through
  `installNpmPlugin`, and in-tree wrappers build and link their own package
  directory (see [Adding plugins](#adding-plugins-at-runtime)). A plugin the
  profile already holds at its exact pinned version — installed, mounted, with
  its bundle row in `dsh.profile.bundles` — is **skipped**: `dsh plugin add`
  would re-resolve the whole profile graph for nothing. `link:` installs skip
  only that dependency write; the package itself is still built.
- Runs every agent-preset install script under `presets/` — since harness
  `dsh-v0.1.7-rc.2` each `presets/<id>/` directory lands as an
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` declaration row in the profile patch and
  appears on the preset roster (see `presets/README.md` for the pattern; the
  retired `.dsh/.agent-presets/` directory is no longer discovered).
- Fills in the **global agent template** — `AGENTS.global_template.md` is
  deployed to `<runtime-root>/.dsh/AGENTS.md` (the harness home's user-global
  instruction file), and the `global_template.agents/` tree is merged into
  `<runtime-root>/.dsh/` itself (`docs/`, `skills/`), so its always-loaded docs
  and user-level skills (the `review` skill among them) reach every session
  from the harness home — no `DSH_AGENTS_HOME` override is needed. Only missing
  files are written: an already-installed doc or skill is never overwritten, so
  your edits to the installed copy survive every build. An installation from the
  retired layout is migrated in the same step: a `<runtime-root>/.dsh/.agents/`
  tree is merged up into `.dsh/` (and removed once every file lives there), and
  `.agents/` path references in an already-installed `AGENTS.md` are rewritten
  to the home-relative paths — the only in-place edit, because those references
  point at a directory that no longer exists.

The result is the entry binary at the runtime root (cargo keeps its own
output at `src-tauri\target\release\` or `target\debug\`).

Flags (pass after `--`): `--debug` for a `cargo build` debug build,
`--skip-harness` to skip the dsh runtime install/build, `--skip-exe` to skip
cargo entirely (runtime/plugins only — useful on Linux without Tauri system
deps), `--force-harness` to reinstall or rebuild the runtime even when it is
current (the same as `DSH_HARNESS_REBUILD=1`), and `--rebuild` to disable every
skip at once (`--force-harness` plus reinstalling every plugin; the plugin
scripts see `DSH_PLUGIN_REBUILD=1`).
Example: `npm run build -- --debug`.

`npm run rebuild` is the same as `npm run build -- --rebuild`: use it after
changing plugin sources, masks, or profile state by hand, or when a plugin needs
to be installed again even though its pinned version is already in the profile.
The global agent template is still never overwritten — that rule is about your
edits, not about being current.

> Packaging/installer generation is intentionally disabled (`bundle.active:
> false` in `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`). The app always runs from this
> installation, which is what lets you `git pull` the submodule or add plugins and
> pick them up on the next launch.

## Run

```powershell
npm start
# or double-click the entry binary at the runtime root
```

`npm start` launches the entry exe detached: the terminal returns immediately
and closing it never kills dsh-gui (or its harness child). The launcher and
entry exe both pin `DSH_HOME` to the runtime root's `.dsh`. Startup refuses an
already occupied loopback port and, on Windows, also verifies that the listener
belongs to the Node child it just spawned, so an unrelated `dsh web` process
can never be mistaken for this installation's backend.

To run only that same harness backend in the foreground, without starting the
Tauri shell or opening a browser, use:

```powershell
npm run harness
```

It uses the same `web --port <port> --no-open` arguments, starts the resolved
runtime's CLI from that runtime's working directory (`.harness/` in `npm` mode,
`deepseek-harness/` in `source` mode), and pins `DSH_HOME` to the runtime root's
`.dsh` (the build deploys the global agent template — `AGENTS.global_template.md`
-> `.dsh/AGENTS.md` and the `global_template.agents/` tree -> `.dsh/` — which
the harness reads from the harness home itself, so no `DSH_AGENTS_HOME` override
is set). Its
output stays in the terminal; press Ctrl+C to stop it.

Both launch paths honor `$env:DSH_GUI_PORT` (default `3080`). Under `npm start`,
harness output is logged to `.dsh\gui\harness.log`; dsh-gui's own status lines
go to `.dsh\gui\gui.log`, and startup failures also pop a message box (a GUI app
has no console to print to).

## System shortcut (Windows)

```powershell
npm run shortcut                          # desktop shortcut
npm run shortcut -- "D:\x.lnk"            # arbitrary location
```

## App icon

The app icon comes from the `src-tauri/whale-icon` submodule
([fornarwhal/deepseek-whale-girl-icon](https://github.com/fornarwhal/deepseek-whale-girl-icon),
CC BY-NC-SA 4.0): `DeepSeekHarness-WhaleGirl.ico` (16–256 px, transparent).
`src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` points `bundle.icon` at it, so it is embedded as the
Windows exe resource and used as the window/taskbar icon. The shell UI itself
keeps no icon copy — swap the submodule to change the icon, then rebuild:

```powershell
git submodule update --remote src-tauri/whale-icon
npm run build
```

## Updating the harness submodule

```powershell
git submodule update --remote deepseek-harness
npm run build             # install the submodule's version, then rebuild exe + plugins
```

The submodule stays the pinned version source: in the default `npm` runtime the
build installs `@deepseek-ai/dsh` at the version the submodule's
`apps/cli/package.json` records, and in `source` it compiles the checkout in
place — see [docs/dsh-gui/harness-runtime.md](docs/dsh-gui/harness-runtime.md).

## Validating an upgrade in the staging worktree

`.staging/dsh-gui` is a git worktree of this checkout on the dedicated
`staging/verify` branch, submodules included; `<repository root>/.staging/` is
that worktree's runtime root and carries its own `DSH_HOME`, toolchain, pnpm
store, harness install, and build output, so the whole copy lives inside the
session workspace. Move an upgrade through the worktree first, so a broken
harness or plugin revision never reaches the installation this checkout
serves:

```powershell
npm run staging -- ensure        # first time only: create the worktree
npm run staging -- sync          # move the branch onto this checkout's revision
cd .staging\dsh-gui              # from the repository root
$env:DSH_HOME = 'E:\Git\dsh-gui-home\dsh-gui\.staging\.dsh'   # required: the worktree's own DSH home
npm run build -- --skip-exe      # dsh runtime install/build -> plugin installs -> presets
```

`npm run staging -- sync` resets the branch onto this checkout's HEAD while the
branch holds no unmerged commits, and with `--rebase` rebases those commits on
top otherwise. `npm run staging -- status` reports both revisions, submodule
drift, and how far the worktree's build has come; `npm run staging -- clean
--yes` removes the worktree and its runtime directories and keeps the
`staging/verify` branch (add `--branch` to delete it). Adaptation commits go
straight onto `staging/verify` without approval; merging the branch back into
this checkout is a separate, approved step.
The full upgrade workflow is the `dsh-gui-update` skill; the workspace itself is
documented in
[docs/dsh-gui/upgrade-staging-workspace.md](docs/dsh-gui/upgrade-staging-workspace.md).

## Adding plugins at runtime

Plugins are installed into the `web` profile under the runtime root's `DSH_HOME`
(`.dsh/`). The layout mirrors `presets/`: each `plugins/<id>/` wrapper owns an
`install.mjs`. A wrapper either adds published npm packages at exact pinned
versions, with no package source in this repository, or owns its package in a
second-level directory and builds it in place:

```
plugins/<id>/install.mjs     # npm wrapper: installs the exact-pinned npm package(s)
                             # in-tree wrapper: builds, links and mounts its package
plugins/<id>/<package>/      # the in-tree package (absent for npm wrappers)
```

A minimal npm wrapper delegates the shared pipeline and pins its package:

```js
import { installNpmPlugin } from '../../scripts/plugin-install.mjs'

installNpmPlugin({
  id: 'my-plugin',
  packageSpec: 'dsh-my-plugin@1.2.3',
})
```

owns:

# dsh-balance

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) web
plugin that shows your **real DeepSeek account balance** and the **current
peak/off-peak pricing window** in a window-anchored card, and estimates the
**cost of every conversation and workspace** from the session log.

![Balance card and detail panel](screenshot.png)

## Features

- **Balance card** — fixed to the bottom-right of the window, independent of the
  composer: live account balance, current window (`谷价` / `高峰`), remaining
  time, and the next switch in your local timezone. It stays at the window
  bottom even on the no-conversation/hero screen, and moves above the composer
  or the per-conversation status row when they reach that corner, so it never
  covers other readings.
- **Native detail panel** — click the card to open a menu-style panel above it:
  account balance / topped-up / granted, next switch in local and Beijing time,
  current local/Beijing time, peak hours, price-table source and update time,
  ledger path, and a refresh button. The granted row is always shown (`0` when
  empty) and links to the Billing page for its expiry while some granted credit
  remains. Closes on outside click or `Esc`.
- **Cost estimates** — per-conversation and per-workspace estimates in the
  sidebar, summed from a persistent ledger that records each usage event once.
- **Dynamic pricing** — CNY and USD price tables and the peak-hour windows are
  fetched from the official DeepSeek pricing pages; the Chinese holiday calendar
  comes from `api.apihubs.cn`.
- **Theme and language aware** — uses the DSH menu-surface design tokens
  (light/dark, radius, type scale), follows the DSH UI language
  (`zh-*` / English).
- **Peak-switch notifications** — optional browser notification when the window
  changes, only if notification permission was already granted for the DSH site.

## Requirements

- **DSH 0.2.1.x** with the web profile. Tested with `0.2.1-rc.3`; the package
  declares `engines.dsh = ">=0.2.1-0 <0.2.2-0"` and DSH refuses to mount it on
  other lines.
- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (the DSH requirement).
- A DeepSeek API key configured in DSH's credentials as `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`.

## Install

Install this repository directly from GitHub:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:zz0-0/dsh-balance
systemctl --user restart dsh-web
```

Or with an explicit git URL:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add git+https://github.com/zz0-0/dsh-balance.git
systemctl --user restart dsh-web
```

Then **hard-refresh** the DSH web page (`Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + R`). The plugin
injects its browser script into the DSH index page, so the refresh is needed the
first time. The `systemctl` line assumes the Linux user service; if you run
`dsh web` manually, restart that process instead.

> **Not the npm package.** The npm package named `dsh-balance` is an unrelated
> project by another author. Install this plugin with the GitHub coordinate
> above, not with `dsh plugin add dsh-balance`.

### Update

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:zz0-0/dsh-balance
systemctl --user restart dsh-web
```

### Remove

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-balance
systemctl --user restart dsh-web
```

## Usage

Click the balance card in the bottom-right corner to open the detail panel.
The card itself shows the total balance, the current pricing window, the
countdown to the next switch, and that switch time in your local zone.

The sidebar shows an `≈¥…` estimate on each conversation row and the sum of its
conversations on each workspace row. Hovering a badge shows its tokens and the
recorded estimate.

There is deliberately **no cost pill in the composer status row**: that row is
per-conversation and gets crowded quickly, and the conversation row already
carries the estimate.

If notification permission was granted for the DSH site, the browser notifies
when the peak/off-peak window changes while the DSH tab is open. A fully closed
browser cannot receive notifications.

## Pricing and the ledger

### Pricing is fetched, not hardcoded

At startup and whenever the cached table is older than six hours, the host
fetches both official pricing pages:

| Currency | Page |
|---|---|
| CNY | `https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/pricing` |
| USD | `https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing` |

The parser reads the model pricing table dynamically, including the model
columns, cache-hit/cache-miss/output prices, and the peak-hour windows from the
Chinese page footnote. If a page changes shape and parsing fails, the previous
cache is kept and the detail panel marks the source as `缓存/默认`
(`cache/default`).

### Peak windows

Peak is Beijing weekday **09:00–12:00** and **14:00–18:00**. Weekends are
always off-peak (from 2026-08-23), and a weekday marked as a public holiday is
off-peak. A make-up weekend is still a weekend, so it is off-peak.

The holiday calendar is fetched from:

```
https://api.apihubs.cn/holiday/get?year=YYYY&size=500
```

for the current and next year, and cached for 30 days.

### The ledger never reprices old spend

The cost ledger is `~/.dsh/.dsh-balance-costs.json`. Each session entry stores:

- `costs.CNY` and `costs.USD`
- `tokens`
- `lastSeq` — the last event already recorded
- `pricingVersions` — price snapshots used for its recorded events
- `calendarVersions` — holiday calendars used for its recorded events

When a session is scanned again, only events with `seq > lastSeq` are priced.
Already-recorded events are never recalculated, so a price change affects only
**new** events and a restart cannot rewrite what was already spent.

### Currency

`/user/balance` can return multiple `balance_infos`. The plugin stores costs in
both CNY and USD, then displays the bucket for the primary account currency: the
**largest non-zero balance** returned by the API (CNY wins a tie). If both
currencies have a positive balance, the card shows both stacked while estimates
use the larger one. A USD-only account uses the USD pricing table and `$`
badges.

**Granted credit expiry.** The official balance API reports only the unexpired
granted total, not per-grant expiry dates. The panel therefore keeps the granted
row visible at zero and links it to the DeepSeek Billing page
(`https://platform.deepseek.com/transactions`) while a granted balance exists.

## How it works

The plugin is a DSH bundle: `package.json` declares
`dsh.bundle.patch = ./cordis.patch.yml`, and that patch inserts the
`dsh-balance` entry into the web profile. It has two halves:

| Half | File | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Host | `lib/index.js` | Resolves `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` through DSH credentials, queries `/user/balance`, reads session events, keeps the ledger, fetches prices/holidays, serves `GET /dsh-balance/data` and `GET /dsh-balance/client.js`. |
| Browser | `client.js` | Injected into the DSH index page. Draws the balance card and detail panel, and adds cost badges to conversation/workspace rows. |

The browser only talks to the local DSH server. The API key never reaches the
browser.

Cache files, all under `~/.dsh/` (or `$DSH_HOME`):

- `.dsh-balance-costs.json` — the cost ledger
- `.dsh-balance-pricing.json` — current price table and peak hours
- `.dsh-balance-pricing-history.json` — one entry per changed price snapshot
- `.dsh-balance-holidays.json` — current holiday calendar

## Privacy

- **Outbound requests**: `api.deepseek.com/user/balance` (with your API key),
  the two DeepSeek pricing pages, and `api.apihubs.cn/holiday/get`. Nothing
  else, and no telemetry.
- **Local-only**: the ledger and caches stay in `~/.dsh/`. The browser only
  requests `/dsh-balance/data` from your local DSH server.
- **Credential handling**: the key is resolved host-side through DSH's
  credentials service and is never serialized into the browser payload.

## Troubleshooting

- **Card shows `余额?` / `Balance?`** — `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is missing or invalid;
  check DSH's credentials configuration and the host log.
- **Price source says `缓存/默认`** — the pricing page could not be fetched or
  parsed; the last cached table is still used.
- **No notifications** — permission was not granted for the DSH site, or the tab
  is closed.
- **Plugin not visible after install** — restart the `dsh web` process and
  hard-refresh the browser. Verify the profile lists the plugin.
- **Install refused with an incompatible-version error** — the package declares
  `engines.dsh` for the DSH 0.2.1 line only.

## Development

The plugin has no build step: plain ESM on the host and a classic browser script.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zz0-0/dsh-balance.git
cd dsh-balance
dsh plugin --profile web add link:$(pwd)
systemctl --user restart dsh-web
```

- `client.js` is served with `Cache-Control: no-store`. With a `link:` install,
  edit and hard-refresh the browser.
- `lib/index.js` is host-side: edit and restart `dsh-web`.
- A git install keeps its own copy under the profile's `node_modules`; after
  editing the checkout, reinstall the plugin (or sync `client.js` into the
  installed package) and refresh.

### Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | DSH bundle metadata and compatibility |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Inserts the plugin into the web profile |
| `lib/index.js` | Host: balance, pricing, holidays, ledger, HTTP routes, client injection |
| `client.js` | Browser: balance card + detail panel, row badges, notifications |
| `screenshot.png` | README screenshot |

### UI integration

The browser side does not patch React. It uses stable attributes exposed by the
workspace sidebar and composer:

- `[data-row-key="session:<sessionId>"]` and `[data-row-key="workspace:<workspaceId>"]`
  for cost badges (re-added by a `MutationObserver` after React re-renders)
- `[data-composer-card]` and `[data-slot="conversation.composer.dock"]` to keep
  the window-anchored card clear of the composer and the status row

MIT, documented nested Git path installation and a named DSH 0.2.1-rc.3 baseline bind host/client. rejected() allows requests when connection authentication is absent or throws. Routes can read/edit chosen paths and invoke Windows PowerShell/native actions, leaving a material caller-authorization boundary unresolved. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

Literal relative closure is not complete transitive dependency or runtime proof. No candidate archives executed.
